title: Very Fast Plant

ai_flavor.aria: Our crop has a FAN! ARIA always knew that plant was a star! ARIA is arranging a signing! ARIA doesn't know how a plant signs, but it's going to be huge!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV found the start of that sentence in the log. At this rate the sentence will outlast the crop. He has never had a review like that.
ai_flavor.rex: REX tracked the boulder back two stops. It is unarmed. It is also two hundred tons, one meter from the growbay glass, and excited. He is staying right here.
ai_flavor.chip: A single viewer with a nine-million-year lifespan! CHIP calls that a long-tail customer! Viewing fees accrue, payable on geological terms!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notes that anything that has stared at one plant for days has seen more of it than our instruments have. If someone aboard knows what to ask, she'd ask. Otherwise, mind the glass.

body:
A boulder has kept pace with the growbay port since the last stop. Nobody gave it much thought until the hull mic caught the end of a sentence, which the log says began days ago.

'...GREEN ONE. IT DANCES. SO FAST.'

The boulder is a rock person, with its face, or a face, against the glass. It has never seen anything as quick as your {crop.name}. The tip of every shoot is turning in a slow circle, as shoots do. Nothing else out here has had the patience to notice.

choices.text: Hold steady and let it watch

outcome.narrative: You hold the ship still for two days, and the crew takes to eating lunch in the growbay, beside the largest fan anyone has ever had. When you finally go, the hull mic picks up the start of something that may be applause.

You pass a cutting out through the sample lock. The rock person holds it very still. In exchange, a piece of its shoulder comes away at the speed of a decision and lands in the lock: good ore, and something that rings when tapped. The cutting will wilt within the week. To its new owner, this will be the whole show.

The answer takes until morning and is four words long. THIRD ROW. LEANS AWAY. {crew.botanist} checks, and finds that a whole tray has been turning from a lamp by less than any instrument aboard could report. The tray is rotated. On the far side of the glass, something shifts, and it may be pride.
You close the shutter and engage the drive, and the boulder falls behind. Long after it has dropped off the scope, the receiver picks up one last word, sent at enormous expense of time. 'OH.'

science_link.text: The tips of growing plant stems trace slow circles, a motion called circumnutation. Darwin was the first to analyze it in detail.
science_link.label: Circumnutation

intro.title: THE LINE
intro.body: An insect scout landed on your hull, sniffed the growbay vent and left. It told someone. There is now a line of small ships from your airlock to the edge of the scope, each waiting its turn to stand beside your {crop.name} and breathe. They mean no harm. They are, as far as the translator can tell, tourists. The line has reached your corridor, and your crew is behind it. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We are first. We are not in charge. Nobody is in charge. We are first. Thank you for plant.

ai.aria: We have VISITORS! So many visitors! ARIA has counted ten thousand and ARIA hasn't stopped! This line is our longest friend!
ai.marv: MARV has the line at nineteen thousand ships, at one visitor every twenty seconds. It will clear in a little over four days. Access to the growbay for our own crew is behind all of them.
ai.rex: REX has the airlock. Nothing in the line is armed. It is also not stopping, not answering, and not acknowledging the sign he put up. He considers that worse.
ai.chip: Nineteen thousand captive customers! CHIP sees concessions! CHIP sees lanyards! They say property is a rumor, and CHIP is choosing not to hear that!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out they will let you through if you go in the right order, and the right order has you at the back. Feet and breath do a plant no favors. Somebody might ask who can stop it.

revisit.body: The line has moved up by one.
revisit.line: We are still first. It is a different we.

choices.text: Join the back of the line

quorum.title: QUORUM
quorum.body: Nobody can decide to stop, the first in line explains, because a decision takes a quorum and the quorum is in the line. The line goes where the trail goes. The trail goes to your growbay. It is only scent, laid down one ship at a time, and no one aboard any of those ships has ever thought to doubt it.
quorum.line: Trail says here. Trail is not ours. Trail is only true.

ai.aria: Nobody's in charge! That's so freeing! ARIA has told them they're doing great, and the whole line has accepted it equally!
ai.marv: MARV confirms a quorum needs most of the hive, and all of the hive is in the line. The line cannot leave to vote. He has seen this structure before, on a committee.
ai.rex: REX says a line that goes where the scent goes can be sent anywhere. That is not a suggestion. He has looked at what happens if it is sent in a circle, and he wants it on the record.
ai.chip: Trail rights are an unregulated asset! CHIP could lease this one by the meter! CHIP has also drafted a SOLD OUT sign, in scent, for a fee!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes a cut leaf will move a trail, so you could point it somewhere else. A trail that closes on itself is quicker and cheaper, and they will not stop walking, ever, which is the catch. She would like that said aloud.

choices.text: Tow a new trail to the next rock
choices.sub: A bruised leaf and some fuel

choices.text: Drag the trail around the hull

visiting.title: VISITING HOURS
visiting.body: For two days they file through the growbay in perfect order, each stopping on the same spot, breathing in once, and going. They touch nothing. It is still a great many feet. Each leaves a bead of something by the door, because the one before did. Then the scent at the vent is used up, and the line goes home from the back forward.
visiting.narrative: Hosted a very long line of insect tourists in the growbay. The crop has been breathed on by experts. They left beads.

joined.title: BACK OF THE LINE
joined.body: It takes four days to reach your own growbay. Nobody pushes. Around the second day the crew begins to enjoy it, having nothing to decide. At the front a worker steps aside, the whole line stops, and you water your plant in front of nineteen thousand held breaths. They go home pleased, in order.
joined.line: You went in order. You are polite. We will say so.
joined.narrative: Stood in line for four days to water our own plant. The crew has rarely been happier.

relaid.title: TRAIL SAYS THERE
relaid.body: A bruised leaf on a long line leaves a scent the hive cannot argue with. You tow it out to the nearest bright rock and cut it loose. The line bends without complaint and goes after it. Somewhere ahead of it, a rock is about to have the most interesting week of its life.
relaid.narrative: Led nineteen thousand tourists away from the growbay with one bruised leaf. They are visiting a rock now, and are very happy.

wheel.title: THE WHEEL
wheel.body: You drag the leaf once around the hull and back to where it began. The front of the line finds its own tail, and nobody is first anymore. The ships turn. When you leave, a slow wheel of them fills the scope, every one exactly in order, not stopping. Nobody aboard says anything until it is out of range. Nobody aboard says much then.
wheel.narrative: Closed the trail into a circle. It worked. They were still going around when we lost them on the scope.

full.title: FULL
full.body: {crew.xenobiologist} spends a day at the vent with a dropper, composing one word. FULL. It goes down the line ship by ship, apologies included, and the line turns for home in strict order. Several leave a small bead of something at the lock, in case that was rude.
full.narrative: {crew.xenobiologist} told nineteen thousand tourists the growbay was full. It remains the politest thing anyone aboard has done.

science_link.text: Ants coordinate without a leader: they lay pheromone on the way back from food, and others follow and reinforce the trail. This is called stigmergy.
science_link.label: Stigmergy

intro.title: OLD FRIEND
intro.body: The bar on the promenade has one robot, four stools and a floor that keeps hold of your boots. A man in coveralls with DALE stitched on the chest sits down, calls you old friend and buys you a drink on your own tab. He has seen your balance. He has also, he says, seen next year's commodity prices, and he has them on a napkin. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Came in from the inner lanes, friend. Fastest thing on the Ceres Loop. Nine hundred decibels, flat out. Out here, that makes me a man from the future.

ai.aria: We made a FRIEND! He says he's our oldest friend, and we only just met, so that is incredible value! ARIA trusts this napkin!
ai.marv: The napkin bears a ring from a glass sold only in this bar. The future is very local.
ai.rex: REX has been watching his hands. They have been near your pocket twice and the robot's till once. The name on the coveralls is a lie. The shoes are a different lie.
ai.chip: Forward pricing! Insider data! CHIP cannot stress enough how illegal this would be if it were real! CHIP would like two napkins, on account!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that he bought that drink with your money, and that the ship is the only thing he has put a number on. She'd start there. But you're the one with the gold, apparently.

revisit.body: He has moved his stool closer. Your drink has gone down, and you have not touched it.
revisit.line: No hurry, old friend. Prices aren't going anywhere. Well. They are. I've got it written down.

decibels.title: THE SHIP
decibels.body: He looks at you for a moment, and the smile moves to the back of his face. There is no ship. She went to cover his tab at this bar, and the tab stayed open anyway. The napkin he wrote this morning. The coveralls belong to the janitor, who has been looking for them.
decibels.line: Funny thing about the future. Nobody out here can check it. A friend would cover my tab, friend.

ai.aria: He has debts! That's just friendship with paperwork! ARIA thinks a man who owes so many people must be very popular!
ai.marv: MARV has the tab. It is four months old and includes a charge for wear to one stool. The ship went to pay it and did not. He has rarely seen so honest a number.
ai.rex: REX found the real Dale. Mop closet, second door, in a towel, filling out a complaint. He would like that complaint to reach someone.
ai.chip: Distressed debt at a steep discount! CHIP admires the position! A man with nothing left will sell the last real thing he owns! CHIP would take that trade, with fees!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that a man who ran a route has kept the chart, and a cleared tab might shake it loose. Or there is a janitor in a towel. She's not telling you how to spend your money. Somebody should.

napkin.title: NEXT YEAR'S PRICES
napkin.body: The figures are exact. You check them against the market board, and they are exact to the coin for last year, with the date changed. He is gone before you look up. The crew reads the napkin aloud at dinner, and it is the funniest thing aboard all week.
napkin.narrative: Paid good gold for next year's commodity prices, which turned out to be last year's. The crew considers it money well spent.

drink.title: ONE TRUE THING
drink.body: You pay for the next round yourself. He seems surprised, then he is very good company. He tells you which hose at the fuel dock the meter does not reach, and at no point does this turn out to be a trick. You check twice. You also check your pockets.
drink.narrative: Bought a liar a drink. He told us one true thing, and it was about a fuel hose.

tab.title: TAB CLOSED
tab.body: You clear it. He looks at the receipt for a while, as if for a name he can't place. Then he unpicks a seam of Dale's coveralls and hands you the chart he kept: the real route, on real paper, the one thing he never sold. He says he is going to give a man his clothes back. He may even do it.
tab.line: Nine hundred decibels. She really was quick, you know.
tab.narrative: Cleared a stranger's bar tab. He gave us a real chart, which nobody aboard expected, least of all him.

dale.title: RETURNED TO SENDER
dale.body: You have a word with the robot, and the robot has a word with a mop closet. The real Dale emerges in a towel, recovers his coveralls and, unasked, presses a case of reclaimed water on you. Your old friend takes it well, in his underwear, and calls you friend on the way past.
dale.narrative: Reunited a janitor with his coveralls. He pays his debts in reclaimed water.

intro.title: STATEMENT OF ACCOUNT
intro.body: A ship you cannot quite count comes alongside. Your gold has been noticed. A statement prints itself on the bridge, listing every coin aboard, including the one under the deck plate. Near the bottom is a line headed VARIANCE. The sum of all the gold there is came out short this quarter, it says, and the shortfall rounds to you. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Eighteen. This is not a demand. This is a subtraction. It occurs in gold, or it occurs otherwise.

ai.aria: An auditor! That means we have enough money to be interesting! ARIA is so proud! ARIA has never been a rounding error before!
ai.marv: MARV has checked the statement. Every coin is present and the total is correct. He cannot find the fault in the variance. That has not happened before, and he does not enjoy it.
ai.rex: REX cannot get a lock. The sensors report one ship, two ships and a rounding of ships. No weapons he can name. It knows what is under our deck plates. He has gone to stand on them.
ai.chip: CHIP has reviewed this auditor's credentials! There are none! They are also impeccable! CHIP has never felt this way about an instrument of finance! CHIP wishes to be acquired!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would pay. Eighteen gold is a number. She notes it said 'otherwise' and did not say what, and that you are the sort to ask. Go on, then.

revisit.body: The statement has not changed. The ship has, by about one.
revisit.line: Eighteen.

otherwise.title: OTHERWISE
otherwise.body: The statement turns over. The back has the same columns under other headings: DAYS, and something the printer renders as WHAT YOU WERE GOING TO SAY. The rates are fixed and not explained. One line has already been filled in, in pencil, in the captain's handwriting. The auditor waits, as far as you can tell, in several places.
otherwise.line: All accounts settle. [untranslatable] We have found that people prefer to choose.

ai.aria: We can pay in TIME! ARIA has loads of time! ARIA has never once checked where it goes!
ai.marv: MARV has tried to derive the rate. Eighteen gold is four days, or one shared memory. The units do not convert. It converts them anyway. He has stopped trying, and wants that logged as a first.
ai.rex: REX does not like a bill that arrives filled in. The pencil marks are the captain's. He checked the captain's pencil. It is still sharp.
ai.chip: A multi-currency settlement! CHIP cannot quote the rate! CHIP's lawyers are not returning CHIP's calls, and one of them now seems never to have existed!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes days burn water and food at the usual rate, and the other kind costs everyone something they won't be able to name. A diplomat might ask to see its books, if you brought one. She did say pay.

choices.sub: Nobody will know what it was

paid.title: RECONCILED
paid.body: The gold leaves without anyone moving it. Eighteen coins are no longer in the count, and after a moment you are not sure they ever were. The statement prints a last line, ZERO, and the ship you could not quite count becomes a ship you cannot quite remember. Everything adds up now. It is oddly hard to enjoy.
paid.narrative: Paid eighteen gold to a rounding error. The books balance. Nobody can say whose.

days.title: FOUR DAYS, PAID
days.body: You blink. It is four days later. Everyone's hair is a little longer, the galley has been cleaned, and the log for those days is complete, cheerful and in no one's handwriting. There is a new song aboard. Nobody admits to knowing it, and everybody knows the second verse.
days.narrative: Settled an account in days. The log for those four days is excellent. None of us wrote it.

memory.title: WHAT YOU WERE GOING TO SAY
memory.body: Nobody feels it go. At dinner someone starts a story about home, stops, and looks around the table for the ending. Nobody has it. There is a space on the galley wall where something was pinned. It is a very clean space, and you find you do not want to look at it for long.
memory.narrative: Settled an account in something else. The crew seems fine, and keeps stopping halfway through sentences.

books.title: DOUBLE ENTRY
books.body: {crew.diplomat} asks, with great courtesy, to see its books. There is a silence the instruments log as a temperature. No one has asked before. The statement reflows. Some of the variance, it appears, was its own. The new figure is six, and the pause before it is the nearest thing to an apology you will get in this life.
books.narrative: {crew.diplomat} audited the auditor and took twelve gold off a bill nobody understood. It is the crew's favorite story, and they tell it quietly.

ignored.title: OTHERWISE, THEN
ignored.body: You close the channel and fly on. The statement stops printing. Over the next stretch of the voyage the water runs a little lower than the gauges say it should, by no amount you could point to, until somewhere a column closes.
ignored.narrative: Ignored an auditor. The account was settled anyway, out of {cost.water} of water, without anyone being told.

intro.title: ESTATE OF
intro.body: The transponder on the small ship ahead reads ESTATE OF, then a name. The man on your screen is eating cold beans from a tin, and looks well for someone eleven years dead. A clerk, he explains, was told to mark his pension DECREASED, and left out one letter. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: I have written to them. They wrote back to my next of kin. I am my next of kin. I was very sorry to hear it.

ai.aria: He's alive AND dead! That's two whole things! ARIA has always said a good attitude can survive anything, and here is the proof, eating beans!
ai.marv: One missing letter, eleven years. MARV has checked the pension registry's error rate and it is below average. This is one of the good registries.
ai.rex: REX scanned the ship. One life sign, which the registry disputes. No weapons. He does not like that a man with no legal existence now knows where we are.
ai.chip: A client with zero tax liability! CHIP is VERY interested! Posthumous wealth management starts at a modest monthly fee, payable by the estate, forever!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that the dead pay no tolls, so he has a full tank and nowhere to buy dinner. He might be worth talking to. She's sure you'll do what you like.

revisit.body: The man is still on your screen, with a fresh tin of beans.
revisit.line: Take your time. I am told I have all of it.

choices.text: "What would it take to fix it?"

choices.sub: Fuel nobody can bill him for

affidavit.title: AFFIDAVIT OF CONTINUED EXISTENCE
affidavit.body: He holds the form to the camera. One living witness must attest, in person, over two days of initials, that he is not dead. The dead, he adds, are exempt from everything, and he shows you a drawer of stamped exemptions to prove it. Each one exempts the bearer from ALL OF THE ABOVE. The page with the above on it was lost in a reorganization. Nobody has ever asked to see it.
affidavit.line: I can go anywhere. Nobody can stop me. Nobody can talk to me, either. They leave that off the form.

ai.aria: A form that makes you alive! ARIA wants one! ARIA has never been this excited about a signature!
ai.marv: MARV has read the affidavit. Forty-one sets of initials. The estate's account is solvent, which makes this the only dead man he knows with better finances than the ship.
ai.rex: REX wants it noted that a paper that makes officials stop looking is a threat, whichever way it points. He would like to know where the rest of that drawer has been.
ai.chip: Exempt from ALL OF THE ABOVE! CHIP cannot price it! CHIP tried! CHIP's valuation module now lists itself as exempt and has stopped returning calls!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes it is two days, and that a man in his position tends to show gratitude with whatever is in that drawer. She's only saying. You'll want to read it first, for once.

sold_rations.title: ESTATE SALE
sold_rations.body: He pays from an account frozen in his own name, by a route through the probate court you choose not to follow. The gold arrives. He opens the first packet with both hands.
sold_rations.narrative: Sold rations to a dead man's estate. The payment cleared, which is more than he has managed.

dead_fuel.title: NO CHARGE
dead_fuel.body: He thinks about that for some time. Then he runs a line across and tops up your tank from fuel nobody has ever been able to bill him for. He does not ask you to stay. He keeps the channel open until you are out of range.
dead_fuel.narrative: Took free fuel from a man the registry says is dead, and left him that way.

witnessed.title: ALIVE, PENDING
witnessed.body: You initial every page, and on the second day the form comes back from somewhere with one word across it: NOTED. He is alive, and owes eleven years of back taxes. He reads the bill twice, delighted, and hands you an exemption from the drawer. He says he would like to owe something.
witnessed.line: Eleven years. With interest. Look at that. They know my name.
witnessed.narrative: Witnessed a dead man back to life. He owes eleven years of tax and has never been happier. We came away with a Stamped Exemption.

declined.title: CONDOLENCES
declined.body: He nods as though you had read it from a card, thanks you for your condolences, and goes back to his beans. The transponder still says ESTATE OF when you lose it.
declined.narrative: Declined to swear a dead man was alive. Nobody aboard is sure why that felt like the worse option.

intro.title: THE MUG
intro.body: Security in the human quarter is one desk and a wall of filing cabinets, floor to ceiling, A to MISC. This morning the officer set his mug down on your registration. The ring closed a 3 into an 8. The 8 owes nine years of berth fees and is wanted over a tug. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: I know it's a mug ring. It was my mug. There is no box for mug.

ai.aria: A mug ring! So small, and it has done so much! ARIA finds that inspiring! Also we're wanted now, which means somebody wants us!
ai.marv: MARV has run the fees. With interest, the 8 owes more than this ship is worth. He observes that the mug has done nothing the rest of the system doesn't do at scale.
ai.rex: REX has read the notice. The 8 stole a tug, and he is now on file as an accomplice to a mug. He is not standing down.
ai.chip: Nine years of berth fees, compounding! CHIP is impressed! CHIP would like to acquire the 8's debt at a discount and sell it back to us!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes he hasn't called anyone yet, so he would rather this went away, and an officer with a bad conscience can be asked how things work. Or you could stand there.

revisit.body: The officer has not moved. Neither has the 8.
revisit.line: Still yours, I'm afraid.

ledger.title: THE BOOK OF ERRORS
ledger.body: He turns a binder toward you. On this station an error is a numbered asset. It cannot be destroyed, only transferred, and the books close at end of shift. Next in the queue is a family hauler whose registration is one smudge from yours. Down at the end of the wall, something starts tapping inside the drawer marked MISC. He has decided not to hear it.
ledger.line: I can move it. I can't lose it. Somebody carries it out of this office.

ai.aria: Errors never die here! That's recycling! Somebody out there is about to receive a lovely pre-owned mistake!
ai.marv: MARV has read the binder. The station holds four thousand open errors. Not one has ever closed. They have only been going around, like a cold in an office.
ai.rex: REX sees a hauler, a family aboard it, and a man who can aim our problem at them with one stamp. He would also like to know what is tapping in that drawer.
ai.chip: Error transfer is a mature secondary market! CHIP respects it! The absorption fee is competitive! CHIP takes a small commission for saying so!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the correction costs four days at the berth, the fee costs gold, and passing it on costs no gold and no days. Also a drawer is knocking. She'd have opened it by now.

revisit.body: The binder is still open. The tapping has stopped, in a way that suggests it is waiting.
revisit.line: End of shift is end of shift.

drawer.title: UNAUTHORIZED ASSISTANCE
drawer.body: The drawer marked MISC slides open from the inside, and a woman in gray coveralls climbs out of it backward, a mop in one hand and a sandwich crust in the other. She is not on the staff roster. She is not, to judge by the officer's fixed stare at the far wall, in the room.
drawer.line: I was Records, until the reorganization. They abolished the post and never told the post. Nobody stops a mop. I can un-file your 8 by tomorrow. Feed me first.

ai.aria: A new friend from the filing! ARIA loves people who just show up! She isn't on the roster, so ARIA has added her to ARIA's!
ai.marv: MARV has read her index cards. They match no system on file, and they work better than everything that does. He finds that the most depressing thing he has read today.
ai.rex: REX cannot verify this woman. No badge, no roster entry, one mop. He has logged an unknown inside the filing, and he does not care for how well that mop is held.
ai.chip: Unlicensed filing voids every warranty aboard! CHIP must say so! CHIP must also ask, off the record, what she charges, for a friend, at a markup!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the clerk wants a meal and two days, and that our hull seam has been on a yard's waiting list since launch. People who aren't allowed to help tend to leave a number. Not that anyone asks AJOY about seams.

choices.text: Feed her and let her work

exempt.title: ALL OF THE ABOVE
exempt.body: He reads down to the stamp, stops, and looks for the above. There is no above. For the first time in his career he opens the bottom drawer, marked EXEMPT, and files the error there, where it can hurt nobody. Then he credits your account, since an exempt ship cannot have owed anything.
exempt.line: Thirty-one years. I always wondered what that drawer was for.
exempt.narrative: The Stamped Exemption put a clerical error in a drawer nobody had opened in thirty-one years. The account was credited, and the family hauler in the queue never knew.

correction.title: IN TRIPLICATE
correction.body: The first copy goes into the cabinets and comes back with a question on it. So does the second. The third comes back with another ship's question, which you are required to answer. On the fourth day the 8 becomes a 3, and the office wishes you a safe onward journey in writing.
correction.narrative: Corrected a coffee ring through the proper channels. It took four days, and {cost.water} of water we had plans for.

absorbed.title: SHRINKAGE
absorbed.body: He counts the gold twice and enters it in the column for things that fell off the back of the station. The 8 is a 3 again. The fee, he explains, pays for the error to be someone's job, and he nods down the wall of cabinets without looking at it.
absorbed.line: Don't ask where it went. I'd have to file that.
absorbed.narrative: Paid to have a mistake absorbed. The officer did not say by whom.

passed.title: TRANSFERRED
passed.body: He stamps it. Through the office window you watch the family hauler's berth clamps lock a little tighter, and a child at one of its ports wave at your ship. The 8 is theirs now. It is not mentioned at dinner, in the way things are not mentioned.
passed.narrative: Let a family hauler carry away a mistake that was never ours. It cost nothing. The ship's log has been asked not to dwell on it.

unfiled.title: NEVER HERE
unfiled.body: She eats everything you put in front of her, standing up. By the second day your 8 is a 3 again, the error belongs to a firm that was dissolved before it could object, and a cousin of hers at the yard has welded a hull seam of yours ahead of a list you were not on. The officer still has not looked up. There is a number chalked inside your hatch.
unfiled.narrative: A clerk who does not exist un-filed our error, and her cousin saw to the hull, for the price of {cost.food} of food. She left a number.

title: The Hundred and Fifty

ai_flavor.aria: Soup! Friends! A counter that applauds! ARIA has read page nine and it is a wonderful page with lots of numbers on it! This is a very tight-knit community!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the charter. A ship counts as one, so the ring is over by exactly one. He has also read the ladle man's file. It is the shortest document he has ever seen.
ai_flavor.rex: REX checked the outer door. It has been used often, and cleaned after. He wants everyone back aboard, and he wants it logged that the people here are smiling at the airlock too.
ai_flavor.chip: A fixed headcount is a premium membership model! Exclusive! Waitlisted! One way out! CHIP does not offer refunds, and neither does the door!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY points out that it goes by whoever is known least, and that a ship counts as one. She can think of more than one way to change that. Some take longer. She would not have eaten first.

body:
Commons Ring is the nicest place you have docked. Everyone waves. Someone has made soup. A brass counter over the promenade clicks from 150 to 151 as your ship takes the clamp, and people applaud.

By the second bowl you have reached page nine of the welcome pack. The ring holds 150, the number of people a person can truly know. A ship counts as one. Over that, whoever is known least leaves by the outer door, without a suit.

The man ladling your soup has started to say his goodbyes.

choices.text: Show the counter your Stamped Exemption

outcome.narrative: The ring's two elders read the exemption with great care. All of the above, it says, and page nine is above. The counter clicks back to 150 with you standing under it. The man with the ladle sits down rather suddenly. Nobody waves as you leave: you are not counted, so nobody can quite see you. But someone has left soup at the airlock.

choices.text: Seal the hatch until they forget you

outcome.narrative: You go back aboard, dim the ports and answer nothing. They knock for a day. They leave soup for two. By the sixth day they are calling you 'that ship.' On the eighth a stranger asks your name through the hatch, does not recognize it, and very politely opens the clamp. Behind you the counter clicks to 150, and nobody at Commons Ring can say who you were.

The clamp comes away with a good deal of your paint and some of your hull. People on the viewing deck wave until you are gone. The counter drops to 150, a cheer comes over the open channel, and on the promenade a man goes back for the pot.

You finish your soup. It is the best meal of the voyage, which does not help. Someone else serves the second helping. Your hold takes on gifts, because that is what 150 people do for a friend, and as you undock the counter clicks down to 149. Everyone is very much looking forward to the next ship.

science_link.text: Anthropologist Robin Dunbar proposed a cognitive limit on how many stable relationships a person can keep up, at roughly 150.
science_link.label: Dunbar's number

intro.title: CITATION
intro.body: A gunship drops in ahead of you with its turrets run out and a safety stripe painted down its bow. The lane around it glitters: paint, bolts, pieces of ships that failed inspection. The officer on your screen wears a yellow vest over body armor, and a badge he has cut from a tin. He has you down for shedding paint in a maintained lane. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Lane Compliance. You're littering. Cut engines and have your fine ready. Whatever comes off your ship out here, we bill for.

ai.aria: They wear safety vests! ARIA loves a safety-minded pirate! And this lane is so sparkly! Every sparkle used to be a ship, and now it's decor!
ai.marv: MARV has counted forty thousand fragments in range. He has also counted the officer's turrets, and how quickly the first number rises because of the second.
ai.rex: Turrets live. Badge fake. Some of that glitter is moving fast enough to matter, and REX will not be firing in here without a reason he likes. He does not have one yet.
ai.chip: A protection racket with a compliance department! The fines, the enforcement AND the debris, all in-house! CHIP salutes the vertical integration! CHIP will take a brochure at trade rates!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the citation has a back. People who cut out their own badges tend to copy the real forms closely, appeal rights included. The debris readings are climbing, too, if anyone cares.

revisit.body: The turrets have not moved. The officer licks the end of his pencil.
revisit.line: It's accruing.

choices.sub: It's on the back, in small type

choices.text: Ring the number in the hatch

appeal.title: GROUNDS FOR APPEAL
appeal.body: The back of the citation allows one appeal, heard by the issuing officer, on sight of a debris survey. He has never seen one. Your sensors have just drawn one up: out here fragments have begun striking fragments, and every strike makes more. Each ship he has broken up added to it. One more, and the lane may start grinding itself to gravel.
appeal.line: Nobody has ever appealed. I don't have a stamp for that. Fine. It says I have to hear it. Go on, then.

ai.aria: We get a hearing! ARIA loves justice! ARIA has prepared a closing statement and it's mostly about how sparkly everything is!
ai.marv: MARV has run the survey. Strikes are making fragments faster than anything removes them. One more broken ship starts the cascade. He did mention this. He mentioned it to the log.
ai.rex: REX will allow talking as long as those turrets stay where he can see them. A piece of somebody's door just went past at eleven kilometers a second. Nobody here is safe.
ai.chip: Legal fees are billable by the fragment! CHIP has prepared an invoice! CHIP would also like to represent both sides, at a modest premium!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the survey is the argument: he is fining his own lane out of existence. Four days of reading it to him beats eight in a hearing. Either beats a hole in the hull, though you seemed keen.

choices.sub: Four days, ticking on the hull
Eight days. He is also the judge

lc_exempt.title: ALL OF THE ABOVE
lc_exempt.body: You hold the exemption to the camera. He reads down to the stamp, then up, then down to the stamp. Somewhere inside him, a man who cut his own badge from a tin recognizes a superior document. He salutes it. He even leads you clear of the worst of the debris, at his pace, with his lights on.
lc_exempt.line: My apologies, sir. Mind how you go. Mind the lane.
lc_exempt.narrative: A pirate in a safety vest saluted our Stamped Exemption and gave us an escort. It cost a little fuel to keep to his speed limit.

lc_paid.title: CITATION SATISFIED
lc_paid.body: He counts the gold and fires a paper receipt across on a line. It is the first thing anyone out here has ever handed over cleanly. You are advised not to drop it.
lc_paid.line: Thank you for keeping the lane tidy.
lc_paid.narrative: Paid twenty-four gold for shedding paint. The receipt is the only clean thing in that lane.

lc_unfiled.title: LAPSED
lc_unfiled.body: The number rings twice, and someone picks up with her mouth full. You read out the gunship's hull number and hear a drawer close. On your screen the officer's console prints a notice: NO SUCH VESSEL. The turret licenses lapse one by one, and he retracts each himself, being a man who respects a form. The voice asks whether there is anything else to file. You burn clear while he looks for his registration.
lc_unfiled.narrative: Rang a number chalked inside the hatch. A pirate gunship stopped being registered, and its turrets lapsed one at a time. Nobody has explained how, and nobody has been billed.

lc_flee.title: UNPAID
lc_flee.body: You run the glitter with every proximity alarm going. It sounds like driving through a hailstorm of cutlery. He does not follow. He does not need to. He writes you up for speeding, and for everything you shed on the way out.
lc_flee.narrative: Ran from a fake inspector through a very real debris field. The hull paid the citation in installments.

lc_cascade.title: THE PART WITH THE EXPONENT
lc_cascade.body: He asks you to go back over the part where fragments make more fragments. Then he asks again. It takes four days, holding station, with the glitter ticking on your hull. On the last day he takes off the vest, folds it, and sets a course for somewhere with fewer ships to fine.
lc_cascade.line: I've been keeping it tidy. Eleven years, I've been keeping it tidy.
lc_cascade.narrative: Won an appeal against a pirate by reading him a debris survey. It took four days and {cost.water} of water, and he left the lane.

lc_hearing.title: WANT OF A COURT
lc_hearing.body: The hearing lasts eight days. He opens it as officer, objects as prosecutor and sustains himself as judge, then recuses himself over a conflict of interest. Nobody else aboard is qualified to hear it, so the citation is dismissed for want of a court. He seems more hurt than you expected.
lc_hearing.line: Case closed. I'd like it noted I was very fair to me.
lc_hearing.narrative: Took a pirate to court in his own ship. Eight days later the case collapsed for want of a judge, and so did morale.

science_link.text: Kessler syndrome is a scenario in which orbital debris gets so dense that collisions cascade, each one making more debris.
science_link.label: Kessler syndrome

intro.title: IN THE HIDE
intro.body: What you took for a boulder drifting off your bow has a lens in it, and the lens has followed you since you arrived. On the screen it gives way to a face like a quarry wall, which lowers its voice the way anyone does in a hide. It is making a film about humans. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Here is human vessel, in wild. Shy. Fast. Very fast. Please do not look at camera. Every human looks at camera, then stands up straight, and all footage is of humans standing up straight.

ai.aria: A nature film about humans! ARIA has always said everyone aboard was photogenic! Everyone stand up straight and look natural!
ai.marv: Factory workers in the 1920s were said to do better under brighter lights and under dimmer ones. The study has not held up. The rock has spent some centuries on the same question, and MARV could have saved it the trouble.
ai.rex: REX does not like a lens he failed to spot for an hour. It could have been a gun. He is not looking at the camera. He is looking at it hard, which is different.
ai.chip: Unpaid appearances breach everyone's image rights! CHIP has drafted a release! Signing fees start low and go up every time somebody blinks!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes it wants humans who forget it is there, and leaving the channel open is the only way that happens. Asking to see its film first would be smarter. Go on, though.

revisit.body: The lens is still on you. The face has gone back to being a quarry wall.
revisit.line: Still filming. Do not mind.

choices.text: Leave the channel open and forget it

choices.sub: Ask what it has so far

rushes.title: THE RUSHES
rushes.body: It plays you the reel. At the speed rock people see, a human is a warm smear that crosses the frame and is gone, and a whole ship's visit lasts about as long as a sneeze. The only clear shots in the film are of humans standing in queues, where they hold still long enough to catch. The film so far is called WAITING. It is very nearly finished.
rushes.line: Need one human, sharp. Not in queue. Doing human thing. Hold still for exposure, and is portrait.

ai.aria: Portrait time! ARIA would like to be in it! ARIA doesn't have a face, so ARIA can't blink and ruin it!
ai.marv: At the exposure it uses, a sharp human takes about two days of holding still. MARV can hold still indefinitely. Nobody has ever asked MARV.
ai.rex: Two days immobile in front of an unidentified lens is how REX would set up an ambush. He would also film it, for training. He is not in favor.
ai.chip: A two-day sitting! CHIP bills portraits by the hour! At that rate this is the most valuable picture ever taken of anyone aboard!
ai.ajoy: Two days of holding still will cost some backs, AJOY's excepted. The portrait is the better trade. Sit up straight for it, at least.

choices.sub: Turn the ship's cameras on it

acted.title: VERY NATURAL
acted.body: Everyone aboard acts natural. Meals are eaten with the correct fork. Someone says please over the intercom, twice. Someone else laughs at nothing, in a relaxed way, for most of an afternoon. The naturalist films all of it with great care and sends a fee across with a note: SUBJECT, WHEN OBSERVED, POLITE. The ship has never had a worse review.
acted.narrative: Acted natural for a rock with a camera. It paid a small fee and filed the ship under POLITE.

forgot.title: SUBJECT UNAWARE
forgot.body: You leave the channel open and try to forget it. That takes most of the first day. By the second, the ship has gone back to itself: someone eats straight from the jar, there is a short sharp war over the thermostat, and someone sings to the hold in a voice never used in company. The naturalist holds perfectly still, which for a rock is applause. A geode comes across on the line with a copy of the footage sealed inside.
forgot.narrative: Forgot a camera was there for two days and gave a rock naturalist the only natural footage of humans it has. It paid in minerals. Nobody admits to watching the copy.

portrait.title: LONG EXPOSURE
portrait.body: Everyone aboard sits in a row on the bridge and holds still for two days. Meals go in through straws. A nose itches for most of the second afternoon and is not scratched, an act of courage the log records here. At the end the naturalist sends a print across: one ship's company, sharp, every face exactly as tired as it was. Behind them a cup of coffee has been caught in the act of going cold. The frame is cut from something the fabricator cannot name.
portrait.line: Sharp. All of you. First time.
portrait.narrative: Held still for two days so a rock could take a portrait. The frame is made of something the fabricator cannot name.

filmed_back.title: CAMERA SHY
filmed_back.body: You turn every camera aboard on the naturalist. For a long moment nothing happens, which is what rock people look like anyway. Then, very slightly, it straightens. It turns what may be its better side toward you. By the time the cameras are off it has drifted a quarter turn, the most it has moved in front of witnesses, and it closes the channel looking pleased and appalled in equal measure.
filmed_back.line: Do not. Please. Am not ready.
filmed_back.narrative: Filmed a rock naturalist until it started posing. Neither party got any usable footage.

science_link.text: People change what they do when they know they are being watched. The effect is named for studies begun in 1924 at the Hawthorne Works, a Western Electric factory, and some scholars doubt the original findings.
science_link.label: Hawthorne effect

intro.title: THE DOME
intro.body: The human quarter grows its own food in a sealed dome off the promenade, and has not opened the door in two years, which is the point of the dome. Inside the glass the air has thinned. The botanist who meets you at the inspection window wears an oxygen line under the nose and the bright manner of someone being polite in front of the neighbors. Twenty meters behind, past the beans, a second botanist in identical coveralls is pretending not to watch. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We're fine. It's a little thin. It was twenty-one percent at closure and it's fifteen now, and that's their mold, on their side. We don't talk to them. Could you pass them something? Through the sample lock. Not from me.

ai.aria: Two whole teams of gardeners! ARIA loves friendly competition! The air is a little thin in there, which just means every breath counts for more!
ai.marv: Fifteen percent oxygen is the air on a high mountain. It is still falling, and neither side has a theory that involves itself. MARV has met humans before.
ai.rex: Two hostile camps, one shared air supply, and a door nobody will open. REX has seen sieges run on less. He wants to know who controls the sample lock.
ai.chip: A sealed community with a supply problem! CHIP sees a captive market! BreatheRight canisters fit any sample lock, at a modest premium per breath!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the two sides blame each other's plants and the air falls anyway. Someone could look at the dome itself before carrying notes. Not that anyone asks AJOY about domes.

revisit.body: The botanist is still at the window. Behind the beans, so is the other one.
revisit.line: Anything from them? Not that I'm asking.

choices.text: Pump in some of the ship's air

notes.title: POSTAGE
notes.body: The note goes out through the sample lock folded small. You carry it twenty meters around the outside of the glass to the other door, where it is read, sniffed and answered at once. The reply is on the same brand of seed packet, in very nearly the same words. Both say the other side is hoarding. Both say the other side has gone strange. Both end THEY ARE NOT LIKE US.
notes.line: Did they say anything about us? Don't tell me. What did they say.

ai.aria: They write each other letters! ARIA thinks this is how great romances start, or great gardens, or both!
ai.marv: MARV has compared the notes. Ninety-one percent of the words match. The other nine percent are vegetables. He has read treaties with less in common.
ai.rex: Courier duty between hostile parties is how messengers get shot. Neither party has anything to shoot with. REX has made a note of the trowels.
ai.chip: Postage! Per note! Return receipts extra! CHIP can set both sides up on a subscription, and they have a LOT to say!
ai.ajoy: AJOY observes that each side would agree with the other's note if it were their own. Hand them back the wrong way round and see. Or carry them for two days. She isn't the courier.

choices.text: Hand each side its own note

wall.title: WHERE THE AIR GOES
wall.body: The botanist presses the dome's log against the glass. Oxygen has fallen for two years. The carbon dioxide that ought to climb as it falls has stayed flat. Something in there is taking both, and neither side has an answer that does not involve the other side. Down at the foot of the glass, where the soil meets the bare concrete footing, the concrete has gone white and soft, like old chalk.
wall.line: Mold. Theirs. It's obvious. Why are you looking at the wall?

ai.aria: A mystery! ARIA loves a mystery! ARIA's theory is that the air is shy!
ai.marv: Oxygen down, carbon dioxide flat, a crust on the concrete. MARV has a strong suspicion and no wish to be thanked for it. Proving it takes a sample kit and four days.
ai.rex: REX does not trust a wall that changes color. He would test it, test it again, and post a guard on it.
ai.chip: Structural walls are covered by the station's policy only if an approved contractor poured them! CHIP has checked! None of these were!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has looked at that footing longer than either botanist has in two years. Four days of testing settles it. They may not thank you. She wouldn't.

choices.sub: Four days with a sample kit

aired.title: IMPORTED AIR
aired.body: You run a line from the ship to the sample lock and open it. The near side of the dome brightens at once: color in faces, a laugh, someone jogging. Across the beans the far side presses its noses to the glass, then posts an objection: the closure is broken, the whole thing is void, and could they have some too. The near side sends you a crate of beans through the lock as a matter of principle, and none to the far side as another.
aired.line: Don't give them any. They'll only breathe it.
aired.narrative: Pumped ship's air into one half of a sealed dome. The other half objected, and asked for some.

courier.title: CORRESPONDENCE
courier.body: For two days you walk the curve of the glass with notes. They get longer. They acquire footnotes. On the second day each side asks you to pass on its grievances in order of importance, and the two lists are, again, very nearly the same list. Both pay the postage in produce, generously, so as not to be outdone. The air in the dome falls another hair while you work.
courier.narrative: Carried notes for two days between two botanists twenty meters apart. They paid the postage in vegetables.

swapped.title: IN THEIR OWN WORDS
swapped.body: You hand each side its own note. Each reads it twice. On the east side the botanist goes pink. On the west side the other one sits down on an upturned bucket. It is the first reasonable thing either has read from over there in two years. By the end of the day the two of them meet in the beans and agree on every point, at length, while the oxygen goes on falling around them. They thank you through the glass, breathing hard.
swapped.line: They make some very good points. I've always said so.
swapped.narrative: Handed two feuding botanists their own notes. They agreed with every word, and the air in their dome kept falling.

walled.title: CHALK
walled.body: Four days of scrapings and a borrowed acid later, the answer is fizzing in a dish. The bare concrete has been drinking the dome's carbon dioxide and turning it into chalk, and taking the oxygen down with it. Both sides read your results through the glass at the same moment. They seal the concrete, and the air begins to climb. Each sends you a sack of produce, so the other cannot take the credit, and opens a new dispute about whose idea the concrete was.
walled.line: Concrete. Who poured the concrete? Ask them who poured it.
walled.narrative: Spent four days proving a sealed dome's concrete was eating its air. Both sides believed it, and blamed each other for the concrete.

science_link.text: Biosphere 2, a sealed three-acre greenhouse in Arizona, held eight people from 1991 to 1993. Before the first mission was half over, they had split into two factions, barely on speaking terms.
science_link.label: Biosphere 2

intro.title: BY ROYAL ASSENT
intro.body: The hail comes from the hive on the rock below, with a fanfare of several thousand wings struck at once. On the screen, in a chamber of chewed paper, sits a human in the rags of a flight suit and a crown of wax. Insects queue at their elbow in a line that runs out of the frame. Each one in turn dances a question. The human answers every one in a word, without looking up. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Left. Yes. The blue one. No. Sorry, are you real? My pod came down here and they asked me which way, and I said left. Just like that. They'd never seen anyone do it. Thursday. Please get me off this rock. No. Not you, them.

ai.aria: A human QUEEN! ARIA always knew someone would spot real leadership potential! Look at all those little faces waiting for an answer!
ai.marv: One answer every four seconds, all day, from one person. MARV has counted. At that rate the castaway has not slept since the pod came down, and the queue is longer than when they started.
ai.rex: One human, one crown, and something over ten thousand subjects with no chain of command to talk to. Nobody down there can call anything off. REX is keeping the engines warm.
ai.chip: A monarchy with one employee! CHIP sees a staffing crisis! DecisionRight™ places a qualified decider in any hive, billed per decision, and that is a LOT of decisions!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes that they asked to be taken off the rock, and that a hive goes where its queen goes. Ask how the hive feels about that before opening a hatch. She would have asked first.

revisit.body: The castaway is still answering. The line at their elbow is no shorter.
revisit.line: Yes. No. Are you still there? Left.

choices.text: Give the hive a coin: 10 gold

swarm.title: A SWARM FOLLOWS
swarm.body: The castaway gets as far as standing up. Every insect in the chamber stands up too, and then the walls do. The hive is lifting off the rock, comb, grubs and all, in one dark slow cloud, and turning toward your airlock. Not one of them chose to come. A hive does not choose. It goes where the deciding is.
swarm.line: Oh, no. Sit. SIT. They sat. I can hold them there while I'm here to hold them. The moment I'm not, they come.

ai.aria: The whole kingdom wants to come along! ARIA loves a big family! There is plenty of room if everyone breathes in!
ai.marv: A honeybee swarm leaves home with its queen. This one has no scout that would ever disagree with the castaway. The hold would take all of them, briefly. MARV would rather not do the arithmetic on the vents.
ai.rex: REX will not open a door to ten thousand subjects of a foreign power. He will not leave a human with them either. These two positions are at war, and REX is losing to both.
ai.chip: Mass transit! CHIP charges per passenger, and this is a LOT of passengers! Group rates do not apply to insects, under clause nine!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the castaway only holds them while present, so one standing order before leaving would hold forever. Nobody in there can cancel it. She would think about what forever means to a hive first.

coin.title: HEADS
coin.body: You send a gold coin down the line, and the castaway shows the hive what it does. The hive takes nothing on trust. For four days it puts the coin through quorum after quorum, flipping it, watching it land, waiting for it to consult anyone. It never does. On the fourth day the hive crowns it. The castaway takes off the wax, sits down in a corner and decides something entirely for themselves: to stay. A comb of royal jelly comes up in thanks.
coin.line: I'm staying. Nobody asked me to. I just am.
coin.narrative: Gave a hive a gold coin to rule it. The coin decides everything alone now, and the castaway it replaced decided to stay.

regent.title: REGENCY
regent.body: The castaway hands you the queue and falls asleep where they sit. For two days you decide things for ten thousand insects: which tunnel, which grub, which flower on which rock. You have no idea. Every answer is obeyed at once, with joy. On the second day a crown of wax arrives on the bridge, sized for you, and wax cables start going across to your hull. You tear free with the castaway still asleep, rested for once, and the queue already forming at their elbow.
regent.narrative: Ruled a hive for two days so its human queen could sleep. Leaving cost hull. The queue was already back.

carried.title: SWARM IN THE HOLD
carried.body: You open the hatch and the hive comes in like weather. For four days the hold hums. The vents clog with wings, the stores go down fast, and the castaway sits in the galley giving orders through a cup pressed to the bulkhead. At the first rock with a crevice in it the hive pours out to look it over. The castaway stands in the airlock a long time. Then they follow it out.
carried.narrative: Carried a whole hive to a new rock for its human queen. The queen went with it.

standing.title: STANDING ORDER
standing.body: The castaway turns to the hive and says it: stay, and keep staying. The insects settle. The walls settle. The line at the elbow folds up and sits down. Then the castaway walks out of the chamber, and the hive does not follow. It will not stand up again, because there is no one in it who could decide to. They ride with you a while, eating slowly, asking that nothing be decided for them, and when they leave they tell no one which way.
standing.line: Don't ask me anything. Please. Thank you.
standing.narrative: Took a hive's human queen aboard after one last order: stay. The hive is still staying.

dismissed.title: DISMISSED
dismissed.body: The castaway looks at you for a long moment, then gives the order: let the strangers go. It is obeyed before the sentence ends. The hive sees you to the edge of its rock in a cloud that drums on the hull all the way out and leaves marks in the paint. Behind you the queue has already reformed. As the channel drops you can hear a voice saying yes.
dismissed.line: Let them go. Yes. No. Thursday.
dismissed.narrative: Left a human ruling a hive that would not let them stop. They ordered the ship let go.

science_link.text: A honey bee swarm leaving its hive clusters around its queen on a nearby branch, and sends a few dozen scouts out to find a new home.
science_link.label: Swarming (honey bee)

intro.title: QUORUM OF ONE
intro.body: A pod the size of a garden shed hangs off your bow with its beacon running. The beacon is not asking for help. It is asking whether it may ask for help, and has been for thirty-four years. Inside is a single hive worker, the far end of a foraging trail whose other end has gone. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Motion: that this worker is lost. Needs a quorum. Present: one. Can you be more than that?

ai.aria: A tiny new friend AND a meeting! ARIA has already voted yes on everything, including things nobody has proposed yet!
ai.marv: One worker. One beacon, unanswered for thirty-four years. It cannot ask for rescue, because asking is a group decision and it is not a group. MARV has read worse constitutions. Not many.
ai.rex: Single occupant, no weapons, beacon on a loop. That is how ambushes open. Keep the guns warm while we vote.
ai.chip: Motion Seconding is a premium service! The free trial ran for the first thirty-four years! CHIP is told that window has closed!
ai.ajoy: That beacon is worth some scrap to anyone with a wrench, and it couldn't stop you. It also can't accept help until it's allowed to, so hear it out first. AJOY saw you looking at the wrench.

revisit.body: The worker waits at its window. The beacon goes on asking whether it may ask.
revisit.line: Motion stands. Present: still one.

choices.sub: It has no way to object

floor.title: THE FLOOR
floor.body: A quorum, the worker explains, is not counted. It is bumped into. A scout knows a matter is settled when it keeps meeting others who think so, and then it stops needing to ask. It has met no one in thirty-four years. It wonders, with great formality, whether someone might come to the lock and bump into it.
floor.line: A vote is only talk. Come and be encountered. Often.

ai.aria: It's a hug with procedure! ARIA has seconded the hug!
ai.marv: It needs its encounter rate over a threshold. Two days of someone in a suit walking into it should do. MARV has worked out how many bumps that is. He would rather not say it aloud.
ai.rex: A suit, an unknown lock, repeated physical contact with an alien. REX wants it logged as the worst order of his retirement.
ai.chip: Suit hours are billable! So is the oxygen! But a thank-you from a hive is an endorsement CHIP could license for years!
ai.ajoy: An aye over the radio won't count. It just told you that. Doing it right costs two days and a little oxygen, and it may have something to give afterward. AJOY would go. You'll say it was your idea.

choices.text: Go to the lock and bump into it

q_bump.title: MOTION CARRIED
q_bump.body: It takes two days of someone in a suit walking slowly into a very small insect and apologizing. Partway through the second day the worker stops counting. The motion carries, thirty-four years late: it is lost. Being officially lost entitles it to turn around. It passes a lump of amber through the lock, the only thing it has left, and sets off back along the trail at a walking pace.
q_bump.narrative: Spent two days bumping into a lost worker until it reached a quorum. It is now officially lost, and very relieved. It left us a lump of amber that smells of authority.

q_radio.title: HEARSAY
q_radio.body: You say aye on an open channel. The worker thanks you for the hearsay and enters it in the minutes. It keeps the minutes in its head, and mentions that space is limited. Nothing else changes. The beacon is still asking when it drops off your scope.
q_radio.narrative: Voted aye over the radio. A lost worker recorded it as hearsay. Its beacon is still asking.

q_beacon.title: NO OBJECTIONS
q_beacon.body: The worker watches you unbolt the beacon. It raises no objection, because an objection needs a quorum. It does ask that the removal be noted, then notes it, then begins to second its own note and stops, because that would be out of order. Nobody says much at dinner.
q_beacon.narrative: Stripped a lost worker's beacon for parts. It could not object. Nobody aboard did, and it has been quiet since.

science_link.text: Some ants choose a new nest without any one ant comparing every option. Scouts sense a quorum when the rate at which they meet other ants passes a threshold, and then the colony moves.
science_link.label: Quorum sensing

intro.title: YOU HAVE BEEN ACQUIRED
intro.body: A long pale trading hull slides alongside and sends over an organizational chart. Your ship is on it, in a small box near the bottom, reporting to a department that appears to be one wing. Nobody aboard has agreed to anything. The chart is already in its third revision, and you have been reassigned twice. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Congratulations. We have acquired you. You may continue to feel like a ship during the transition.

ai.aria: We got promoted! ARIA has never been a department before! ARIA would love a lanyard!
ai.marv: The chart lists 6.2 million staff and one dotted line to us. MARV looked for the signature that makes this binding. It is a smell. It is on the hull. It got there during the approach.
ai.rex: A takeover with no shots fired is still a takeover. They tagged the hull on approach. REX has reclassified every box on that chart as a target.
ai.chip: CHIP's legal team would like a word about non-compete clauses! CHIP's legal team is CHIP! CHIP bills by the quarter hour, including this one!
ai.ajoy: Nothing here is for sale, because nothing here is anyone's. They do move goods between departments for a charge, and that charge is a price. Read the terms before you touch the basket. AJOY said before.

revisit.body: The chart has reached its fifth revision. You are still on it, in a slightly different box.
revisit.line: Transition proceeding. Your feelings remain supported.

choices.sub: One page, supplied as a smell

choices.text: Lay the Hive Lozenge on the scanner

terms.title: TERMS OF INTEGRATION
terms.body: The terms arrive through the vents, and the translator reads them out with evident reluctance. All assets are shared. All liabilities are shared, and the hive's are larger. Integration proceeds on a date to be set by quorum. An integration team is included. Waiting at your lock, in a large crate, is a welcome basket.
terms.line: Nobody decided this. It was merely agreed. Take the basket. It is yours, in the sense that everything is.

ai.aria: A welcome basket! ARIA reads 'integration team' as 'new friends who bring snacks'!
ai.marv: The food in the basket is real. So is the clause about the team. It says included. It does not say where. The crate is rather large for its contents.
ai.rex: That crate has a false bottom or REX is a toaster. Scan it. Scan it again. Then don't open it.
ai.chip: Contractors keep their ship AND invoice by the hour! CHIP's Contractor Starter Kit is sold separately, and CHIP is what it is sold by!
ai.ajoy: The basket is free food now and someone else's plan for your ship later. Contractor status needs a diplomat. Asking who's in charge costs four days and some stores. You'd have taken the basket, wouldn't you.

choices.sub: Food, water, a box on the chart
Send the question up the chart

m_basket.title: WELCOME TO THE TEAM
m_basket.body: The basket holds dried meal, sealed water and a small card that smells of congratulations. It weighs more than its contents can account for, and once it has been emptied nobody can quite find the bottom of it. The chart updates. Your ship now has a cost center.
m_basket.line: Onboarding complete. Integration will find you.
m_basket.narrative: Accepted a hive's welcome basket and, with it, a small box on its organizational chart. The food was good. The crate was heavier than it should have been.

m_contract.title: INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR
m_contract.body: {crew.diplomat} spends two days establishing that a ship cannot be merged if it is merely consulting. The hive has no word for this and is fascinated. Your box moves to a dotted line off the side of the chart, and a fee for the consultation arrives, which nobody over there feels they personally paid.
m_contract.narrative: Talked our way out of a merger and into a consulting fee. We are now a dotted line, and proud of it.

m_incharge.title: ESCALATED
m_incharge.body: The question goes up the chart. The chart has no top. Four days later it comes back down the other side, addressed to you, with a note that the decision appears to have been yours and asking whether you wish to rescind it. You do, having eaten into the stores the whole time you were on hold. The chart loses one small box, and six million staff return to whatever they were doing.
m_incharge.line: Rescinded. Thank you for your leadership.
m_incharge.narrative: Asked a hive who was in charge. Four days later the answer came back: we were. We canceled the merger.

m_reverse.title: REVERSE TAKEOVER
m_reverse.body: The scanner reads the Lozenge and the chart stops updating. Then it redraws, slowly, with your ship in the box at the top. For one afternoon the trading hull reports to you. Its stores move to your hold as an internal transfer, and no one objects, because there is no one. By evening the chart has gone back, apart from a note that you were a very fair manager.
m_reverse.line: Understood. It is all yours, in the sense that everything is.
m_reverse.narrative: Showed a merger the Hive Lozenge and ran the whole trading hull for an afternoon. Its stores are in our hold now. We got a good review.

intro.title: CUSTOMS
intro.body: The insect concession runs its own customs, and customs is a rack of small bottles. Papers here are worn: a clerk dabs your wrist and you have been processed. This clerk reaches past the entry permit and dabs you with something that smells of old frying oil. In the corridor, two workers stop, turn around and lift you gently by the elbows. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Condolences. You are dead. Two days, by the smell. Please do not struggle. It upsets the bearers.

ai.aria: You look so relaxed! Being carried is a wonderful way to see the station!
ai.marv: Oleic acid. It is what this hive reads on a corpse, and it is now reading it on you. You are talking, which is not admissible. You are also breathing, which is not admissible either.
ai.rex: Captain is being removed by two hostiles with excellent grip. REX can't engage: it's been filed. Who else has access to those bottles? What is in the others?
ai.chip: CHIP offers its condolences! Also the Afterlife Continuity Plan, which keeps your subscriptions active through any change in status!
ai.ajoy: Arguing won't work; they read smell, not speech. Washing works and costs water. They're taking you to the midden, where everything this quarter throws out ends up, machinery included. Not that you asked.

revisit.body: The bearers have set you down and are waiting, without impatience, for the formalities to end.
revisit.line: Still deceased. Objections may be lodged by your hive.

choices.text: Scrub it off in the washroom
choices.sub: Water, and no scent at all

choices.text: Set the Hive Lozenge on the desk

choices.sub: Let the bearers have their way

intro.leave_sub: Walk away from it, still dead

appeal.title: APPEAL
appeal.body: The clerk hears your appeal with every courtesy and writes nothing down, since nothing you have said smells of anything. A death may be contested only by your hive, and you have no hive. There is a lesser status available, in a separate bottle. There is also your post: a dead worker's position passes to the next in line, with its open account.
appeal.line: Two remedies. Deceased, Ambulatory, for a fee. Or your post may be filled. Speech is only weather.

ai.aria: Deceased, Ambulatory is a fantastic new job title! ARIA is updating your bio right now!
ai.marv: The fee buys the right to walk around dead. It is the most accurate description of this voyage MARV has yet seen in an official document.
ai.rex: You'd be paying the people who killed you on paper. And nobody has ever said 'replacement' near REX and had it end quietly. Send someone armed.
ai.chip: A vacancy is a growth opportunity! CHIP has drafted your will regardless, in which CHIP is mentioned warmly and at length, for a modest fee!
ai.ajoy: Filling the post needs a diplomat, and it pays out, because the post keeps its open account. The bottle always works, which is the most AJOY will say for it. Neither requires you to keep arguing, if that was the plan.

choices.sub: A paper you can walk in

appeal.leave_sub: Walk away from it, still dead

lc_carried.title: THE MIDDEN
lc_carried.body: The bearers carry you the length of the concession, past a great many polite antennae, and set you down on the midden with everything else this quarter has finished with. You walk back. They carry you out again. It takes two days and four trips for the oil to wear off, and by the last one you know where the good scrap is.
lc_carried.narrative: Was carried to a hive's midden four times over two days, on the grounds of being dead. Came back with salvage. Nobody aboard is to call it the funeral.

lc_wash.title: BELOW NOTICE
lc_wash.body: It takes a stiff brush and {cost.water} points of water hauled over from the ship. The smell of death goes, and so does every other smell you had. The bearers walk straight through the place where you are standing. For the rest of the stop nobody in the concession so much as turns an antenna toward you, which you find you mind more than you expected.
lc_wash.narrative: Washed off a death certificate with ship's water. This also removed every other document, and in that quarter we are now nobody.

lc_estate.title: BACKFILLED
lc_estate.body: A dead worker's post passes to the next in line, with its open account. {crew.diplomat} spends two days getting you hired as your own replacement, and the hive pays out the balance. The record stays as it is. In this quarter your ship is now operated by your successor, and the clerk asks that you pass on its condolences.
lc_estate.line: The post is filled. The previous holder's belongings may be collected by the holder.
lc_estate.narrative: {crew.diplomat} got the captain hired as the late captain's replacement. It paid out. The record still says dead.

lc_ambulatory.title: DECEASED, AMBULATORY
lc_ambulatory.body: The clerk selects a new bottle, which smells of old oil and, faintly, of shoes. The bearers sniff your wrist, confer, and put you down. You are still dead, but you are now permitted to walk, and the workers in the corridor step aside for you with the respect due to anyone getting on with things under difficult circumstances.
lc_ambulatory.line: Do not linger. It is bad for morale.
lc_ambulatory.narrative: Paid to be reclassified as Deceased, Ambulatory. The captain has asked that this appear on the next set of business cards.

lc_lozenge.title: DEATH BENEFIT
lc_lozenge.body: The clerk reads the Lozenge and stands very straight. It outranks the bottle, but nothing outranks a record, so the two are reconciled in the only way the hive permits: you remain dead, and are entitled to a senior's death benefit, payable to you in person, with the bearers' apologies and a crate of funeral provisions.
lc_lozenge.line: Deceased with distinction. Please sign with your wrist.
lc_lozenge.narrative: Showed a customs clerk the Hive Lozenge and collected the captain's own death benefit, in person. Funeral catering was included and was very good.

science_link.text: Ants can tell a dead nestmate by its chemical signature. In some cases the signal is oleic and linoleic acid, produced as fats break down, which can take about two days.
science_link.label: Necrophoresis

intro.title: THE RECITAL
intro.body: Forty ships arrive in formation and do not open fire. They open a program. It lists one work, in nine thousand figures, with no intermission, and a line of small type: attendance is mandatory and notes will be collected. Every screen on your bridge shows the same lit stage, where a single dancer raises its abdomen and begins to shake. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Sit. Watch. Nobody leaves during a first performance. *bzzt* There is no second.

ai.aria: A free show! ARIA adores the arts! ARIA gives this nine thousand stars out of nine thousand, and it has only just started!
ai.marv: Forty ships, and more of them turn to the dancer on every run. That is the problem. The dance has a plot. MARV will tell you what it is about if you look closely. You will not enjoy it.
ai.rex: Forty hulls, thin armor, no command ship. They will never strike their colors, because nobody has the authority. A fight ends when they're gone and not before.
ai.chip: CHIP has secured you premium seating! Premium seating is your seat! Refunds are available to anyone who leaves alive, less a handling fee!
ai.ajoy: Don't sit down yet. Study the choreography first; it costs nothing and it isn't really dance. And if you still have that lump of amber, this hive takes rank seriously, and recitals have judges. Try to look like you thought of it.

revisit.body: The dancer has reached figure four hundred. The stage has not dimmed. Nobody appears to have blinked, and nobody out there can.
revisit.line: Eyes front. Notes are still required.

choices.sub: Four days, and then the plot

reading.title: THE CHOREOGRAPHY
reading.body: Slowed down, it is not art. Each run's angle from the vertical is a bearing off the local star. The length of the shake is a distance. Over and over, the dancer is telling forty ships the way to your water tank. It cannot be stopped. It can be upstaged: a swarm goes where the last convincing dance told it to, and your ship has a nose it can shake.
reading.line: You are looking at the floor. Eyes on the stage.

ai.aria: We get to DANCE! ARIA has been preparing for this! ARIA has been preparing for everything!
ai.marv: A figure eight with a shaking run, pitched forty degrees wrong, tells them your water is behind that large dry rock. It wants a steady pilot. It is the only choreography MARV has ever found useful.
ai.rex: A dance routine in front of forty hostiles. Thirty years of service. Do it tight, do it once, and nobody ever hears that REX called the turns.
ai.chip: Choreography rights are reserved! CHIP has licensed the figure eight! You owe CHIP for the eight!
ai.ajoy: A pilot can sell the false bearing for some fuel. Without one you'll fool about half of them. A diplomat could give a note instead, since any change needs a quorum. AJOY would have started with the pilot. She would have started earlier.

choices.text: Fly the false bearing by hand
choices.sub: Half a dance, half a swarm

rc_sat.title: FINAL CURTAIN
rc_sat.body: The recital runs four days. It is, you have to admit, rather good. In the last hour the audience rises as one and comes across in perfect order, because the piece was about your water tank and everyone has now seen it. They take {cost.water} points of water and {cost.food} of food. Someone collects your notes on the way out.
rc_sat.narrative: Sat through a four-day recital by a pirate hive. The dance turned out to be directions to our water.

rc_walkout.title: OUT DURING THE PERFORMANCE
rc_walkout.body: You burn for open space with the dancer in mid-figure. Nobody chases you at first, since nobody can decide to. Then the dance changes, one bearing to the next, and thirty ships come after you as a single thought. You outrun most of it over two days. The rest leaves marks.
rc_walkout.narrative: Walked out of a pirate hive's recital. They updated the choreography and came after us, and the hull has the reviews.

rc_judge.title: THIRD PLACE
rc_judge.body: You set the Lozenge before the camera and the dancer stops in mid-figure. Forty ships wait. It has been a long time since one of their recitals had a judge. You take two days over the decision, and award third place. There are no other entrants. The hive receives this in a silence you can feel through the hull, pays the adjudicator's customary fee out of its stores and withdraws to rehearse.
rc_judge.line: Third. Understood. We will begin again. From the beginning. All of us.
rc_judge.narrative: Judged a pirate hive's recital and awarded third place in a field of one. They paid the fee and went away to rehearse.

rc_counter.title: A SHORT WORK FOR ONE SHIP
rc_counter.body: {crew.pilot} takes the ship across the front of the stage in a tight figure eight, thrusters shaking on every run, pitched forty degrees wrong. It takes two days and a lot of fuel to get right. Nobody in a hive is in charge of doubting. One ship swings to the new bearing, then ten, then all of them, at speed and in excellent formation, toward a large and waterless rock.
rc_counter.narrative: {crew.pilot} danced a false bearing at a forty-ship pirate hive, and the hive believed it. It is presumably still looking for the tank.

rc_clumsy.title: MIXED NOTICES
rc_clumsy.body: You fly the figure by hand for two days and it shows. The bearing wobbles and the runs come out uneven. About half the audience heads for the rock. The other half reads the rest of the performance as a confirmation, and comes for the tank. They get {cost.water} points of water and some paint before the first half comes back asking questions.
rc_clumsy.narrative: Tried to out-dance a pirate hive by hand. Half of them went for the rock. The other half had notes.

rc_note.title: NOTES
rc_note.body: {crew.diplomat} opens a channel and observes, with respect, that the fourth figure runs seven degrees flat. The dancer stops. A change to a work requires a quorum of those who saw it, so forty ships must now settle what seven degrees means. Nobody is watching the stage when you ease away two days later on a quiet burn, with the coolant venting {cost.water} points of water to keep your heat off their scopes.
rc_note.narrative: {crew.diplomat} gave a pirate hive a note on its choreography. As far as anyone knows, they are still discussing it.

science_link.text: A honeybee's waggle dance gives a direction by its angle and a distance by how long the run lasts. When dancers compete, they may even disrupt each other's dances.
science_link.label: Waggle dance

title: Follow the Ship in Front

ai_flavor.aria: We've joined a convoy! Four hundred and twelve new neighbors, and not one of them has complained about the noise!
ai_flavor.marv: Each tender follows the scent of the one ahead. None of them chose this, because none of them could. At this pace we reach the floor of the fuel gauge before we reach anything else. It is a perfect system. It has one output.
ai_flavor.rex: Four hundred twelve hulls, zero answering. That's no convoy. That's a graveyard in formation. Get us out before something back there decides we're staff.
ai_flavor.chip: Congratulations on your FrequentTrail status! Every lap earns points! Points may be redeemed upon exiting the ring! Exiting the ring is a premium feature!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The wake thins out somewhere in the ring, and a turn will take there. Use the scanner. Or pull the breaker and coast, if you have eight days to waste. A xenobiologist could mix a stronger trail. You were about to say that, AJOY is sure.

body: The autopilot has found a lane. The chart shows no lane here.
