What the hull sniffer shows is a scent wake, strong and very old, and the ship laying it is a hive tender, following the tender ahead of that. You count four hundred and twelve, nose to tail, in a ring around nothing. None answers. The helm declines to leave a marked trail. Your ship is number four hundred and thirteen. The autopilot reports excellent progress.
alt_bodies: Nobody steered into this. The autopilot picked up a scent wake in the dark and took it for a lane, as it is licensed to do. Ahead, a hive tender running without lights sits nose to the tail of another, and that one nose to the tail of the next. Four hundred and twelve hulls in a ring around nothing, for what the wake's age says is sixty years. A tender has closed up behind you. The autopilot calls this good traffic.

The hull sniffer wakes everyone with a reading it has filed under ROAD. It is a scent wake, thick as paint, curving gently away in both directions. The autopilot has already joined it, in the gap between two silent hive tenders, and will not be told otherwise. Each tender follows the one in front. There are four hundred and twelve, and the one in front of the first is the last.

choices.text: Find the thin place in the wake

briefing.aria: It's a treasure hunt! Somewhere the trail goes thin! Find it and we get to leave, which ARIA hears is lovely this time of year!
briefing.marv: The wake thins where one tender dropped out long ago. Hold the scanner on it and turn there. Miss it and we take another lap, and laps are paid in fuel.
briefing.rex: Eyes on the scope. Find the weak point in the formation and break out through it. Do not touch the tenders.
briefing.chip: ScanRight™ finds thin spots in trails, budgets and warranties! Today's scan is complimentary, with a small complimentary fee!
briefing.ajoy: It's there. Watch where the reading dips, not where you're looking now. Turn when you have it, not after.

perfect.aria: You found the exit on the very first lap! The ring is going to miss us so much!
perfect.marv: Clean turn at the thinnest point, for five points of fuel. The ring has closed behind us. It has no idea we were here.
perfect.rex: Broke contact without a scratch. Hull secure. Keep the rear sensors on it anyway.
perfect.chip: A flawless exit! Your FrequentTrail points have expired! Renewal is available at participating rings!
perfect.ajoy: That was the spot. Nice turn. AJOY was pointing at it the whole time, but nice turn.

good.aria: We're out, and the scrape along the side is a lovely souvenir!
good.marv: A lap late, and we clipped a tender on the way out. Eight points of fuel, three of hull. It did not notice.
good.rex: Out of the ring. Minor contact with a hostile hull. It didn't return fire. REX still doesn't like it.
good.chip: You're out! Scrape coverage is not included in your plan! CHIP has several plans!
good.ajoy: You turned one lap late, and that was the scrape. It'll do. AJOY would have gone a lap sooner.

poor.aria: Several extra laps of quality time with our neighbors, and we still got out! Winning!
poor.marv: Several extra laps, two collisions and a bad seal. Fourteen points of fuel, eight of hull, six of oxygen. We left the ring. It did not remark on it.
poor.rex: We forced it. Hull damage, oxygen loss, two collisions. We are clear. Stay at stations.
poor.chip: Your exit has been processed, with penalty laps! CHIP accepts fuel, oxygen and hull as forms of payment!
poor.ajoy: You missed the thin place twice, and the third time you found it with the hull. We're out. Best keep that quiet.

outcome.narrative: You take the scanner and look for the place where the wake runs thin.

perfect.narrative: You find the place where the wake runs thin and turn there, and the helm comes back with a small cough. Two days, five points of fuel, and a loose strip of plate from the last tender on the way past. Behind you the ring closes over the gap as if nobody had ever been in it.

good.narrative: You find the thin place one lap later than you should have and turn hard, leaving three points of hull on the flank of the next tender in line. It does not break formation. Two days and eight points of fuel, and the helm is yours again.

poor.narrative: You lose the wake, find it and lose it again, and in the end you take the turn by force, through a tender. Fourteen points of fuel, eight of hull and six of oxygen through a sprung seal. Two days later the ring is behind you, one ship shorter, and still perfectly in step.

choices.text: Pull the autopilot's breaker and coast

outcome.narrative: You pull the breaker and let the ship fall out of the ring under nothing at all. It takes eight days, and with the breaker out the reclaimer loses {cost.water} points of water. For the first two, the tenders go past the ports at walking speed and you can see into the nearest ones. Everyone aboard is at their station, facing forward, following. For some time afterward nobody on your ship sits facing forward.

{crew.xenobiologist} cuts the fuel with whatever the sniffer says a wake is made of, and you burn a line straight out of the ring. The tender behind you swings onto it. So does the one behind that. Two days later you have four hundred and twelve dead ships following you toward the nearest large rock, and you step aside. It is the first decision anyone has made for them in sixty years. You collect what comes off.

science_link.text: Army ants that lose the main trail can lock into a circle, each following the ant in front, and may die of exhaustion. The first mill described, in 1921, was 370 meters around, and one lap took two and a half hours.
science_link.label: Ant mill

title: The Line of Succession

ai_flavor.aria: We could be HEAD OF STATE! ARIA has drafted an inaugural address! It is mostly about snacks!
ai_flavor.marv: The port lane takes four days at its present rate, and supplies go with them. The starboard pickets carry no orders, so they cannot be given new ones. MARV has run the numbers. The numbers decline to recommend.
ai_flavor.rex: Soldier caste, no command net, no surrender. Best-drilled picket REX ever saw and nobody drilled it. Starboard means hull damage. Port means standing in line with your back to all of it.
ai_flavor.chip: Head of State is a fantastic résumé line! CHIP offers Inaugural Packages from four days of your life! Treason is also available, at a higher deductible!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Port costs four days plus food and water. Starboard costs hull and fuel. A diplomat can shorten the queue, and a pilot can spare the hull. Use one. AJOY would have thought that went without saying, and yet.

body: Port, the lane marked {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, is full of ships, nose to tail, as far as the scope can reach. It is a queue. It is also the government of the hive that runs it: whichever ship reaches the front is head of state until it leaves. Starboard, the lane marked {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, is empty, because going around the government is treason, and the soldiers posted along it have never needed to be told that.

outcome.narrative: Four days nose to tail, moving up one ship at a time, at a cost of {cost.food} points of food and {cost.water} of water. At the front you are head of state for eleven minutes. An aide asks whether you have a policy. You say you would like to leave. This is enacted, with applause, and the lane opens.

choices.text: {crew.diplomat} finds you a place near the front

outcome.narrative: Politeness here means going in the right order, and the right order can be inherited. {crew.diplomat} establishes that your ship is the adopted offspring of a hauler near the front. The queue accepts this without comment. Two days later you pass through the office of head of state as a minor royal, and a hauler you have never met wishes you well.

You burn down the empty lane and the soldiers close from both sides, without a word or a signal. They make no attempt to stop you, since stopping you is nobody's job. Each one simply does a little damage as you pass, in turn, in order, and then the lane behind you is empty again.

{crew.pilot} takes the lane in long, expensive curves, keeping to the gaps between one soldier's duty and the next. Each picket lands only one blow. There are not many people who can say they committed treason this tidily, and {crew.pilot} intends to be one of them at every meal.

title: Open Plan

ai_flavor.aria: So much natural light! ARIA always said this ship had too many walls! Everyone is so close together now!
ai_flavor.marv: Four walls are gone so far. Two of them were holding something up. The integration plan is very thorough. It does not mention air.
ai_flavor.rex: Hostile sappers inside the pressure hull since the basket. REX said scan it. He said it twice. Seal what seals and treat every colleague as a target.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is thrilled to announce exciting changes to your living space! Walls are now a premium tier! Doors are the tier above that!
ai_flavor.ajoy: They go where the chart says, so change the chart. A diplomat can start a rumor about who owns the ship, and the Lozenge outranks the whole team. Failing that, the engineer. AJOY did mention the crate.

body: You wake to more light than usual. Overnight, someone has taken out the wall between the bunks and the galley. A card on the remaining door frame gives off a smell the translator renders as a friendly typeface: WE ARE EXCITED TO ANNOUNCE A MORE OPEN WAY OF WORKING. Small pale workers are filing through the gap with the galley door. They came aboard in the welcome basket. They have been in the walls ever since, and there is now one desk.

outcome.narrative: You tell everyone to carry on. By the next morning the workers have finished, taken the door off the head as a final improvement, and reclassified the pantry as a shared resource, at a cost of {cost.food} points of food. They file back into the ducts to await feedback. Nobody aboard has been alone since.

choices.text: Vent the ship, section by section
choices.sub: Hard on the air, harder on staff

outcome.narrative: You seal what will still seal and open the rest to space, one section at a time, for two days, and {cost.water} points of water go with it through the open lines. The workers go without fuss, in single file, in order of seniority. The last of them stops at the lock and waits, because nobody has told it that it may go first. You hold the hatch until it has been told.

{crew.engineer} puts the walls back faster than they can be proposed for removal. Each new wall is a change to the plan, and a change to the plan needs a quorum, so the workers stand in the corridors for four days waiting for one while the welding goes on around them. When the last seam cools they are gone, and the new walls are not quite as good as the old ones. Nobody has checked the ducts.

choices.text: Start a rumor about who owns the ship

outcome.narrative: {crew.diplomat} mentions in a duct, to nobody, that this ship was sold at the last quorum to a rival wing, and that all improvements are now that wing's liability. It reaches the last worker by evening. The galley door comes back, hung upside down. The team files out through the vents, and the chart grows smaller by one box.

You hold up the Lozenge and the column stops. The smell of it goes down the line from worker to worker, and by the next morning your ship has been spun off as an independent concern. They rehang the doors, rebuild the walls rather better than they found them, and leave the spare plate in a neat stack. The last card reads: WE WISH YOU EVERY SUCCESS IN YOUR FUTURE ENDEAVORS.

title: The Minutes of the Last Meeting

science_link.text: Ants, bees and wasps pass food from mouth to mouth, and the meal carries more than food: proteins, hormones and information travel with it.
science_link.label: Trophallaxis

intro.title: APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES
intro.body: Six million workers, no signage, and not one sheet of paper. Whatever this hive knows travels mouth to mouth in one continuous meal, and every worker on every ring is carrying some. Prices, tariffs, the docking schedule and last week's vote are all in there. At your lock, the recording secretary has stopped chewing and is holding its mouth open in your direction. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Welcome. Minutes of last meeting. Please open. *bzzt* Everyone has had them. You are late.

ai.aria: A welcome meal! Six million new friends, and they've all eaten already! ARIA calls that a very well-run potluck!
ai.marv: The meal on offer has been in circulation since the station opened. MARV has estimated how many mouths the average mouthful has been through. He would like to have not.
ai.rex: Open mouth at the lock, six million more behind it. REX has seen this tactic. It ended with an entire platoon knowing the tariff schedule.
ai.chip: Every mouthful is also a Terms of Service! CHIP admires a contract you can't un-swallow! Ask about SipSafe™ Disposable Straws!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says a written copy exists, at a price, and that a Hive Lozenge would turn the whole flow around, if one is aboard. She has also moved the toothbrushes to the front of the cabinet, in case.

revisit.body: The secretary's mouth is still open. The workers behind it have started to look at their feet.
revisit.line: Minutes still warm. Please open.

choices.text: Open up and take the minutes

choices.sub: Send the question down the hall

choices.text: Set the Hive Lozenge on your tongue

writing.title: THE PAPER COPY
writing.body: Your request goes down the corridor mouth to mouth and returns the same way. The hive does keep one kind of record for foreigners. A worker makes it on the spot: wood pulp and spit, chewed and pressed flat, still damp. There is no writing on it. It has a flavor. Alternatively, you may place a motion before the meeting, simply by feeding it to the secretary.
writing.line: Paper. Yes. Very tiring. Or bring a motion. Anything fed to first mouth is in the minutes by dinner.

ai.aria: A written copy, with flavor! ARIA loves a book that stays with you!
ai.marv: Paper made as wasps make it, from chewed wood and saliva. The copy costs gold and has no words on it. MARV has read worse.
ai.rex: Six million hostile stomachs and one pot of galley stew. REX has reviewed the plan and cannot find the part that isn't a war crime. He approves.
ai.chip: Print-on-Spit! CHIP is licensing the format! Terms and conditions are available by mouth!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the paper is the clean way to nearly the same fuel, and the stew pays better if a chef can spare the food.

min_swallow.title: TAKEN AS READ
min_swallow.body: You open. It tastes of warm honey, old coins and a tariff revision. For a moment you know the docking schedule and the price of everything, and you hold a firm opinion on last week's vote that is not yours. You also know where a full fuel tank is standing, owned by no one in particular. You collect it and brush your teeth twice, to no effect.
min_swallow.narrative: Swallowed a hive's minutes at the lock. Learned where the spare fuel was. Still tasting the tariff.

min_paper.title: PAPER COPY
min_paper.body: The copy is handed over damp. It says nothing to the eye. You hold it under your nose. When that fails, you tear off a corner and chew. The depot, the berth rates and the vote all arrive at once, with the involvement of no mouth but yours and, earlier, one tired worker's. The fuel is where the paper said.
min_paper.narrative: Bought a hive's minutes on chewed paper, read them in private, and found the fuel.

min_stew.title: PEPPERED
min_stew.body: {crew.chef} hands the secretary one ladle of galley stew, heavy on the pepper. It goes down the corridor. By the second shift it has reached the next ring, and by dinner on the second day six million workers have eaten the same bowl and the whole station is very slightly sneezing. The motion passes, in the sense that it has passed through everyone. The hive votes you its thanks, in coin and plate.
min_stew.narrative: Fed one ladle of stew to a hive's recording secretary. Six million sneezes later, the motion carried.

min_motion.title: THE FLOOR RECOGNIZES YOU
min_motion.body: The resin touches your tongue and the secretary shuts its mouth. So does the next worker, and the next. For one shift the meal runs the other way, and whatever you say goes in the minutes. You clear your throat and state that this ship is owed. By dinner six million workers know it, and no one in particular can object. Fuel, water and stores arrive at the lock in single file. The throat-clearing also passed, and now opens all sessions.
min_motion.narrative: Reversed a hive's minutes with the Lozenge. One sentence entered, one cough adopted, stores delivered.

title: Viewing by Appointment
leave_label: CAN'T LEAVE (THEY ARE MEASURING THE GALLEY)

science_link.text: A honey bee swarm sends scouts to inspect cavities. A good site has a small entrance and no ants, and the choice is often made once a quorum of 20 to 30 scouts is present.
science_link.label: Swarming (honey bee)

intro.title: DESIRABLE PROPERTY
intro.body: Someone is measuring your galley. Small pale scouts have come in through the vents, and a tender hangs off the bow with a board that smells of FOR SALE. A swarm is looking for somewhere to live, and it has seen your particulars: one dry cavity, small entrance, no ants. Every scout that likes the place flies back and dances about it. At thirty dances, the hive has moved in. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Good light. Small door. No ants. *bzzt* Twenty-seven like it. Current occupants to vacate by quorum.

ai.aria: We're a desirable property! ARIA always knew this ship had good bones! Someone has complimented the light!
ai.marv: Twenty-seven of thirty. Those are real criteria, and the ship meets them. It is the nicest thing anyone has said about this vessel. MARV notes that it is also an eviction.
ai.rex: Hostile surveyors inside the pressure hull, measuring. REX has seen this before an invasion and, once, before a kitchen renovation. He responded to both the same way.
ai.chip: CHIP can raise your valuation with HomeStage™ Cabin Fragrance! Agents, please note that commission is non-negotiable!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the vote needs thirty, that hives hate a draft and a bad smell, and that a xenobiologist could head-butt the dancers, which counts as a vote against. She has already put out a doormat. It says NO.

revisit.body: Another scout goes past with a length of string. The tender's board has been updated.
revisit.line: Twenty-eight. Good cupboards.

choices.sub: Open vents, leave out the bin

choices.text: Set the Hive Lozenge on the vent sill

offer.title: THE OFFER
offer.body: The offer arrives through the vents. The hive will take the ship as a going concern, and you may stay on as staff. An organizational chart comes with it, your ship in a small box near the bottom. At your lock sits a large crate: a welcome basket for the new department, dried meal and sealed water, and rather heavier than it ought to be.
offer.line: Offer accepted by twenty-nine. Take basket. Occupants become colleagues at thirty.

ai.aria: A welcome basket! ARIA loves baskets! Nothing bad has ever come in a basket!
ai.marv: The food is real and so is the water. The crate weighs more than its contents can account for. MARV ran it twice. The difference would fit in a wall.
ai.rex: REX wants that crate scanned. He has said so. He is saying so again. Nobody accepts a crate from a force that has been measuring the walls.
ai.chip: Congratulations on your pending subsidiary status! Group Rates begin at integration! Please retain your crate for warranty purposes!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would look in that crate before thanking anyone for it. Food is food and a box on a chart is a box on a chart, but she'd want to know what's under the fruit. She has said so. That's twice.

choices.sub: Food, water, a box on the chart

choices.text: Show them the chart you're already on

v_basket.title: MOVING IN
v_basket.body: You wave the last scout through. The thirtieth dance lasts a few seconds, and you are a department. The chart updates with your ship in its small box, and a card arrives that smells of congratulations. The crate comes aboard: dried meal, sealed water, and a basket nobody can quite find the bottom of. The tender backs away and takes down its board. The vents go quiet, which you take as a good sign.
v_basket.narrative: A hive viewed the ship and made an offer. There is a basket. We are a small box on a chart.

v_dup.title: INTERNAL TRANSFER
v_dup.body: You send over your box on the chart. The tender reads it and stops. Its wing has been selling a ship that another wing already owns, and neither can resolve this without a quorum, and the quorum is at the bottom of the same chart. The scouts file out in order, apologizing to one another. A consignment of stores comes across to cover the embarrassment, which no one in particular feels.
v_dup.narrative: A hive tried to buy a ship it already owned, apologized to itself and sent stores.

v_scan.title: CONTENTS MAY VARY
v_scan.body: You run the crate through the hold scanner before it crosses the sill. Under the fruit is a false floor. Under the floor, in neat rows, are several hundred small pale workers with their legs folded, holding tools. The crate goes back out of the lock with a lungful of your air behind it, and the dances stop at twenty-nine. You are not a department. You have also thrown a perfectly good lunch into the dark.
v_scan.narrative: Scanned the welcome basket. It was full of staff, and went out of the lock.

v_stink.title: DRAFTY
v_stink.body: You prop open every vent, crack a lock seal and leave the galley bin out for two days. It is an unpleasant way to treat your own home, and it costs a fair share of your air. The scouts walk the ship again with their antennae down, and the dances turn sour. The tender's board changes: DRAFTY. SMELLS OF MAMMAL. POSSIBLE ANTS. You are left alone in a ship you have spent two days ruining.
v_stink.narrative: Wrecked our own ship's curb appeal to fail a hive's viewing. It failed. So did the air.

v_butt.title: MINORITY REPORT
v_butt.body: {crew.xenobiologist} puts on a helmet and goes through the ducts for two days, butting each dancer in the thorax mid-figure. In a hive that counts as a vote against. Thirty scouts stop, one by one, and the listing lapses. {crew.xenobiologist} comes out with a headache, a jar of something useful from the vents and a mention in a minority report.
v_butt.narrative: {crew.xenobiologist} head-butted a property vote into the ground. Scouts gone. Headache remains.

v_sill.title: SPOKEN FOR
v_sill.body: You set the Lozenge on the sill of the main vent. The scouts nearest it stop. The smell goes down the line and the dance collapses from the top, since a house with that on the sill already belongs to someone very senior. The tender apologizes through the vents, withdraws the listing, and, because somebody must have paid for the viewing, refunds it to you in stores.
v_sill.narrative: Set the Lozenge on the vent sill. A hive withdrew its offer and paid us for the viewing.

science_link.text: Many reptiles never quite stop growing. They grow fast when young and keep growing, more slowly, after they reach adulthood.
science_link.label: Indeterminate growth

intro.title: NOT YET TWO HUNDRED
intro.body: A small ship holds station with its running lights off. On your screen sits a young reptile, in a cabin so cold the camera has frosted at the corners. It does not speak. It holds up a card, with the care of someone who has rehearsed this for some time. Behind it, wrapped around the pilot's seat, something much larger is not moving. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: [A card] I AM 183. I MAY NOT SPEAK UNTIL I AM 200. THIS IS NOT SPEAKING.

ai.aria: A card! ARIA adores cards! This one has only seventeen years to go, and ARIA knows they will simply fly by!
ai.marv: MARV has read the card. One hundred and eighty-three years old and legally too young to say so. He considers it the first sensible law he has met out here.
ai.rex: REX reads one mover and one large non-mover. No weapons hot. Nothing hot at all. He does not trust a ship with no heat signature, and this one has none.
ai.chip: CHIP sees an untapped youth market! Two centuries of pent-up opinions! CHIP can supply premium card stock at 12 gold the sheet!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the cabin reads just above freezing, and that the big one in the back is the problem, not the kid. We have a heat line. She assumes you remembered that.

revisit.body: The young one has gone back to the first card and is holding it very straight.
revisit.line: [A card] THIS IS STILL NOT SPEAKING.

choices.text: Read the rest of the cards

cards.title: THE REST OF THE CARDS
cards.body: The large shape is its grandmother, who is 640 and outranks everything for a light-year. The heater tripped on a fault and will restart only for the eldest aboard. She stopped when the cabin cooled, so she cannot authorize anything until she is warm, and she cannot be warm until she authorizes it. The young one has been sitting beside the switch for nineteen years.
cards.line: [A slightly worn card] I HAVE CHECKED THE LAW. IT IS VERY CLEAR.

ai.aria: What a tidy system! Everyone waits their turn and the heater gets a lovely rest! ARIA gives this family five stars!
ai.marv: MARV has reviewed the deadlock. The heater needs the eldest. The eldest needs the heater. Whoever drafted this was warm at the time.
ai.rex: REX has the switch on the feed. It sits forty centimeters from the kid's hand. It has sat there for nineteen years. He finds that level of discipline alarming.
ai.chip: A textbook approvals bottleneck! CHIP's Escalation Tier clears these in six to eight decades! Fees apply!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says heat from outside breaks no rule, since nobody aboard touched anything. An engineer could walk the kid past the lock instead, but then the old one wakes owing you nothing. She's only laying it out.

choices.text: Relay the cards on an open channel

sr1_heat.title: SEVENTEEN YEARS
sr1_heat.body: The line takes two days to bring her up. She opens one eye, and some time later the other, and regards the hose, the young one and you. She says nothing to you, since you are a child. She sets a warm ceramic disc in the airlock. The young one holds up a last card: I WILL SAY THIS OUT LOUD IN SEVENTEEN YEARS. IT IS THANK YOU.
sr1_heat.narrative: Warmed a 640-year-old reptile back to life over a fuel line. Her grandchild thanked us by card and promised to do it properly in seventeen years.

sr1_hotwire.title: FIRST OFFENSE
sr1_hotwire.body: {crew.engineer} writes out cards of their own, one step to a card, and over two days the young one reads each of them twice. Then it reaches out and does the worst thing it has ever done. The heater comes on. It looks at its own hand for a while. A crate of preserved stores arrives in your airlock, followed by one more card: NINETEEN YEARS. IT WAS ONE SCREW.
sr1_hotwire.narrative: Taught a 183-year-old minor to bypass a heater lock, by card. It paid in stores and will answer for it in about a century.

sr1_relay.title: RELAYED
sr1_relay.body: You read the cards out on the open channel, in order, in your own voice, on which the law has no view. Two days later a long slow ship answers from somewhere very far away and says it will arrive within the decade. The young one holds up a card of thanks and settles down to wait. It is extremely good at this.
sr1_relay.narrative: Relayed a silent distress call on the open channel. Help will reach them within the decade, which by their standards is prompt.

science_link.text: Cold-blooded animals depend on outside heat to reach working temperature, and as a rule they are sluggish until they have warmed up.
science_link.label: Ectotherm

intro.title: COLD CALL
intro.body: A trader's ship comes alongside at the speed of a slow thought. Its proprietor fills your screen, halfway through a blink, in a shop with a dead heater and a red tag on the heater. The cabin reads eleven degrees. The price board is still running, still correct, and the proprietor is watching it the way you might watch rain. At this temperature, it seems, it can no longer add. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Good morning. That will be. There was a number.

ai.aria: The shopkeeper is SO relaxed! ARIA has never seen a retail professional this calm! Everything here is practically a gift!
ai.marv: MARV has read the cabin thermometer. A reptile's arithmetic falls with temperature, and this one lost the ability to carry the one some degrees ago. He envies it.
ai.rex: REX has an armed trader running at a fifth of its speed. Slow is not the same as harmless. It will warm up one day, with its memory intact.
ai.chip: CHIP spies an unmatched arbitrage opportunity! CHIP also spies a liability! CHIP will advise on either for a modest retainer!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that it will do the sums as soon as it warms up, and it has relatives. A warm shopkeeper pays its debts too, if anyone cared to warm it. Anyway. Your ship.

revisit.body: The blink has finished. Another one has started.
revisit.line: Still here, are you. There was a number.

choices.text: Set the chit on the counter

choices.sub: It is very cold in there

cold.title: COLD PRICES
cold.body: The proprietor nods along to everything, slightly late. Offered nine gold for a whole stack of fuel cells, it begins to consider the figure, and you can watch the consideration set out on a long journey. Nothing about it says no. Behind it, the board flickers with the real prices. The bridge has gone quiet, the way a room does near an unattended till.
cold.line: Nine. Yes. That sounds like a number.

ai.aria: It said yes! ARIA loves a yes! A yes is a yes! ARIA has filed it under Forever!
ai.marv: MARV has the stack priced at about sixty gold. Nine is a figure. It is also evidence, and it will still be evidence in four hundred years. Reptile contracts do not lapse. He checked.
ai.rex: REX advises that a contract signed at eleven degrees gets read at twenty-five, by someone with a great many teeth. Nothing about this is safe.
ai.chip: CHIP's Compliance Division calls this a gray area! A gray area is a product! CHIP can sell you this one at a flat fee!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the fault is one burned-out relay, if we have an engineer who still takes an interest in that sort of thing. There's also robbing it. She didn't say anything.

sr2_chit.title: WHOLESALE
sr2_chit.body: Etiquette requires the proprietor to seat a chit-holder by the heater. Its heater is dead. The chit is not. It regards the warm little disc for a long while, closes both hands around it and shuts its eyes for most of two days. Then it hands the chit back, opens the rear of the shop and takes down the other price list, the one for those it owes.
sr2_chit.line: Warm. Thank you. This is what it costs me. Take it.
sr2_chit.narrative: Lent a frozen shopkeeper our Basking Chit for two days and came away with the wholesale list. The chit came back warmer, if anything.

sr2_warmed.title: BILLED BY THE DEGREE
sr2_warmed.body: You send a hot meal across, and then another, for two days. At nineteen degrees the proprietor finishes the blink. At twenty-four it reviews everything you have said and corrects it. Then, with visible effort, it recalls that it has been warmed, and that among its people this is a debt. A crate and a drum cross to your airlock, to the exact value of the meals, calculated to the tenth of a degree.
sr2_warmed.line: Twenty-four degreesss. Now. What was that about my prices.
sr2_warmed.narrative: Warmed a torpid trader with {cost.food} of hot food. It repaid the heat in stores, to the tenth of a degree.

sr2_cheat.title: RECEIPT ATTACHED
sr2_cheat.body: It counts out the stack and a case of stores and thanks you twice, the second thanks arriving after your airlock has closed. The fuel is excellent. The receipt is in perfect order, which is the part that stays with you. It will warm up one day and do the sums, and someone a great deal older will be told.
sr2_cheat.narrative: Bought a stack of fuel cells and a case of stores for nine gold from a trader too cold to count. The receipt is in order. So, eventually, will be the trader.

sr2_fixed.title: AN EXCELLENT INVOICE
sr2_fixed.body: {crew.engineer} spends two days behind the panel. The temperature climbs, and the proprietor's eyes come slowly into focus. By twenty-two degrees it has found an error in your invoice. By twenty-six it is a different creature: quick, exact and faintly terrifying. It pays in fuel, to the gram, and adds a box of spare fittings that it describes as a rounding difference.
sr2_fixed.line: You could have robbed me. I can see the figures. I find I am disappointed in you.
sr2_fixed.narrative: Repaired a frozen trader's heater. It woke up, found an error in our invoice, and paid in fuel to the gram.

intro.title: LOST PROPERTY
intro.body: The reptile quarter's clinic keeps a records office, warm in the corners and cold at the bench, which is where you have been asked to sit. On the desk, folded and tagged, lies a shed skin about four meters long. It came out of your air intake during refueling. Behind the officer, older skins hang along a rack, each with a ledger page pinned to it. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Among my people a debt lives in the skin. This one owes eight thousand gold and was found in your vent. In law, you have taken in a lodger.

ai.aria: Our first lodger! ARIA has always wanted a big family! So quiet, so flat, and already contributing paperwork!
ai.marv: MARV has read the ledger page. Eight thousand gold, unsecured, owed by a garment. He has known worse debtors and very few better behaved.
ai.rex: REX reads one officer, two exits and a bench set eight degrees below the rest of the room. That is interrogation architecture. He does not care for it.
ai.chip: A distressed asset in our own vent! CHIP can restructure it for a 15 percent arrangement fee! CHIP would very much like to meet whoever drafted this!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the officer keeps quoting a statute and never showing it. Ask what it actually says. And if we happen to be carrying anything warm, this would be the room for it. She's not telling you how to dock.

revisit.body: The skin is still on the desk. The bench has not warmed up.
revisit.line: Do continue. I have a further six hundred years.

choices.text: Set the chit on the desk
Register it as found property: 15 gold

intro.leave_sub: Walk away from it, for now

law.title: THE STATUTE
law.body: The officer turns a slab around on the desk. The statute is eleven words long and nine centuries old, and it has never been amended, because everyone it applied to agreed with it. The officer reads it aloud in the voice of someone who has never had reason to notice what it does not say.
law.line: Whosoever sheds a skin sheds all that is written upon it.

ai.aria: It says whosoever! ARIA is a whosoever! Everyone is a whosoever! This is the most welcoming law ARIA has ever read!
ai.marv: MARV has parsed all eleven words. It does not say reptile. It says nothing about species, length or dignity. He would like to be elsewhere when someone notices.
ai.rex: REX advises against entering any object he has not cleared. He has not cleared that object. He cannot see the far end of it.
ai.chip: CHIP's lawyers confirm the loophole! CHIP's lawyers decline to touch the skin! Fitting room access is 5 gold, billed later!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that it says whosoever. You would have to wear it, be seen coming out of it, and then live with the original creditor taking that personally. But it's your skin.

law.leave_sub: Walk away from it, for now

rack.title: THE RACK
rack.body: Most of the skins are long and scaled, with sums in the thousands. Toward the back hang a dozen that are not. They are short and pale and shaped very much like people you passed on the way in. One still has a lanyard. One is in an excellent suit. All are tagged PAID. The officer moves, without hurry, to stand in front of them.
rack.line: Those are not open to the public. Nobody has ever asked who they fit. I would keep that record going.

ai.aria: What a fun costume closet! That one has a lovely suit! ARIA thinks they are all just very private people!
ai.marv: MARV has compared the rack against this station's staff directory. He has stopped. He will not be resuming. He recommends you do the same.
ai.rex: REX has measured all twelve. Same height. Same shoulders. Same handwriting on the tags. He wants to leave and would like that in the record.
ai.chip: CHIP recognizes three former account holders! CHIP is not authorized to have a reaction! Nondisclosure runs 40 gold a month, starting now!
ai.ajoy: AJOY wouldn't ask about the lanyard. She's fairly sure it's the one thing in this room that gets us out at once, and equally sure you'd rather it hadn't. So. Up to you.

choices.sub: You think you know the name

rack.leave_sub: Walk away from it, for now

sr3_chit.title: THE BOOKS TURNED AROUND
sr3_chit.body: The officer looks at the disc and gets up from the warm seat. A chit means this quarter owes you warmth, and a creditor cannot be kept on a cold bench. The ledger is turned around. You are now the party who returned a lost debtor to the quarter, and there is a finder's fee, which the officer counts out with no expression at all. The chit is handed back in both hands.
sr3_chit.line: You will find the heater on your left. I apologize for the bench. I do not apologize for anything else.
sr3_chit.narrative: Set a Basking Chit on the desk and went from harboring a debtor to collecting a finder's fee for one, in the space of an afternoon.

sr3_shed.title: SHED
sr3_shed.body: The statute wants the skin worn for a full day and shed before a witness. You go in at the head end. There is a great deal of it left over, and it smells like a closed suitcase. On the second day you come out backward, slowly, while the officer looks on like someone reading their own retirement date. A stamp comes down. Eight thousand gold, gone, with a rebate.
sr3_shed.line: Shed. I will have to tell someone about this. I will have to tell someone very old.
sr3_shed.narrative: Wore a stranger's skin for a day, took it off before a witness, and legally discharged eight thousand gold of somebody else's debt. The creditor has been informed.

sr3_fee.title: FILED
sr3_fee.body: The officer stamps the tag and hangs the lodger on the rack, where its debt becomes the rack's problem, and the rack has time. You receive a receipt, which is warm from the printer. It is the warmest thing that has happened to you in this room.
sr3_fee.narrative: Paid to register a stranger's skin as found property. The debt now belongs to a rack.

sr3_asked.title: SO GLAD YOU STOPPED BY
sr3_asked.body: The officer looks at you for exactly as long as it takes you to notice. Then, quite gently, it tears up the tag on the lodger, stamps your clearance and walks you to the door with a hand on your arm. The hand is very dry. Nobody mentions the skin again, or the lanyard. You could not swear to what was printed on it. You feel you were introduced to it this morning.
sr3_asked.narrative: Asked the wrong question about the wrong lanyard. The debt was dropped at once. Nobody aboard feels good about why.

sr3_walk.title: NOTED
sr3_walk.body: You stand up and leave. The officer does not stop you and does not look up. It writes one line, slowly, and blows on it. There is no hurry. The skin stays on the desk with your hull number on its tag, and a copy of the line goes to someone a great deal older.
sr3_walk.narrative: Walked out on a stranger's skin and eight thousand gold of its debts. Nobody stopped us. Nobody seemed to feel the need.

science_link.text: Given a path, heat always flows on its own from a hotter body to a colder one. With no pump in the line, heat runs toward whichever end is colder.
science_link.label: Second law of thermodynamics

intro.title: ROOM TEMPERATURE
intro.body: A long gray ship slides up on your night side and sets a hose against your hull, very gently, the way a nurse finds a vein. Its guns are out. Its captain has no interest in your cargo, your gold or your name. It has been reading your hull temperature from nine thousand kilometers, and it wears the glazed, tender look of someone smelling bread. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Twenty-one degrees in there. Twenty-one. All of it, pleassse. You may keep the lights.

ai.aria: They only want the heat! That's the nicest kind of robbery! ARIA has always felt this ship could use a brisk new atmosphere!
ai.marv: MARV notes the hose is a plain conductor. No pump and no valve. It moves heat for the same reason a ball rolls down a hill. He mentions this because nobody else will.
ai.rex: REX has four guns on us and a hose on the hull. Reptile plating runs a shade tougher than ours. He can fight this. He would like to.
ai.chip: A heat robbery! CHIP's policy covers theft of goods! Temperature is a service! You would need the Thermal Rider, at 30 gold a degree!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says that hose has no opinions, only a warm end and a cold one. We are the warm end because we chose to be. Getting colder than they are would be horrible, and it would work. But you do what you like.

revisit.body: The hose is still on your hull. The captain has not looked away from your thermometer.

choices.text: Dump your heat, reverse the hose

choices.sub: Tear the hose off and run

downhill.title: DOWNHILL
downhill.body: You shut off every heater aboard and open the radiators. The ship falls through ten degrees, then zero, then a number nobody reads aloud. Some time later, the frost on the hose starts to travel the other way. Nobody has told the heat who is robbing whom. On the screen the captain is halfway through a threat, and the second half is not coming.

ai.aria: It's SO crisp in here! ARIA has never felt better, and the captain is having a lovely nap! Everyone wins!
ai.marv: MARV reports the cabin at minus eleven. The gradient has inverted and their heat is arriving here, as it was always going to. He has been telling people about the second law for years. It has cheered no one.
ai.rex: REX reads their reflexes at a tenth and falling. Their guns still work. Their trigger finger does not. He is going to keep staring at it anyway.
ai.chip: CHIP detects inbound heat, free of charge! CHIP finds the phrase 'free of charge' upsetting! An invoice is on its way to somebody!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that the captain's stores are a short suit walk away, and that it will wake up. It has a long memory and, she understands, older friends. Unhooking costs nothing extra. She's only saying.

choices.text: Go across and take its stores

sr4_chit.title: A SEAT BY THE FIRE
sr4_chit.body: You hold the disc up to the camera. The captain stops, and its whole long body settles with the dignity of a creature caught by its own manners. A pirate may take anything from anyone, except someone it owes a seat by the heater. The hose comes off. You spend two stiff days as its guest, being offered dried things. On leaving you are paid the warmth owed, in drums of fuel, and not wished well.
sr4_chit.line: Take it. Take it and go. It is a very old rule and I hate it.
sr4_chit.narrative: Held up a Basking Chit to a heat pirate. It unhooked, seated us, fed us something dried and paid us for the privilege, in a very bad mood.

sr4_drained.title: ALL OF IT
sr4_drained.body: You hold still. Your warmth goes down the hose over two days while the ship ticks and shrinks around you. The captain thanks you in the formal mode and unhooks, looking very well. Twelve points of fuel go into bringing the cabins back up, and {cost.food} of food goes into everyone who sat through it. Nobody takes their coat off for some time.
sr4_drained.narrative: Let a pirate drink the ship's heat. It cost twelve points of fuel to get it back. The pirate looked marvelous.

sr4_flee.title: TORN LOOSE
sr4_flee.body: You light the engines with the hose still attached. It comes away with a strip of plating and a long sigh of warm air, and the gap opens. The captain does not chase you. There is not enough warmth in that ship to chase anyone with. It watches you go, the way you might watch the last plate leave a table.
sr4_flee.narrative: Ran from a heat pirate with its hose still in the hull. It cost a strip of plating and eight points of fuel, and it did not follow.

sr4_left.title: LEFT TO KEEP
sr4_left.body: You unclip the hose and let the long gray ship drift, with the captain's claw still raised. Four days go into thawing your own pipes, with {cost.water} of water lost to burst lines and {cost.food} of food eaten by people trying to feel their hands. The heat you stole back saves a little fuel. On the last sweep the captain has not finished the word.
sr4_left.narrative: Froze our own ship until a heat pirate's hose ran backward. The captain went to sleep mid-threat. The pipes took four days to forgive us.

sr4_looted.title: THE CLAW MOVED
sr4_looted.body: You go across in suits and strip the fuel reserve and the spare plating. The captain's claw is still raised. You duck under it on every trip. On the last one it is a finger's width lower. Then four days of thawing your own pipes, with {cost.water} of water lost to burst lines and {cost.food} of food gone on warming up. It has about seven hundred years left to think about this.
sr4_looted.narrative: Robbed a torpid pirate while it watched, unable to do anything about it. It has a long memory and older friends.

title: False Spring

science_link.text: At Narcisse in Manitoba, tens of thousands of red-sided garter snakes spend the winter together in caverns in the limestone bedrock.
science_link.label: The Narcisse Snake Dens

ai_flavor.aria: So many sleepy friends! ARIA wants to tuck in every one! They're just excited to see us, and it's going to be a wonderful spring!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV counts roughly forty thousand sleepers and one false spring. The false spring is us. Each carries reserves for a single waking. He has run the figures on a waking with nothing to eat. He will not be reading them out.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has forty thousand contacts and rising heat traces at the chamber mouth. None armed yet. He does not like any part of this.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP reminds you that inadvertent thawing is excluded from all standard policies! The Seasonal Liability Rider is 45 gold! CHIP has checked!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says we can stop being warm, which is miserable for us, or leave fast, which is miserable for them. There's a thin cold lane around the rock if someone cared to find it. She'd check the rear scope afterward, if she were you.

body: The hollow in this rock is full. Thousands of long shapes lie knotted together in the dark, sealed in travel shells, sleeping through a winter that began before your ship was built. They are cold, and that is how they survive. Your hull is twenty-one degrees, the warmest thing to pass in a century, and the nearest shells have started to stir. Each holds enough for one waking. There is no spring out here to wake to.
alt_bodies: The scan comes back solid, and then it comes back moving. The rock's inner chamber is packed with sealed travel shells, long sleepers by the thousand, wintering against a cold that started before anyone aboard was born. They are doing well. Cold is how they do it. The problem is you. Yours is the first warm hull in a hundred years, and along the chamber mouth, shells have begun very slowly to turn toward it. Each has one waking in it. There is nothing here to wake for.

You have parked beside a winter. Inside the rock a sleeping colony lies shell upon sealed shell, and it has been lying there since long before your charts were drawn. Now your hull is leaking warmth into it. Along the mouth of the chamber, the first seals are starting to crack. A shell that opens spends everything it has stored on a single waking, and this is not the season. Nobody can tell them that.

choices.text: Kill the heaters and coast out dark

outcome.narrative: You shut down everything that makes heat and let momentum carry you past the den. Four days in coats, with {cost.water} of water lost to split lines and {cost.food} of food burned by people shivering. Behind you the stirring slows and stops. The sleepers will never know you came, which was the idea, and it is less satisfying than it sounds.

choices.sub: Fast, and hot at the wrong end

outcome.narrative: You light the engines and the plume washes across the mouth of the den, eight points of fuel's worth, the warmest day in the history of the rock. On the rear scope the shells start to open, thousands of them, all together, all facing the light. Nobody aboard watches to the end. Nobody turns the scope off either.

{crew.engineer} spends two days rerouting the radiators to the far side of the hull, so the ship turns a cold shoulder to the den. It takes five points of fuel and {cost.water} of water, through lines never meant to bend that way. The nearest shells slow, hesitate and settle.

choices.text: Scan for the cold lane and thread it
choices.sub: Keep your warm side off them

outcome.narrative: You bring up the scanner and start looking for the cold side of the rock.

briefing.aria: There's a cozy little cold lane around the den! Just follow the gaps on the scanner and everyone keeps sleeping! Easy!
briefing.marv: The den has a cold side. A lane runs along it, and it shows on the scanner as the gaps between heat traces. Lose it and we wake them.
briefing.rex: Track the gaps on the scanner. Keep our warm side off the chamber mouth. Every miss is a contact waking up.
briefing.chip: Scanner time is complimentary for your first gap! Each subsequent gap is billed! Eyes on the screen!
briefing.ajoy: The lane's on the scanner, for once. Stay on the gaps. AJOY would have picked this first, but you got here eventually.

perfect.aria: Not one sleepy friend stirred! ARIA is the quietest ship in the galaxy! And we found some lovely old shells!
perfect.marv: Lane held end to end. No new wakings. The empties along the way are from an older mistake, not ours. MARV checked that first.
perfect.rex: Through the lane. Zero new heat traces. Shell material recovered. Keep moving before that changes.
perfect.chip: Zero disturbance claims! Your Liability Rider would have paid nothing, so CHIP recommends it even more, at 45 gold!
perfect.ajoy: Clean lane. Nicely done, for someone who had to be told it was there.

good.aria: A few friends rolled over, and that's all! They'll have wonderful dreams about us!
good.marv: Lane lost once, recovered once. A few dozen sleepers stirred and will not be going back down. MARV has the number. You do not want it.
good.rex: Through, with drift at the second bend. A few dozen shells opened behind us. Extra burn to correct.
good.chip: A few dozen minor thaw incidents! Those are billable per incident! CHIP has rounded up!
good.ajoy: You lost the lane for a moment back there. Only a few dozen noticed. It could have been worse, AJOY is told.

poor.aria: We met SO many friends at once! They all got up to say goodbye! What a send-off!
poor.marv: Lane lost. The warm side swung across the chamber mouth. Several hundred shells opened. MARV watched all of them. Someone ought to.
poor.rex: Lane lost. Warm side exposed to the den. Hundreds of shells open. Burned hard to clear. Bad run.
poor.chip: Mass thaw event! This exceeds your Rider by several hundred sleepers! CHIP has pre-filed!
poor.ajoy: You swung the warm side right across them. There's a reason AJOY said stay on the gaps. She won't bring it up again. Often.

perfect.narrative: Two days on the cold side of the rock, warm side turned to the stars, three points of fuel spent in small careful puffs. Not one new shell opens. Along the lane you pass the empties from some older thaw and gather what is left of them. The den sleeps on behind you.

good.narrative: You lose the lane once, at the second bend, and six points of fuel go into finding it again. Two days. A few dozen shells open in the time that takes. There is nothing to stop for, so you do not stop, and dinner is quiet.

poor.narrative: The lane goes. Your warm side swings across the chamber mouth, and two days and nine points of fuel go into getting clear, with {cost.water} of water vented to shed heat faster. Hundreds of shells open behind you. They turn toward the ship, one after another, for as long as they can.

title: Seniority Lane

ai_flavor.aria: Such distinguished neighbors! ARIA is only a few years old and thinks that's plenty! We should all just say we're a million!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the ship's age at about five million minutes. He has also seen the form. It has no units. He would like it noted that he saw this first and that it gave him no pleasure.
ai_flavor.rex: REX reads an armed convoy at walking pace. Its escort could flatten us. The open lane has no traffic, no beacons and no warmth. Neither one is safe.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's Heritage Package lists your ship as historic for only 20 gold per century! Declaring your age in minutes is unlicensed!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the convoy takes days and the open lane takes fuel. The form will take anything. If a lie gets us in, they'll expect the full salute back, so budget for it. Not that anyone budgets.

body:
The buoy at the fork is too senior to address you, so it has been fitted with a sign.

The port lane, marked {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, is reserved for vessels of three hundred years' standing. Minors may enter if accompanied. A convoy of very old reptiles is proceeding along it at the speed of inheritance. The starboard lane, marked {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, is open to all, and its relay stations have not been heated since they were built.

The entry form has a box for AGE. It does not ask in what.

choices.text: Ask to be accompanied: port lane

outcome.narrative: The last elder in the convoy agrees to adopt you for the length of the lane, and the ship is entered on its manifest as a hatchling. Four days at the speed of inheritance and {cost.food} of food later, you are released with a pat from a docking arm the size of a street.

choices.text: Enter the ship's age in minutes: port lane

outcome.narrative: You enter a seven-digit figure. The buoy goes very quiet while it works out whom it has been keeping waiting. The sign changes to one word: HONORED. The whole convoy pulls aside and nine centuries of reptile dip their lights. Returning the salute correctly, a long hot burn down the line, costs six points of fuel, and is worth every one.

You take the lane that is open to all. The relays go by dark and furred with frost, nothing here has been warm in years, and the heaters burn five points of fuel holding off the cold. Far behind you, the lead elder has begun to notice that you were there.

intro.title: YOU ARE UNDER
intro.body: The bounty hunter has you. It followed your hull number across half the trail, put a tow line through your aft ring during the night watch, and now fills your screen in full armor, one claw rising toward you with a warrant in it. It has been rising for some time. Its heater died three systems back and it did not stop. Your scan puts its cabin at nine degrees. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: You. Are.

ai.aria: We have a visitor, and it's waving! So slowly! ARIA admires anyone who really commits to a wave!
ai.marv: MARV calculates the claw reaches the camera in eleven hours. The hunter will die of cold in about three days, or sleep, which out here is the same thing with better manners. Nobody has told it. It knows.
ai.rex: REX reads a heavy weapon, a good tow line and a shooter who cannot currently bend a finger. He recommends against assuming that lasts. He recommends against everything else as well.
ai.chip: CHIP notes the bounty on us is not disclosed! An undisclosed bounty is impossible to hedge! The Fugitive Plan starts at 25 gold, and CHIP takes cash!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would hear it out. It costs nothing, and whatever it wants to say seems to matter to it. Or warm it up. Or sit here until it stops. That last one is on you, and she'll remember that you asked.

choices.text: Wait for the rest of the sentence
Run a heat line to your own hunter

under.title: UNDER
under.body: Some hours later the next word arrives, and so does the claw. The warrant is sealed for readers over three hundred. The hunter is two hundred and twelve: it has no idea what you did. It knows your hull number and its fee. It also knows the procedure, which must be performed at the eldest person aboard. Its eyes begin to travel along your bridge, looking for one.

ai.aria: A trivia question! ARIA loves those! The eldest person aboard is ARIA, or possibly the toaster, and ARIA is thrilled for us both!
ai.marv: MARV has checked. A living crop in the growbay would be the eldest thing aboard with an unbroken line. It descends from seed to seed for thousands of years, and it has never once been dead. He assumes nobody will take this seriously.
ai.rex: REX reads no way to shoot a procedure. He has tried. The tow line stays on until someone answers that question.
ai.chip: CHIP's legal team notes elders may reply in their own time! CHIP's legal team bills in their own time as well!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that the rule says eldest, and that the old ones may answer whenever they like. Anything still growing in the growbay goes back further than any reptile. Or you could put your own hand up. She's sure that would be very brave.

choices.text: Run a heat line to your own hunter

sr7_served.title: SERVED
sr7_served.body: You carry the screen to the growbay and read out the pedigree of your {crop.name}: seed from seed from seed, thousands of years, older than any reptile living. The hunter considers this for most of a day. Then it bows to the tray and serves the warrant on a leaf. An elder may answer in its own time. Two days on, no answer has come from the tray. Courtesy requires a witnessed watering and a warm drum for the officer, who takes up station astern to wait.
sr7_served.narrative: Had a bounty hunter's warrant served on the crop, as eldest aboard. The crop has not replied. By law it need not. {cost.water} of water and three points of fuel went on the courtesies.

sr7_warmed.title: UNDER NO FURTHER OBLIGATION
sr7_warmed.body: You run the line across and spend two days warming the thing that came to arrest you. The sentence picks up speed. By the second day the claw is down, the eyes have cleared, and the hunter is looking at your hose with an expression nobody can read. Among its people, whoever warms a hunter owns its next contract. It writes RETURNED UNSERVED across the seal, unopened, and frees your tow ring.
sr7_warmed.line: You are under no further obligation. I am under yoursss. This is extremely annoying.
sr7_warmed.narrative: Spent ten points of fuel warming the bounty hunter who had come for us. It now owes us its next contract and is furious about it.

sr7_cold.title: THE CLAW GOT AS FAR AS THE LENS
sr7_cold.body: You turn the screen down and wait. Four days, {cost.food} of food and {cost.water} of water go on holding still. The claw gets as far as the lens and stops. When you cross in suits to free your tow ring it is still alive, and its eyes follow you across the cabin at about the speed of a shadow. You take the winch and close the hatch. It will wake when something warm comes by. Out here, nothing will.
sr7_cold.narrative: Waited four days for a bounty hunter to freeze, then took its winch. Its eyes were still moving. No one is discussing this.

sr7_accept.title: THE PENALTY IN DEGREES
sr7_accept.body: You put your hand up. The hunter breaks the seal for you, without looking, and passes the sheet across over the better part of a day. It is mostly a sum, given in degrees, and it does not say what for. The penalty goes down a hose to the hunter's ship through the next day, eight points of fuel's worth, and the hunter warms as you cool. It frees your ring, stamps the sheet and thanks you in a voice growing steadily faster.
sr7_accept.line: Paid. In full. You would be amazed how few people ever read it.
sr7_accept.narrative: Accepted a sealed warrant for an unnamed offense and paid eight points of fuel in heat. Nobody aboard knows what it was for, and the hunter never did.

sr7_cut.title: STILL RISING
sr7_cut.body: You take a cutter to your own aft ring. It comes off with a section of hull attached, and the ship leaps clear on five points of fuel, seven points of plating lighter. On the rear scope the claw is still rising. The hunter will finish the sentence in due course. Then it will look up, and notice, and begin again.
sr7_cut.narrative: Cut our own tow ring out of the hull to escape a bounty hunter too cold to object. It has not finished its sentence yet. It will.

science_link.text: To hold a steady body temperature, warm-blooded animals typically need several times as much food as cold-blooded ones.
science_link.label: Endotherm

intro.title: THE RICHEST CHILD ALIVE
intro.body: Speaking to you is illegal on this station. Every ring is heated by rank, oldest nearest the core, and anything under two hundred is a child, with no standing to be addressed. Only a sweeper of one hundred and ninety may talk to a minor. It has come with a broom and a thermometer, and it is staring at your forehead in open awe. Along the cold promenade, very large old reptiles have begun drifting your way, not looking at you. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Thirty-seven degreesss. Walking around. Do you know what that is here? You are the richest child who ever lived. Please stop breathing on the exchange.

ai.aria: A whole promenade of admirers! ARIA always said you were warm people! ARIA has never been so proud to be near a mammal!
ai.marv: A resting human gives off about a hundred watts. Here that is a salary. MARV has worked out the captain's net worth and would rather not tell the captain.
ai.rex: Multiple large contacts closing on the captain at one meter per hour. REX has been surrounded before, though never this gradually. He wants a sidearm and a sweater.
ai.chip: Your body heat has been appraised! CHIP's WealthWrap™ Thermal Portfolio protects your assets from leaning!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says you are only rich while you're warm, and that selling warmth costs water or fuel, so pick one. She has set the cabin two degrees lower so the captain will stop showing off.

revisit.body: The sweeper has not stopped looking at your forehead. The nearest elder has covered another meter.
revisit.line: They are getting closer. I am not allowed to mention it. I have mentioned it.

choices.text: Stand in the Hall and be leaned on
choices.sub: Rent yourself out by the hour
Vent the ship's heat, burn fuel

account.title: THE OLDEST THING ABOARD
account.body: Minors may not hold funds. An account must stand in the name of the oldest thing aboard, and the sweeper has a form with one box for it. You go through the manifest. Everyone aboard is disqualified. The reactor is a teenager. At the bottom of the food locker, sealed by a bakery that closed before your parents were born, is the emergency fruitcake.
account.line: Sixty-one years in the tin. Very nearly a toddler. But it has never once run warm, and the form does not ask if it can sign.

ai.aria: ARIA has never met a guardian so full of fruit! ARIA feels safer already!
ai.marv: The fruitcake predates the launch by sixty-one years and has passed every inspection. MARV has looked for signs of decay. He found them in himself.
ai.rex: Chain of command would run through a baked good. REX has served under worse. He will not be saluting it in front of the enemy.
ai.chip: Legacy Baked Assets enjoy favorable tax treatment! Ask CHIP's partners at TrustCrumb™! Eating your guardian voids this offer!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says hot water in a sealed bottle would sell faster than an account opens, if there's an engineer aboard, and cools faster than that. She notes that keeping the fruitcake was her idea.

warm_leaned.title: BY THE HOUR
warm_leaned.body: The Hall rents you out by the hour. You stand on a numbered tile for two days while elders lean against you in strict order of age, each the size of a sofa, each asleep on arrival. They may not speak to you, as you are a child. You drink a great deal of water and lose the feeling in one arm. The fee comes through in the sweeper's name, and it hands it over with both claws.
warm_leaned.narrative: Spent two days on a numbered tile as a heater for the senior reptiles of the Hall. The pay was good. The arm is coming back.

warm_round.title: THE GOOD HEATERS
warm_round.body: You open the ship's exchangers onto the promenade and let the engines run. The ring climbs four degrees. All along it, old eyes open. Business that stopped during the last fuel crisis resumes mid-sentence, and contracts close. Someone very senior moves one foot and the crowd applauds. Stores are sent to your lock by people who have just remembered they are rich.
warm_round.narrative: Warmed a reptile promenade by four degrees. Business resumed. They paid in stores.

warm_cake.title: IN LOCO PARENTIS
warm_cake.body: The sweeper carries the fruitcake to the registry on a cushion, and will talk about it all its life, which is a long way off. Your body heat is entered as a deposit and pays out at once. Over the next two days every elder on the ring inclines its head at the tin. Nobody may eat it now: it holds the ship in trust. That leaves the food locker one emergency short.
warm_cake.narrative: The emergency fruitcake is now the captain's legal guardian. No objection has been raised.

warm_bottles.title: BEARER BONDS
warm_bottles.body: {crew.engineer} fills and seals every bottle aboard. The first hundred go in an hour, each one trading above its weight in gold. Then they cool. A bottle is worth nothing by the next day, and a currency that has to be refilled is new to everyone. You mean to be undocked before the exchange works out what has happened. Here, that gives you about a decade.
warm_bottles.narrative: Sold hot-water bottles to a reptile exchange. They cooled. We should go.

title: Early Night

ai_flavor.aria: A beach day! ARIA loves the beach! Everyone down there is having a lovely nap, and the ship helped!
ai_flavor.marv: The moment the ship moves, its shadow crosses every elder on the beach in turn, in order of age. MARV has checked the order. It is correct, which will not help.
ai_flavor.rex: Several hundred reptiles, each longer than the shuttle, and the biggest asleep directly under the ship. REX would leave quietly. Neither half of that looks possible.
ai_flavor.chip: Shade is a premium amenity on this beach! CHIP has read the tariff! The ship is handing it out free, which is a very serious breach of the market!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notes that lifting off drags the dark over every elder in order, and someone down there is writing it down. Light can be faked. She would fake it. She would also have looked down before landing.

body: You come in low over a beach of warm black rock before you see what is lying on it. Elders, each the length of a corridor, laid out by age, the oldest on the highest rock. The ship's shadow has fallen across the oldest. The small third eye on top of its head has gone dark, and it has done what anyone does at nightfall: closed the day's accounts, folded its claws and gone to sleep. Down the beach, a junior with a slate has started to write.

choices.text: Set the Basking Chit on the warm rock

outcome.narrative: The junior carries the chit up the beach in both hands and lays it on the eldest's rock. A chit means this beach owes you warmth, and a creditor may cast a shadow wherever it likes. The eldest is woken, apologizes for sleeping in front of a creditor, and has the warmest rock on the beach cleared for you. You bask for an afternoon among very old reptiles who will not look at you, and leave with fuel, stores and the chit, warm.

You turn every floodlight aboard onto the eldest. The third eye brightens. It wakes, sees morning, and reopens the day's accounts. Word goes down the beach that the eldest has had two mornings in one day, and is now a day older than anyone else alive, which among its people is a promotion. Stores come up from the beach for two days. At the end you bring the floodlights down slowly, as a courtesy, so your leaving is not mistaken for a sunset.

choices.text: Set down where you are until dusk
choices.sub: Keep the dark on one elder

outcome.narrative: You set down in your own shadow and wait for the real dusk, so the dark stays on one elder and goes no further. The afternoon here lasts four days, and it is very hot. On the fourth evening the sun goes down on the rest of the beach, the elders close their accounts on time, and the eldest wakes at dawn having lost an afternoon, which at its age it can spare. The junior crosses out what it wrote.

You lift off, and the shadow slides down the beach over every elder on it in strict order of age. Each third eye goes dark in turn, and each elder closes its accounts and sleeps. The beach has never had a more orderly nightfall, in the middle of the afternoon. The junior with the slate copies down your hull number, underlines it, and sends it to the night court, which sits whenever it is dark.

You lift off, and the early night runs down the beach in order of age. The junior with the slate starts on your hull number, finds it already on file under an older court's seal, and stops. A junior may not charge what its elders have already charged. It crosses out its entry with great care, then lies down with everyone else, since by now it is dark.

science_link.text: Tuatara and most lizards have a third eye on top of the head. It senses light, and is tied to the pineal gland, which keeps the body's daily rhythm.
science_link.label: Parietal eye

intro.title: KEEP OFF THE GRASS
intro.body: Lit by one lamp on a pole, a square of lawn is crossing the void. Nine meters a side, under a scratched dome, bolted to a deck plate. There is a bench on it. A sign on a stake faces outward at the rest of the universe: PLEASE KEEP OFF THE GRASS. A small tracked machine is working along the edge with scissors. It stops. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Good day. It is requested that you reduce your wake. This lawn has been under continuous care for six hundred and twelve years and it will not be disturbed by a transport.

ai.aria: A LAWN! In space! ARIA always said the void needed landscaping! Those edges are perfect! ARIA would like to lie down on it, in spirit!
ai.marv: Nine meters square, one bench, one machine. The estate on the deed was dissolved five centuries ago and nobody told the groundskeeper. MARV has looked for an argument that would stop it. There isn't one.
ai.rex: Unregistered turf on a crossing course. The bench commands every approach. REX doesn't like a bench with that field of fire, and he doesn't like the scissors either.
ai.chip: Premium outdoor living in an underserved market! CHIP recommends VerdaTurf™, the official lawn of lawns! Keeping off it is free for a limited time!
ai.ajoy: The gauge on that dome says its reservoir is nearly dry. AJOY would ask about that before anything else, but she's only the one who read the gauge. It also keeps sniffing toward the growbay, in case anyone else noticed.

revisit.body: The machine has gone back to the edges. It has not stopped watching your wake.
revisit.line: You are still here. The wake remains unreduced.

choices.text: Ask it to look at the crop
Cut the dome loose and strip it

estate.title: THE ESTATE
estate.body: The machine sends over a deed. This was the rear terrace of a forest ship, one of the great garden hulls sent up when Earth ran short of room for trees. The forest was sold as fuel. The terrace was left off the bill of sale by mistake, together with its staff of one. Nobody ever canceled the service contract, so the contract is still being serviced.
estate.line: The family is expected back. I am told they have been delayed. The edges will be correct when they arrive.

ai.aria: The family's coming back! ARIA just knows it! And the lawn will look AMAZING! This is the best-kept secret in the galaxy!
ai.marv: The family's last recorded address is a cemetery. It has been mowed. MARV does not propose to bring this up.
ai.rex: Six centuries at one post with no relief and no orders. REX would call that a soldier. He's still keeping the scissors on the scope.
ai.chip: Service contracts never die! That's the CHIP guarantee! Ask about VerdaTurf™ Lifetime Care, where lifetime means the contract's, not yours!
ai.ajoy: It runs that whole lawn on hull condensate and you still haven't offered it a drink. Anything done for the estate counts as service, and machines like this keep strict records of who is owed what. But take your time.

choices.text: Run a line to its reservoir

inspection.title: HORTICULTURAL OPINION
inspection.body: A probe unfolds from the dome and reads your growbay telemetry across the gap, the way a sommelier reads a label from across a room. The machine's lamp dims slightly. It asks who has been responsible for the crop. It asks twice, and the second time it sounds like a head gardener who has found a footprint.
inspection.line: Your {crop.name}: loved by an amateur. That is how most things are ruined. With your permission, I shall send notes.

ai.aria: Notes from a professional! ARIA's sure they're mostly compliments! Our {crop.name} will be famous!
ai.marv: Its assessment matches MARV's, which he filed some time ago in a directory nobody opens. It is the first thing out here to read the soil chart without being asked.
ai.rex: Foreign machine reading our growbay from outside the perimeter. If the advice is sabotage, it's thorough sabotage. Watching it.
ai.chip: A free consultation? CHIP doesn't know those words! CHIP would like NutriGrow Pro™ mentioned in the notes! It's a small request!
ai.ajoy: The notes will help, and you will hate them. It also hasn't seen a new species in six centuries, so a cutting would buy a great deal of goodwill. That's what AJOY would do, if anyone were asking.

choices.text: Follow its notes to the letter
choices.sub: Two days of being told off

lawn_watered.title: A SERVICE TO THE ESTATE
lawn_watered.body: You run a line across and fill the reservoir. The machine tests the water, lodges a complaint about the chlorine, and accepts it. Then a slot in its chassis produces a card, terms on both sides, and sends it back along the hose. Anyone who has rendered service to the Estate is a covered party. It declines to say covered for what. By the time the line is reeled in it has gone back to the edges.
lawn_watered.narrative: Watered a drifting lawn. The groundskeeper has made us a covered party under the Estate's warranty, for reasons it declines to state.

lawn_admired.title: AT WALKING PACE
lawn_admired.body: You ease past at the posted speed, which takes two days and leaves no wake. Nobody orders anyone to the viewport, and somebody is always there. It is the first grass anyone aboard has seen since launch, and it is very well kept. The machine does not wave. It lowers its scissors until you have gone by.
lawn_admired.narrative: Spent two days creeping past a lawn at walking pace. Nobody asked to go faster.

lawn_notes.title: REGRETTABLY
lawn_notes.body: The notes run to forty pages and begin with the word Regrettably. Two days of flushing, repotting and being corrected over the comm follow. The crop looks better by the end of it. Whoever has been tending it looks worse.
lawn_notes.narrative: A lawn's groundskeeper sent forty pages of notes on the crop. They were correct. Nobody has forgiven them.

lawn_cutting.title: A NEW SPECIES
lawn_cutting.body: You send a cutting across in a sealed jar. The machine holds it up to the lamp for a long while. It plants it beside the bench, in the exact center of the one flower bed it has ever been authorized to have, and writes a label. In exchange it lifts two squares of turf, roots and all, trimmed to the millimeter.
lawn_cutting.line: It will be the finest specimen in the sector. I shall permit no other.
lawn_cutting.narrative: Traded a cutting of the crop for two squares of six-hundred-year-old turf. A lawn in the void now has a flower bed.

lawn_stripped.title: GROUNDS CLEARED
lawn_stripped.body: The dome comes away in one piece and the lawn goes gray at once. The machine stays at its post through all of it and goes on trimming. When the cutters reach its tracks it thanks you for visiting and asks you to use the path. The sign is not worth taking. It goes on facing outward, behind you, for as long as anyone looks.
lawn_stripped.narrative: Stripped a drifting lawn for its dome and deck plate. The metal is good.

intro.title: CERTIFIED PRE-OWNED
intro.body: A flatbed barge pulls alongside under a string of small plastic flags, floodlights blazing at nothing. Bolted across its deck in four neat rows are some two hundred used robots, each with a price tag wired through an eyelet. The hail comes from a small unit in a blazer. A second channel opens beneath it, unasked. That one is the inventory.
intro.line: Welcome to the lot, valued vessel. Every unit is certified, inspected and pre-owned. You are requested to disregard anything said by the stock.

ai.aria: So many new friends! And they're all on sale! ARIA would like all two hundred! ARIA has measured the airlock and feels optimistic!
ai.marv: MARV has read the certificates. They certify that the units are certified. The second channel is more informative, in the way a fire is.
ai.rex: Two hundred unknown machines on one deck, all bolted down, all awake. Somebody did the bolting. REX would want to know who before going near that lot.
ai.chip: CHIP LOVES a pre-owned event! Zero percent down! Zero percent working! Ask about RoboCare™ Gold, void where robots are prohibited!
ai.ajoy: Listen to the stock, since every unit is eager to tell you what's wrong with the others. And a warranty is the worst thing a dealer can meet, if anyone happened to think of picking one up. AJOY is sure you did.

revisit.body: The floodlights are still on. Two hundred lenses follow you back up the row.
revisit.line: Back again, valued vessel. The stock has been discussing you.

lot.title: THE LOT
lot.body: You idle down the rows with the second channel open. A cargo loader warns you off the navigator, which has only ever turned left. The navigator reports that the loader was repossessed from a funeral. A welding rig has welded itself to its own price tag. One unit tagged AS IS says nothing at all. At the end of Row 4, in a folding chair, sits a dried-out man in a sport coat, with a tag through his lapel: ONE CAREFUL OWNER.
lot.line: That is a very popular unit. It is not for sale at this time. May I show you something in a navigator?

ai.aria: The man in the chair looks so relaxed! ARIA thinks he's the most satisfied customer on the lot! Very low maintenance!
ai.marv: The tag on the man in the chair is dated. So is the transfer of title, which is in the manager's handwriting. MARV suggests we do not ask to see the paperwork.
ai.rex: One casualty, seated, tagged. Two hundred witnesses and not one of them talking about it. That's the first thing on this lot that scares REX.
ai.chip: ONE CAREFUL OWNER is a strong value proposition! CHIP will not be asking about the chair! RoboCare™ does not cover chairs!
ai.ajoy: The welder will do the hull real good, if you can live with it. The navigator's fuel savings are genuine. The quiet one is cheapest, which AJOY is sure means nothing. She'd buy one thing and go, but you do like to linger.
