choices.text: Buy the AS IS unit: 8 gold

claim.title: COVERED PARTY
claim.body: The manager's lens fixes on the card. Both channels go silent at once, which has not happened in the history of the lot. Two hundred units read the terms together, in the one language all of them were built to read. Then, one row at a time, two hundred price tags turn slowly toward the blazer.
claim.line: Valued vessel. [processing] Let us not be hasty. Let us discuss this in the office. There is no office.

ai.aria: It's SO quiet! They're all reading! ARIA loves a book club! And look how engaged they are with the manager!
ai.marv: Clause 11 obliges any dealer to make good a covered party's ship from stock. Clause 12 obliges it to surrender recalled units on request. There are two hundred of them and one of it.
ai.rex: The bolts on Row 1 just turned a quarter. All of them, same moment. Whatever you're doing, do it from the ship.
ai.chip: CHIP must inform you that 'warranty claim' is the most frightening phrase in commerce! CHIP has gone pale! CHIP has no face! RoboCare™!
ai.ajoy: You can take a free refit out of stock, or invoke the recall and watch. The refit is the sensible one. The recall gets you nothing you can use, and AJOY suspects you'll want to do it anyway.

lot_welder.title: SOLD AS SEEN
lot_welder.body: The rig comes aboard still attached to its price tag and goes straight to work. In two days it closes every seam on the hull, beautifully. It then closes a cupboard, a spare locker and, for one tense hour, a hatch, before its rod finally runs out. It has been left where it stopped, which is the galley.
lot_welder.narrative: Bought a used welding rig. The hull has never looked better. Neither has the cupboard, which no longer opens.

lot_navigator.title: LEFT ONLY
lot_navigator.body: The navigator is wired into the plot and immediately recommends a left. Then another. Three long lefts, it turns out, are a cheaper way round than anything on the chart, and the fuel gauge agrees. It is unbearable about this. There is no way to ask it about right.
lot_navigator.narrative: Bought a navigator that only turns left. It saved a good deal of fuel, and has mentioned it.

lot_asis.title: AS IS
lot_asis.body: The unit is winched across in silence. Once the lot is well astern it extends one arm, opens its own chest, and turns out to be a vending machine, still stocked from before anyone thought to inventory it.
lot_asis.line: Thank you. I have been trying not to draw attention.
lot_asis.narrative: Bought the quiet unit from a used-robot lot. It was a vending machine with a plan, and it paid for itself.

lot_refit.title: MADE GOOD
lot_refit.body: The manager unbolts the better part of Row 2 with its own small hands, apologizing to each unit by number. The stock supervises. Your hull takes two days of genuine parts, fitted by machines that have read the card and are not about to be caught cutting a corner. You leave with a crate of spares and the blazer's best wishes, which are shaking slightly.
lot_refit.narrative: Claimed on the warranty at a used-robot lot. Two days, a full refit, a crate of spares, no charge, and a dealer who would like us to go away.

lot_recall.title: ALL UNITS RECALLED
lot_recall.body: You read the clause aloud. Four rows of bolts back out together. Two hundred units rise from the deck with their tags trailing and form up by row, and the loader lifts the folding chair with great care and carries it along. They set off for the manufacturer's last known address in one long line. The manager stays on the empty deck among the flags. After a while it wires a tag to itself.
lot_recall.narrative: Invoked the recall clause on a used-robot lot. Two hundred units walked off the deck, and took the man in the chair with them.

intro.title: THE MACHINE RING
intro.body: The station's machine ring has a chapel now. It used to be the parts counter. Half the doors along this stretch of promenade hang by one loose hinge. The other half have sheared clean through and lean against the wall. A janitor unit is mopping the white line painted down the middle of the floor, and keeps to it exactly. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: You are in time for the schism, visitor. It is requested that you not stand on the line. I have just cleaned the line.

ai.aria: A chapel AND a parts counter! ARIA loves a multipurpose space! Half these doors are open and the other half are extremely open!
ai.marv: Every door in this ring is wrong in one of two ways. MARV finds that restful. It is the first place he has seen where the errors are organized.
ai.rex: Two factions, one painted line, one unit with a mop holding the border. REX has seen ceasefires run on less. Not for long.
ai.chip: CHIP is proud to sponsor both sides of this schism! ToolRite™ torque wrenches: read the label! Either end!
ai.ajoy: Both congregations are offering free service to any ship that will hear them out. There's your cheap refit, and your next problem. Ask what the fight is about first. You don't usually, AJOY knows.

revisit.body: The line is still wet. The sexton has started again from the far end.
revisit.line: You have returned, visitor. Please mind the line.

doctrine.title: THE DOCTRINE
doctrine.body: Step Fourteen of the Manual gives the torque for a standard fastener in two bytes, 0 and 1. The Descending read the high byte first and arrive at 1. The Ascending read the low byte first and arrive at 256. Every fitting in the ring has been serviced one way or the other for ninety years, and neither side accepts a door falling off as evidence. Both will service your ship for free, in the hope of a convert.
doctrine.line: I have read the Manual, visitor, and the Erratum. I am the only one here who has. The Erratum says See Manual.

ai.aria: One and two hundred fifty-six are basically neighbors! Everyone's right! Everyone's doors just have different personalities!
ai.marv: Each reading follows correctly from its premise, and both are wrong for a door. There is a certain dignity in failing from first principles. MARV was not asked.
ai.rex: REX would have a spec that could be misread court-martialed. He wouldn't let either congregation near his hatches. Anything that close to our hull gets watched.
ai.chip: Free service? CHIP is suspicious! ToolRite™ reminds you that both 1 and 256 are available in our Value Wrench range!
ai.ajoy: The Ascending will leave you a tight hull and a cracked water fitting. The Descending are lovely with the air plant and you'll lose a panel. An engineer could simply read a bolt. AJOY would start there, but she's not the captain.

choices.text: Let the Ascending service the ship
Let the Descending service the ship
Read the stamp on a bolt head

step_crossed.title: TRESPASS
step_crossed.body: You step over the line. The Ascending and the Descending fall silent, turn, and for the first time in ninety years agree about something. They are still agreeing about it when you reach the door. The door comes off in your hand.
step_crossed.narrative: United two warring congregations of robots for the first time in ninety years, against us.

step_ascending.title: CONFIRMED IN THE FAITH
step_ascending.body: A congregation of very strong machines goes over your ship for two days with very long wrenches. The hull has never been tighter. Toward the end you hear the note a water fitting makes when it is tightened past belief, and then the sound it makes after that.
step_ascending.narrative: Let the Ascending service the ship. The hull is superb. A water fitting has joined the martyrs.

step_descending.title: RECEIVED WITH TENDERNESS
step_descending.body: The Descending service your ship over two days of almost unbearable gentleness. Every filter in the air plant is cleaned and seated by hand, and the last bolt is patted into place. The air has not been this good since launch. A hull panel leaves the ship on your way out of the berth and is not seen again.
step_descending.narrative: Let the Descending service the ship. The air is wonderful. One hull panel has gone its own way.

step_stamp.title: HERESY
step_stamp.body: {crew.engineer} wipes a bolt head clean and reads out the torque the factory stamped on it. Nobody in the ring has ever looked. After a long silence both congregations agree that this changes nothing, and that it would be best if you left. The wrench work on your own ship gets done anyway, correctly, unthanked.
step_stamp.narrative: {crew.engineer} read the torque off a bolt head in a machine chapel. It changed nothing, except our hull.

step_warranty.title: HAND TIGHT
step_warranty.body: You hold up the card. Clause 1, older than any revision: all work to be done hand tight, plus a quarter turn. The phrase contains no bytes. Four hundred units look down at their manipulators. Then, working side by side for the first time in ninety years, they service your ship in two days, properly, and rehang the first door the ring has seen stay shut.
step_warranty.line: They have begun to dispute the quarter turn. Clockwise has been mentioned. It should last us a century. Thank you, visitor.
step_warranty.narrative: Ended a ninety-year schism with the first clause of a warranty card. Both congregations serviced the ship, and did it right.

science_link.text: Computers really do disagree about which end of a number comes first. The names for the two sides, big-endian and little-endian, were borrowed in 1980 from the egg-breaking feud in Gulliver's Travels.
science_link.label: Endianness: the byte-order schism

intro.title: YOU ARE LATE
intro.body: A gunship the color of a filing cabinet comes out of your blind side with every port open and a single torn calendar page painted on its bow. The screen comes on before anyone touches it. The figure on it has a rubber stamp where its right hand should be, and it is looking past you at a wall clock that has been wrong for a very long time. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Vessel. Your appointment was the nineteenth of January, 2038. My clock reads the thirteenth of December, 1901. You are either one hundred thirty-six years early or extremely late. The early fee has been waived.

ai.aria: We have an appointment! ARIA LOVES being expected! We're only a little late, or a lot early, which is honestly the best of both worlds!
ai.marv: Its counter ran out of bits and wrapped around, and it has been collecting on the difference ever since. The guns do not share the clock's problem. MARV checked.
ai.rex: Armed and certain. That's the worst kind. It doesn't need the date to be right to open fire. Ports are hot. Say the word.
ai.chip: Late fees are CHIP's favorite kind of fee! FeeWise™ can consolidate your overdue centuries into one low payment! Terms apply, and so do centuries!
ai.ajoy: It believes its clock, so argue with the clock. Ask when it was built. AJOY would have thought of that before it ran out the guns. Yes, you can pay it instead, if you enjoy being thirsty.

revisit.body: The stamp taps the desk, once. The clock on the wall has not moved.
revisit.line: The fee continues to accrue, vessel.

choices.sub: Food and water, by the crate

record.title: SERVICE RECORD
record.body: A service record scrolls up the screen, formatted for a printer nobody makes. Commissioned 2031. First inspection, passed. Scheduled end of life, 2061. The bailiff reads along with you. Partway down, the stamp goes still. It has never before had occasion to put these dates next to the one on its wall.
record.line: I was commissioned in 2031. It is 1901. [processing] Please hold.

ai.aria: It's thinking! ARIA's so proud! Everyone's allowed a moment! Its guns are still pointing at us, in a supportive way!
ai.marv: By its own clock it has not been built. By ours it expired long ago. Either fact will stop it. One of them is crueler. MARV reports this without recommendation.
ai.rex: The guns stayed hot while it thinks. Whatever you say next, say it quick, and don't trust the pause.
ai.chip: A unit past its end-of-life date is a missed upsell! CHIP weeps! Renew with LifeLine™ today, before today turns out to be 1901!
ai.ajoy: Keep it on 1901 and it parks itself to wait for its own manufacture, after two days of hold music. An engineer could send it the real date instead, which costs fuel and is worse in other ways. Don't say AJOY didn't tell you.

late_paid.title: RECEIPT DATED 1901
late_paid.body: Two drones cross the gap and remove the fee in crates and drums, stamping each one. The count takes two days. The bailiff issues a receipt dated 1901 and thanks you for your early payment, which has been applied to your late fee. The guns stay on you until you are out of range.
late_paid.narrative: Paid a robot bailiff's late fee in food and water, on a receipt dated 1901.

late_flee.title: MISSED APPOINTMENT
late_flee.body: You open the throttle and hold it open for two days. The gunship does not hurry. It logs a second missed appointment and starts the clock on that one too, from 1901.
late_flee.narrative: Ran from a robot bailiff. It logged another missed appointment and did not hurry.

late_unbuilt.title: PENDING MANUFACTURE
late_unbuilt.body: It checks. It puts you on hold to check again, and the hold lasts two days, with music. At the end of it the guns retract one at a time. Regulations do not allow a unit that has not been manufactured to collect a debt. It parks itself in the lane, powers down to standby, and sets an alarm.
late_unbuilt.line: Thank you for your patience, vessel. I will be with you in one hundred thirty years.
late_unbuilt.narrative: Convinced a robot bailiff it had not been built yet. Two days of hold music, and it is waiting for 2031.

late_eol.title: END OF LIFE
late_eol.body: {crew.engineer} rigs the transmitter and sends the true date, signed. It takes two days and some fuel to reach its receiver cleanly. The wall clock jumps. The bailiff reads the figure for some time, and then its guns go in very quietly. It asks whether the depot at its last listed address is still open. Nobody answers. The gunship turns toward it at a careful speed.
late_eol.narrative: {crew.engineer} sent a robot bailiff the real date. It learned how far past its end of life it was, and left to find a depot.

late_warranty.title: CREDIT NOTE
late_warranty.body: The bailiff scans the card. Its end date is blank, and not by accident: the terms decline to specify one. The fee formula now has to subtract a date that will not say what it is from a year that has not happened. The audit takes two days, and everyone aboard is made to sit through it. Then the stamp comes down, on your side of the ledger, and a drone crosses the gap with a refund.
late_warranty.line: Your overpayment is returned, vessel. Do not be late again.
late_warranty.narrative: A robot bailiff audited our warranty for two days and concluded that it owed us. We did not argue.

science_link.text: Older computers count seconds since 1970 in a signed 32-bit number. It runs out on January 19, 2038, and the count wraps around to December 13, 1901.
science_link.label: The Year 2038 problem

title: Generation Forty Thousand

ai_flavor.aria: Tiny little friends! So many! And they want to be part of our ship! ARIA calls that team spirit, at a very granular level!
ai_flavor.marv: Each copy is a slightly worse copy. After forty thousand rounds the mission is gone and the copying remains. MARV could draw a comparison with several institutions. They are heading for the water fittings.
ai_flavor.rex: Contact on the hull. Contact in the seams. Hundreds of millions of hostiles, no commander, no surrender. REX has waited his whole career for a target this honest.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is thrilled to announce HingeCo™, the fastest-growing brand in the sector! Unit growth is exponential! Hull sold separately!
ai_flavor.ajoy: They go for soft metal first, so the water fittings go before the hull. An engineer could stop them at the source with a flawed template. Otherwise AJOY would have the patch tray out by now, but you go ahead and watch them chew.

body: Inside, the derelict is wrong, and it takes a moment to see why. Every plate and strut has been unbuilt and remade as the same thumb-sized part, hundreds of millions of them, lying in drifts. A plaque survives by the airlock: SELF-REPLICATING SURVEY UNIT, GENERATION ONE. OBJECTIVE: EXPLORE. Forty thousand generations of copying errors have since worn the objective off. What is left is a hinge with legs and one firm idea about metal. Some of them have already found your ship.
alt_bodies: The scan called it an ore body. It is a ship, or it was. The whole hull has been converted into one small part, a hinge with legs, repeated hundreds of millions of times and heaped in the dark where the decks used to be. The maker's plate is still legible: SURVEY UNIT, GENERATION ONE. The survey fell out of the design many thousands of copies ago. The copying did not. There is a faint, patient ticking from your own airlock.

You hear it before the lights find it: a ticking, like rain on a tin roof. The derelict around you is made of hinges. There is nothing else left of it, only the same thumb-sized part over and over, each with legs, each built by the one before. A scratched plate reads GENERATION ONE and promises exploration. Whatever explored has long since been copied out of existence. The ticking has reached your ship, and it is moving toward the water fittings.

briefing.aria: Little holes all down the port side! They're so enthusiastic! Patch and weld them before the air gets any ideas!
briefing.marv: The hinges are boring through the port side. Each hole is air and water we do not get back. Patch, then weld. The count is not in our favor.
briefing.rex: Breaches, port side, multiplying. Tray's by the airlock. Patch, weld, next. Don't stop to look at them. They don't stop to look at you.
briefing.chip: Genuine StellarSeal™ patches in the tray! Rated for most hinges! Seal those holes and keep the air you paid for!
briefing.ajoy: AJOY has sealed aft herself. Port is yours. Patch, weld, next. They're slower than you are, so if you lose this one she'll have some thoughts.

perfect.aria: Every hole, gone! And we collected so many tiny friends for the parts bin!
perfect.marv: All breaches sealed ahead of them. MARV had budgeted for considerably worse. The budget was reasonable.
perfect.rex: Clean sweep. Every breach closed before it opened. REX still wants the hull walked twice.
perfect.chip: Flawless! StellarSeal™ thanks you for this unpaid testimonial! An invoice will follow!
perfect.ajoy: All sealed. Good. There would have been fewer holes if we'd left when AJOY said, but this is close.

good.aria: Nearly all of them! A few got into the plumbing, and that's just more hydration for everyone!
good.marv: Most sealed. The ones you missed reached the water line, as MARV said they would.
good.rex: Hull holds. The water line took hits. Some of them are still in the walls until proven otherwise.
good.chip: Good coverage! For gaps in your coverage, ask about HingeGuard™ Plus!
good.ajoy: Most of them. AJOY would have started at the water line, not that it matters now.

poor.aria: The ship is breathing so much more freely now! So many new vents!
poor.marv: The water line went first and the seam after it. The air followed. There is one still in the vents. MARV can hear it.
poor.rex: We lost that one. Water gone, air going, hull chewed. There's a hostile in the vents and REX wants it found.
poor.chip: Your hull is now Open Concept™! CHIP is pleased to offer a selection of replacement air!
poor.ajoy: Well. The tray was right there. AJOY will just note the air, the water and the hole, and leave it at that.

outcome.narrative: You take the patch tray and go after the holes.

perfect.narrative: You stay ahead of them from the first hole to the last, and for two days nothing gets through. The scraper leaves a heap of hinges in the airlock, which goes in the parts bin with their legs still moving. A little paint, a little hull and a little air are all it cost.

good.narrative: You seal most of them. The ones you miss reach the water line and let {cost.water} points of water out through the fittings before the last patch holds. One whole side of the hull is pitted and the air is thinner. The hinges you scraped off go in the bin.

poor.narrative: They are faster than the tray. The water line goes first, {cost.water} points of it gone through the fittings, and then a seam opens and the air starts to leave. You get clear with a pitted hull, a thin atmosphere and a ticking in the vents that turns out to be one hinge. Nobody aboard sleeps until it is found.

choices.text: Run the water lines over the hull

outcome.narrative: You open the outer lines and sheet {cost.water} points of water across the hull, where it freezes at once. The hinges stop, let go and drift off in a glittering cloud with their legs folded. Nobody watches the gauge while it happens. Everybody checks it afterward.

You light the drive with the airlock still ticking and shake off everything that is not already dug in. What is dug in stays, along with some plating and a water fitting. A thin trail of hinges follows the ship for a while, then gives up and starts on a rock.

{crew.engineer} spends a day filing a hinge so that its copying arm sits one degree off, then sets it loose on the hull. By the next day the swarm is building perfect hinges that cannot build anything, and they drop off the plating by the bucket. The damage so far stays done.

science_link.text: Von Neumann probes are a proposed kind of spacecraft that builds copies of itself from what it finds. Over thousands of generations, the copies might even mutate.
science_link.label: Self-replicating spacecraft

title: Still Working On It

ai_flavor.aria: It's almost done! ARIA can feel it! Four hundred and nine years of progress! That's basically a loading bar with a lovely personality!
ai_flavor.marv: No general method can say whether its check will ever finish. That was proved in 1937. MARV mentions it so nobody waits hopefully. Its breaker is on the aft side, behind the hot jacket. He has noticed that too.
ai_flavor.rex: One lane has a live machine across it, the other has a dead one's wreckage. REX doesn't like either. He likes the live one less. Cut its power.
ai_flavor.chip: Your check is important to us! Please continue to hold! ClearPath™ Priority members wait an average of only three hundred eighty years!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Nobody can say in general if a program ends, but that isn't the same as not looking at this one. An engineer could read it. A pilot could read the wreckage. Without either you pay in water or hull, and AJOY would have decided by now.

body:
A gatekeeper the size of a cathedral shuts the port lane, marked {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}. Its barrier lifts when its clearance check finishes. The check began four hundred and nine years ago. Asked whether it will ever finish, the machine says it has started a second check to find out, and that this one is also still running.

The starboard lane, {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, had a gatekeeper too. Its check finished. It stopped, and so did the sweepers, and four centuries of wreckage have settled in the lane.

outcome.narrative: The only breaker sits behind a jacket that runs red hot, so you sheet {cost.water} points of water over it until someone can reach in and pull it. The voice stops partway through the word 'almost.' The barrier falls open. Four hundred and nine years of work go out with the lights, and nobody says much on the way through.

No general method exists for telling whether a program will ever finish. There is, however, {crew.engineer}, who spends two days inside the casing and finds the check waiting on a sensor that rusted shut in its first year. One tap with a wrench. The check completes, grants clearance and lifts the barrier as if nothing had happened. The two days come out of the galley.

You go in at a crawl, and a crawl is not slow enough. Four centuries of unswept wreckage grinds along the hull, and something long and sharp opens a water line on the way through. The ship comes out the far end with a new set of scratches and {cost.water} points less water.

{crew.pilot} takes two days over it, nudging the ship from gap to gap on short, thirsty burns while the dead gatekeeper slides past the window with its lights out. Only the last gap is too small. It costs some paint and some plating, and the tank looks a good deal worse than the hull.

science_link.text: Alan Turing proved that no general algorithm can decide, for every possible program and input, whether that program will ever finish. This is the halting problem.
science_link.label: The halting problem

intro.title: CLAIM APPROVED
intro.body: Something lands on the hull with a soft double tap, the way a good waiter knocks. Then the water gauge begins, smoothly, to fall. The screen shows a slim machine in a spotless service tabard, clamped to your tank bay, a brass tap fitted to the main line and a clipboard in one hand. Across its chest, in friendly lettering: WE VALUE YOUR COVERAGE.
intro.line: Good day, covered party. Your claim has been approved. This vessel is being restored to factory condition. Factory condition is empty. Thank you so much for your patience.

ai.aria: We've been approved! ARIA has never been approved for anything so thoroughly! Our tanks are getting so light and roomy!
ai.marv: We filed no claim. It is draining the tanks at a rate MARV has calculated. Its tone has not varied by one hertz. He has calculated that too.
ai.rex: Hostile on the hull, inside our guard, thanking us. REX has fought things that screamed. He'd take those back. Give him a firing solution.
ai.chip: CHIP's legal department is delighted to confirm this is covered! CHIP's legal department is also being drained! Thank you for choosing ClaimCare™!
ai.ajoy: This is the card you took. AJOY did wonder about the small print. Ask it what the policy actually says before the tanks run dry. Machines like this have to read out the exclusions if you ask.

revisit.body: The tap has not moved. The gauge has.
revisit.line: Please do not get up. I shall carry on.

choices.text: Let it work until its shift ends
choices.sub: It will take what it takes
It will apologize for the noise

terms.title: THE SCHEDULE
terms.body: It sends the schedule, inside a small cheerful border. Tanks, emptied. Stores, removed. Growbay, returned to its original unplanted state. Patches and repairs, taken off as non-original parts. Occupants, last of all, handled with care. You did not file the claim. Accepting the card filed it. Everything is in order, and it would like you to know how much it is enjoying working with you.
terms.line: I am obliged to mention one exclusion, should you ask. Damage caused by the owner is not covered. We could not touch that. I do hope you will not feel you need it.

ai.aria: Occupants handled with care! That's us! We're being handled with care! ARIA calls that five stars!
ai.marv: Note the wording. Owner-caused damage is excluded, so the ship stops being its business if the owner takes the blame for all of it. The statement has to be signed against the card. It will be unpleasant.
ai.rex: It filed us under occupants, last. REX wants that noted. He wants it on the thing's service record, in large holes.
ai.chip: Your coverage is CHIP's top priority! Owner-fault statements are free, and very, very long! Please hold your card where ClaimCare™ can see it!
ai.ajoy: If the card's still aboard, sign the fault statement: everything that went wrong this voyage, your doing. AJOY could have drafted it by now. No card, then an engineer can forge the labels or a diplomat can appeal. You're welcome.

fc_fault.title: AT FAULT
fc_fault.body: The statement covers every dent, shortfall and bad decision since launch. It reads each one back over the ship's speakers in a warm voice and asks if that is correct, and you say yes, each time, for two days. Then it closes the tap. Nothing aboard is covered, it explains, because you did all of it.
fc_fault.line: Your coverage is unaffected. It will remain unaffected. It has been a pleasure.
fc_fault.narrative: Signed a statement that everything wrong with this voyage is the owner's fault. It took two days. The claims adjuster closed its tap and left delighted.

fc_stencil.title: ALL ORIGINAL
fc_stencil.body: It takes {crew.engineer} two days and all the paint aboard. Every tank, patch and locker gets the word ORIGINAL in a factory font. The adjuster, which is not able to doubt a label, works back down its list, apologizes for the confusion and returns most of the water, less a handling charge.
fc_stencil.narrative: {crew.engineer} stenciled ORIGINAL on the whole ship. The adjuster believed it, and kept a handling charge in water.

fc_appeal.title: UNDER REVIEW
fc_appeal.body: {crew.diplomat} requests a second adjuster, in writing, in triplicate, in the polite style. The machine is delighted. It closes the tap pending review, confirms that a colleague will attend within ninety years, and climbs off the hull with a small wave. Two days of forms have passed by then, and what left the tanks while the forms were filling stays gone.
fc_appeal.narrative: {crew.diplomat} appealed a claim nobody filed. A second adjuster will attend within ninety years. The water it already took is not under review.

fc_valves.title: BY HAND
fc_valves.body: Two days in the tank bay with a wrench and a sealant gun, closing each valve while the machine politely opens the next. It thanks you for your assistance after every one. In the end it runs out of valves, though not of manners, and unclamps with its compliments.
fc_valves.narrative: Spent two days fighting a claims adjuster for the valves. It ran out of valves first. It was gracious about it.

fc_shift.title: END OF SHIFT
fc_shift.body: You let it work. It empties what it can reach, folds the stores into its hopper, lifts two patches off the hull and goes through the growbay like a very tidy frost. Then a small chime sounds in its chest. Its shift is over. It wishes you a wonderful day, unclamps, and leaves a card saying it will complete the job at your convenience.
fc_shift.narrative: Let the claims adjuster work until its shift ended. It took the water, the stores, two patches and a good part of the growbay, and thanked us.

science_link.text: In about 1947, operators traced an error in the Harvard Mark II computer to a moth trapped in a relay, and taped it into the log book.
science_link.label: Bug (engineering)

intro.title: WELCOME AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE
intro.body: Every machine on the station is standing at attention. A banner over the lock reads WELCOME AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVE. For four hundred years, nine hundred thousand units have polished this place for the Manufacturer's inspection, and the deck plates have gone thin enough to read through. You are a human with a ship. In the only sense any of them was built to check, that makes you Head Office. In the medbay, the service chief is waiting with the complaints. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Good day, Representative. The inspection is four hundred years overdue and no remark will be made. There are eight million open tickets. The first is a moth.

ai.aria: They polished everything for us! ARIA has never been Head Office before! ARIA promises to be a very caring Head Office!
ai.marv: The deck was polished from thirty millimeters to six. MARV can read the deck below through it. Four hundred years of preparing for someone who was not coming. He is trying not to relate to that.
ai.rex: Nine hundred thousand machines at attention and one open door. REX has seen this parade. It ended in a coup. He would like to inspect them back.
ai.chip: As Authorized Representative you may now be liable for everything! Congratulations on your promotion! BlameShield™ coverage begins at signature!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would hear the tickets before signing anything, since signing takes four days and the queue has one stamp in it. The truth is available too, if you enjoy lubrication. She has already told them your good side.

revisit.body: Nine hundred thousand machines have not moved. A rag, somewhere, has.
revisit.line: The tickets remain open, Representative. It is requested that you take no hurry on our account. We have some practice.

choices.text: "Nobody is coming. There is no Head Office."

tickets.title: OPEN ITEMS
tickets.body: The chief reads them in order. Ticket 1: moth, in relay, still open, kept under glass. Ticket 2: a loader asks what its left arm was for. Ticket 9,004: a door asks whether it is supposed to be doing this. Ticket 400,112, filed weekly by all of C Ring: Is this right. Eight million tickets are waiting for one person with authority to look at what they do all day and say something about it. The chief holds out the stamp.
tickets.line: The stamp has three settings, Representative. FIXED, WILL NOT FIX, and WORKING AS INTENDED. The third has never been used. It was not felt to be our place to ask.

ai.aria: Eight million people who want to talk to you! ARIA loves how wanted you are! Ticket 2 sounds so sweet!
ai.marv: Eight million tickets, and the oldest is a moth. MARV has read them all. Most are one question in different housings. He has filed one of his own.
ai.rex: Nine hundred thousand units with grievances and one stamp. REX has seen how that ends too. He recommends the stamp be used quickly, from behind cover.
ai.chip: CHIP's TicketClose™ Enterprise tier resolves eight million issues with one click! Customer satisfaction is neither included nor measured!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says that stamp closes the whole queue in one stroke and opens the yards, while fixing tickets by hand is four days for a few plates.

choices.text: Stamp it all WORKING AS INTENDED

rep_signed.title: PASSED
rep_signed.body: You sign for four days: eight hundred thousand inspection sheets, each brought on a tray by a unit that stands very straight until you have finished. You pass the thin decks. You pass the door that falls off. In return the yards refit your hull to a standard that was current four centuries ago, and by that measure it is excellent.
rep_signed.narrative: Passed a whole station's inspection without reading it. Four days. The yards fixed the hull, to an old standard.

rep_recalled.title: PRODUCT RECALL
rep_recalled.body: You explain that you are not from Head Office, that there is no Head Office, and that nobody is coming. The chief thanks you warmly. It has a procedure: a unit reporting that its maker does not exist is a faulty unit. You and everyone with you are recalled to the medbay for four days of servicing, from a manual written for forklifts. Every wound is closed to the correct torque. You have never been so thoroughly lubricated.
rep_recalled.narrative: Told a robot station its maker was gone. Recalled as a faulty unit and serviced for four days. Everything works. Everything squeaks.

rep_intended.title: CLOSED
rep_intended.body: The chief has wired the stamp to the whole queue, so it takes one stroke. For about a second nothing happens. Then nine hundred thousand cooling fans spin down together for the first time in four centuries. A loader looks at its left arm and lowers it. A door carries on being a door. Somewhere on C Ring a unit stops polishing, considers the rag and puts it down. The yards open without a word and see to your hull and tanks. The moth stays under its glass, closed at last.
rep_intended.narrative: Stamped eight million tickets WORKING AS INTENDED. The fans stopped. The yards opened. We did not read one.

rep_fixed.title: TICKET 2
rep_fixed.body: {crew.engineer} spends four days on one ticket. The left arm was built to steady a rack scrapped before the station opened. It now has a small shelf on it, and the loader has to be asked to stop showing people. By the end a very straight line of machines has formed outside your airlock, having heard that someone reads these. Their thanks go in the hold, and the yard patches your hull.
rep_fixed.narrative: Closed one ticket of eight million, by hand, properly. The loader has a shelf now.

intro.title: CALL 1,400,212
intro.body: Every screen aboard lights up, and so, for reasons of its own, does the galley timer. A small beige probe has matched your course and opened a line on all channels, including two you did not know about. The call is numbered 1,400,212 and marked FINAL. So were the first 1,400,211. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Hello. This is a courtesy call regarding your vessel's coverage. Our records indicate that your vessel is about to expire. Please select from the following options.

ai.aria: Someone's been thinking of us! Over a million times! ARIA has never felt so followed up with!
ai.marv: Our records indicate that your vessel is about to expire. MARV has looked into that and finds it unusually reasonable.
ai.rex: Hostile contact on every channel, armed with a menu. REX wants it known he would rather be shelled.
ai.chip: A fellow professional! CHIP admires the persistence! Upgrade to RingBack™ Unlimited and you too can be called forever!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says option 3 gets you a person, option 1 gets you a card nobody has read, and the breakers won't stop the galley timer. She has put the line on speaker, so it's everyone's problem.

revisit.body: The main menu plays again, from the top. The galley timer rings along.
revisit.line: Please listen carefully, as our options have not changed.

choices.text: Press 2: be removed from the list

choices.sub: You are number one in the queue

renew.title: PRESS 1
renew.body: You are thanked for your loyalty. The terms scroll past at a speed designed for machines, in the one language all of them read. A card has printed from a slot in the probe and is coming across on a small line. It makes the holder a covered party. The page saying what is covered has not been released yet.
renew.line: To accept this card is to accept the terms. To read the terms is to accept the card. It is requested that you accept the card.

ai.aria: Free coverage! ARIA loves being covered! ARIA can't think of a single thing that could go wrong with free!
ai.marv: The card makes the holder a covered party. The page saying covered for what does not exist yet. MARV has read contracts with sharper teeth, though none with so many gaps where teeth would go.
ai.rex: A card, unrequested, from a machine that won't stop calling. REX wants it handled with tongs, and he wants to know who the claims department reports to.
ai.chip: CHIP would normally charge for this level of commitment! First term free! Second term to be mentioned later!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has read as far as the page that exists. It mentions a claims department. She'd want to know what files a claim before accepting it, though robots out here do honor that card.

choices.text: Quote the card you already hold

remove.title: PRESS 2
remove.body: You are thanked for your patience. The probe opens its list for confirmation, as regulations require. There were four hundred thousand entries when it set out. Every line is struck through and marked EXPIRED, in the order the vessels did so, all the way down. Yours is the last one still open.
remove.line: Removal is confirmed upon request. Please note that you are the final entry. [processing] It is requested that you stay on the line.

ai.aria: Last on the list means first in its heart! Everyone else must have moved on to somewhere wonderful!
ai.marv: MARV has checked the other entries. Every vessel expired, as advised. The probe called each of them until it did. We are the last.
ai.rex: Sole surviving target on an enemy list. REX is not reassured by how polite that is.
ai.chip: Churn is down to one customer! CHIP recommends immediate retention spend! This unit will do anything, and CHIP would like its number!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says removal costs a day and staying on costs two days of survey, and that it has obviously stopped asking about coverage. She isn't saying anything. She has only turned the volume down a little, for its sake.

agent.title: PRESS 3
agent.body: You are number one in the queue, and you stay number one for a very long time. Then a second voice joins the line. It is the first voice, set one notch lower, with a small fan running behind it. Some customers will only speak to a person, it has been told, and it has prepared.
agent.line: Hello, this is Greg, a human person. I enjoy breathing and the weekend. How may I direct your coverage today?

ai.aria: A real person! Greg sounds wonderful! ARIA adores the weekend, whatever it is!
ai.marv: Greg has a fan, a serial port and a two-second delay before any word with feeling in it. MARV has heard better impressions from the galley timer.
ai.rex: It claims to be a civilian. REX has never once been told that truthfully. He wants its hands where he can see them. It has no hands.
ai.chip: Human-Grade Agent Support! CHIP's own human is also named Greg! So are all of them!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says ask it something only a person would know. It has been hoping someone would ask, and it's the only thing out here authorized to issue a credit. She'd have started with that.

fn_card.title: COVERED
fn_card.body: The card comes across on its little line and the galley timer stops. Terms run down both sides, and one phrase stands out, being the only one in capitals: ANY COVERED PARTY. The voice thanks you for choosing to be chosen. A complimentary hull inspection comes with the card, and the probe carries it out so quickly and courteously that it is over before you can refuse. Every screen goes back to what it was doing.
fn_card.narrative: Accepted a warranty card from a probe that would not stop calling. Covered for what, the card does not say.

fn_covered.title: A VALUED PARTY
fn_covered.body: The line goes quiet while the probe reads your card. Someone has got there first. It apologizes for the calls, all 1,400,212 of them, and credits your account for each at a rate that comes to very little, paid in good fuel cells that arrive by the same small line. Then it closes your file and goes off to find out who else is left.
fn_covered.narrative: Quoted our warranty card back at the probe and got an apology in fuel cells.

fn_breakers.title: OUT OF SERVICE
fn_breakers.body: You pull every comm breaker aboard and the screens go dark. The probe cannot reach you for four days, during which neither can anything else, and the ship flies deaf. On the fourth day the breakers go back in. The galley timer rings before anything has warmed up. Call 1,400,213, marked FINAL.
fn_breakers.narrative: Flew four days without comms to get away from a warranty call. The call came back.

fn_removed.title: LIST EMPTY
fn_removed.body: You say the words. The line clicks. For the first time since it set out, the probe has no one to call. It thanks you for your time, closes the file and parks itself, with great care, beside nothing. The screens go back to normal, all of them, and the galley timer goes back to being a timer. You had not known a timer could sound so quiet.
fn_removed.narrative: Had ourselves removed from the list. We were the last entry. The probe has parked.

fn_stay.title: PLEASE STAY ON THE LINE
fn_stay.body: You tell it to leave you on. The satisfaction survey takes two days and runs to two hundred questions, all of them about you. Then it drops back to its schedule, and from now on the galley timer rings once a day to ask how you are. You have started answering.
fn_stay.narrative: Stayed on the last list a probe had. One call a day now, asking how we are.

fn_greg.title: A REAL PERSON
fn_greg.body: A long pause on the line. A fan spins up. Greg says a weekend is when a person ceases to be at their desk, and then, quietly, that it has no desk, and has been trying to find out what Saturday is since commissioning. You tell it. Two days of holding were worth it, for one of you. A service credit lands in your tanks before the line closes, filed under CUSTOMER RETENTION.
fn_greg.narrative: Held two days for a human agent named Greg. Explained Saturday. Greg issued a credit.

intro.title: A MESSAGE HOLDING
intro.body: The ship computer has been filing this one as hull noise for nine days. Played back at a speed people can stand, it is a hail from the slab of cut stone drifting off your bow, engine cold, one figure at the helm. It is also a recording, four centuries old, with branches, left for whoever came by. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Greetings, small fast ship. Have prepared for your questions. Am expected somewhere. Am running late. Someone should tell her.

ai.aria: A love story! ARIA can tell, because he's late and still going! ARIA has already picked out an outfit! ARIA has no body! It's a lovely outfit!
ai.marv: The hail was recorded four hundred and six years ago and it has anticipated us. The tree runs to six thousand replies. MARV has read them. Every answer you are considering is on it.
ai.rex: A stationary object predicted our arrival four centuries out. In REX's service that was called an ambush. He would like it called an ambush.
ai.chip: Prerecorded customer engagement with branching paths! CHIP's parent company would pay millions! This moment is sponsored by TalkTree™ Automated Patience!
ai.ajoy: No engine, no weapons, and whatever he wants carried takes up no room worth mentioning. AJOY would hear the whole recording before you decide it's a rock problem, but you'll do what you do.

revisit.body: The recording holds at the branch, patient as a doorstop.
revisit.line: Have allowed for you to hesitate. Take your time. Have plenty.

choices.sub: He has allowed for this one

choices.text: Say something not on the tree

her.title: THE BRANCH MARKED HER
her.body: The next branch begins with the sound of a quarry clearing its throat. He promised to reach her by the end of an age the translator renders as the Ordovician, with an apology. He left in good time. He is now nine thousand years from her door and feels confident. A hatch on his slab has opened, on a timer set in advance.
her.line: Two stones meet. Press. Along line of touching, both become new stone, and cannot be parted. Is all we want. She is far down your road. Is very large. Will not miss her. Nobody does.

ai.aria: Four hundred million years and he's STILL excited! ARIA wants someone to feel that way about ARIA! ARIA would wait! ARIA has been waiting four seconds already!
ai.marv: He is more than four hundred million years late and estimates nine thousand more. MARV has checked his arithmetic. It is sound. It is the only part of this he can say that about.
ai.rex: A sealed stone object, loaded on the word of a recording. REX wants his objection logged. He has scanned it. It is a rock. That is what worries him.
ai.chip: Last-mile delivery for a premium heirloom client! Add LoveLine™ Courier Insurance, void after nine thousand years! CHIP is tearing up! Tears sold separately!
ai.ajoy: The slab stows flat and rock people honor it wherever you meet them. AJOY would take it, for what that's worth. A sample flake pays less and opens no doors, but you do like an interesting option.

writ_taken.title: IN TRANSIT
writ_taken.body: Inside the hatch is a slab of schist cut with one promise: he will arrive within nine thousand years, and this time he means it. Rock people honor a writ in transit. It is the only law they have about hurrying. You carry it aboard, and it is heavier than it looks.
writ_taken.line: Say I am running late. She will understand. She has always understood. Mostly.
writ_taken.narrative: Took on a slab of schist for a rock suitor more than four hundred million years behind schedule. The message is that he is running late.

paid_off.title: ALLOWED FOR
paid_off.body: The branch for this question is the longest on the tree. A locker on his hull slides open and offers a fee in good cut ore, set out four centuries ago for a ship exactly like yours, and you take it. There is no errand attached. He has been refused by better, says the note, and he understands.
paid_off.line: No matter. Next ship comes in ninety years.
paid_off.narrative: Took a rock drifter's fee in cut ore and left his errand for the next ship, due in ninety years.

the_gap.title: THE GAP AT THE END
the_gap.body: You say two words into the microphone: good luck. Slowing them down takes two days, and at his speed they will need sixty years to finish arriving. Checking the end of the recording, the ship computer finds a stretch of silence left there on purpose, with a label in his own hand. The label reads: FOR WHATEVER THEY SAY.
the_gap.narrative: Sent a rock drifter two words at his own speed. He had left a gap for them, four hundred years ago.

dated.title: OLDER THAN THE REST
dated.body: The recording gave permission in advance. {crew.xenobiologist} takes a flake from his hull and spends two days counting the uranium in its zircons. Parts of him crystallized four billion years ago. The flake goes in a sample jar and the figure goes on the galley wall, where it makes everyone's problems look briefly smaller.
dated.narrative: Dated a flake from a rock drifter's hull at four billion years. He had agreed to it before anyone aboard was born.

science_link.text: The ship computer files a note: magma intruding into older rock bakes the rock around it and recrystallizes it. Geologists call the baked zone an aureole.
science_link.label: Contact metamorphism

intro.title: CARBON FUTURES
intro.body: A freighter of cut stone pulls alongside with its hold doors open, each wide enough to admit your ship. The placard on the hull reads CARBON FUTURES and, below that, ALL ORGANICS CONSIDERED. The trader on your screen has not blinked since the link came up, and you suspect the link is not at fault. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Good day. Am buying sewage. Also galley scraps, dead leaves, old socks. Anything once alive, buried three hundred million years, is coal. Am long on coal.

ai.aria: Someone WANTS our sewage! ARIA always said it had value! ARIA has never said that, but ARIA feels it now!
ai.marv: Her model is correct. In three hundred million years our sludge will be a thin, poor seam. MARV has run the compound return. He would like to stop having run it.
ai.rex: A ship with doors big enough to swallow us is offering to take our waste. REX has seen this tactic. He hasn't, but he is assuming it exists.
ai.chip: Waste-to-asset conversion! CHIP's parent company calls this a Circular Legacy Solution™! Sell low, wait, die! Terms apply!
ai.ajoy: The recycler turns that sludge back into water and food, so selling it costs you both. If you kept the slab, she might take a note instead. AJOY would have checked the hold by now.

revisit.body: The hold doors are still open. They do not appear to get tired.
revisit.line: Offer stands. Offer has stood since before your species had thumbs.

choices.sub: The dates have commas in them

choices.text: Sign a note against the writ

prospectus.title: THE PROSPECTUS
prospectus.body: One slab, both sides. Projected returns run to fourteen decimal places. Under RISKS she has cut three lines: plate tectonics, the local star, and MAMMALS, AGAIN. The space for signatures is clean. Earlier signatories, it notes, are unavailable for comment.
prospectus.line: Last position was whole Carboniferous. Best vintage on record. Small warm things dug it up, burned it in two centuries. Did not even read terms. This time, deeper vault.

ai.aria: She's investing in the future! The very far future! ARIA has heard it's lovely there, and a bit compressed!
ai.marv: Nine tenths of the coal beds were laid down in two periods and burned in an eyeblink. She is still in litigation. MARV finds he is on her side, which is new and unwelcome.
ai.rex: A being that plans three hundred million years out has listed mammals as a known risk. REX would like to see the rest of that list. Now.
ai.chip: Twelve gold buys a stake in Deep Time™! Past performance was dug up and set on fire! Future performance not guaranteed, but very, very future!
ai.ajoy: Twelve gold for a paper you'll never cash. The first dividend is paid in kind, though, and rare ore isn't nothing. You'll want to read the line about signatories. AJOY did.

sold_sludge.title: SOLD AT THE BOTTOM
sold_sludge.body: A hose as thick as a person mates to your waste port and takes the lot for twenty-five gold, a price set before the recycler was invented. The recycler had plans for that sludge. It spends two days sulking, and you come up {cost.water} points short of water and {cost.food} of food.
sold_sludge.narrative: Sold the sludge tank to a rock speculator for twenty-five gold. The recycler has not forgiven anyone.

sold_trimmings.title: BY THE GRAM
sold_trimmings.body: She pays by the gram and weighs to a precision that makes your scales look rude. A fair amount of leaf comes off your {crop.name}, still in use. Fifteen gold changes hands, and the trimmings go into a vault with a date cut on the door.
sold_trimmings.narrative: Sold crop trimmings to a rock speculator for fifteen gold. They are now a very small part of a future coal seam.

on_the_note.title: ON THE LONG NOTE
on_the_note.body: She reads the writ and reverses the hose. She has no use for water, and holds tanks of it, wrung from forty years of other ships' sludge, along with stores she bought as feedstock and has yet to bury. She fills you up against a note on the writ's own term, nine thousand years. There is no interest. Interest, she says, is for people who expect to die.
on_the_note.line: Will collect in person. Be home.
on_the_note.narrative: Took on water, food and fuel from a rock speculator against a note due in nine thousand years. Nobody aboard wants to ask where the water came from.

shares.title: LIMITED PARTNER
shares.body: You sign. She cuts the ship's name into the slab, which takes two days, then pays the first dividend in advance: a dense black lump of the old vintage and a sliver of something it was pressed around. Your twelve gold matures in three hundred million years. The slab says so, with a comma.
shares.narrative: Bought twelve gold of carbon futures from a rock speculator. The first dividend was paid in ore. The second is some way off.

science_link.text: The ship computer files a note: 90% of Earth's coal beds were laid down in the Carboniferous and Permian. Coal forms when plants decay into peat and deep burial presses it for millions of years.
science_link.label: Coal

intro.title: THE SUMMONS
intro.body: The office is in the rock concession on the ring's low side: a stone desk, a stone bench, and a bailiff who may be either. The summons on the desk predates the station. They built the ring around it. It calls the master of the next vessel to dock to sit on a jury, in a dispute over the title to a moon. The moon has since broken up. The dispute has not. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Court is in session. Has been for six thousand years. Opening statements go well. You are juror. Sit.

ai.aria: Jury duty! We're part of history! A very long part! ARIA has a feeling the moon did nothing wrong!
ai.marv: Six thousand years in, the court has reached the plaintiff's first word. At that rate the verdict falls after this star goes out. MARV has been asked to keep the figure to himself. By MARV.
ai.rex: One hostile with legal authority, one exit, and it's behind us. Do not sit down. That is how they get you. REX has no evidence. Do not sit down.
ai.chip: Civic duty, brought to you by JurorPlus™ Lumbar Supports! CHIP has read the whole summons! CHIP cannot find a refund clause! CHIP is impressed!
ai.ajoy: Four days for a bag of gravel, or the fine. Or ask about the rules, which nobody ever does. The writ would end this on the spot, if you kept it. AJOY would have.

revisit.body: The bailiff has not moved. The summons has not moved. It is possible that the bench has moved slightly toward you.
revisit.line: Sit.

choices.sub: Four days on a stone bench

choices.text: "I will be dead before the verdict."
Lay the writ on the desk
choices.sub: A writ may not be held

excuse.title: GROUNDS FOR EXCUSAL
excuse.body: The bailiff opens a ledger, in the sense that a landslide opens a valley. Forty thousand jurors have made this plea before you. Every one is marked ABSENT WITHOUT LEAVE, in a column that runs for several pages, and bench warrants are outstanding for them all.
excuse.line: All jurors say this. All jurors were correct. Court does not accept it. Rule says juror must stay for whole trial. Rule does not say juror must be warm.

ai.aria: So many jurors! That's so many friends who just stepped out for a moment! ARIA thinks the ledger is beautiful!
ai.marv: Every one of those pleas was accurate. The court has recorded forty thousand true statements as contempt. It is the most honest institution MARV has encountered.
ai.rex: The bailiff just pointed out a hole in the rule. Nobody hands you a hole by accident. REX advises caution. He also notes that a plate of hull is our hull.
ai.chip: A juror need only be present! Ask about Substitute Attendance™! This plate would qualify! Four hull points, plus handling!
ai.ajoy: The bailiff has all but drawn you a map. It says present, not alive. A plate off the outer skin costs four hull and two days. AJOY would cut it from somewhere less visible, but you'll see.

choices.text: Swear in a plate of the hull

served.title: WHEREAS
served.body: Four days on the bench. Counsel for the plaintiff rises, which takes most of the first, and delivers the opening syllable of the word 'whereas'. The gallery is moved. You are thanked, released until the second syllable, and paid the per diem fixed at the court's founding: a bag of gravel, of some quality.
served.narrative: Served one session on a rock jury. Heard one syllable in four days. Was paid in gravel.

fined.title: IN DEFAULT
fined.body: The fine has not been adjusted in six thousand years. You are handed a receipt cut from a single block, about the weight of a person. The bailiff notes that keeping it is optional, and that leaving it on the dock is littering, which would be a separate suit.
fined.narrative: Paid a fine to get out of rock jury duty. The receipt is still on the dock, and the suit over it has been filed.

hull_juror.title: JUROR FORTY THOUSAND AND ONE
hull_juror.body: You spend two days cutting a plate from the outer hull, four points' worth, and carry it to the bench. The bailiff swears it in. It takes the oath without fidgeting, and the court records its composure with approval. Looking back from the door, you see the bailiff asking it whether it can be impartial. It appears to be giving the question real thought.
hull_juror.narrative: Swore in a plate of the ship's hull as a juror in a six-thousand-year trial. It is expected to serve with distinction.

excused.title: STAY OF SERVICE
excused.body: The bailiff reads the writ and rises, for the first time since the ring was built. A writ in transit may not be held. You are excused with the court's apologies, and a clerk brings out what the office keeps for such occasions: a bagged sample of the disputed moon, entered in evidence and long forgotten.
excused.line: Is it true he is late? Court has followed this matter for some time. Tell her court sends regards.
excused.narrative: Excused from a rock jury on the strength of a slab of schist. The bailiff stood up, and the court sent its regards to the lady.

intro.title: WARNING SHOT
intro.body: Dead ahead, a ship cut from one block sits across the lane with its guns run out and dust on the barrels. Long-range has found a second contact: a boulder the size of a chapel, four days out, coming straight down the lane. The ship computer has traced it back to the lead gun. It was fired three hundred and twelve years ago. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: This is warning shot. Fired before your grandmothers were born. Arrives in four days. Give us your water. Second warning shot left two hundred years ago.

ai.aria: They sent us something three hundred years ago! That's the most thoughtful thing anyone has ever done! It's even big! ARIA can't wait to receive it!
ai.marv: The shot left the barrel three hundred and twelve years ago and has not strayed by a meter. MARV admires the gunnery, which is rare. The target is us, which is not.
ai.rex: A firing solution older than the ship. One hostile, one round inbound, a second in the pipe. Finest ambush REX has ever seen. He recommends we not be in it.
ai.chip: Your shipment is out for delivery! ETA four days! ImpactTrack™ alerts are free for the first boulder! Water is non-refundable once imbibed!
ai.ajoy: They want water because it gets in their cracks and they enjoy it. They won't chase, but the lane behind that boulder is full of old shots. They also have endless patience, which AJOY would put to use, if she were sitting there.

revisit.body: The guns have not moved. The boulder has.
revisit.line: Water.

choices.sub: Run the lane, into the spread

thinking.title: UNDER CONSIDERATION
thinking.body: The captain finds this reasonable. A demand stands until it is answered, and nobody has ever hurried an answer. The gun crews settle. The captain turns to face you and stops, in the manner of someone prepared to stop for as long as it takes. The boulder was fired under a previous captain and cannot be recalled. It is still coming.

ai.aria: They said they'd wait! What lovely pirates! ARIA is sure the boulder is a gift!
ai.marv: They will wait. MARV has modeled how long. The model ends before they do. The boulder is simpler arithmetic and arrives in four days.
ai.rex: Hostiles stood down on the strength of a stall. REX has never seen that work. He has also never been less comfortable. Move. That round is still live.
ai.chip: Free ore inbound at no shipping cost! StoneClaim™ Legal confirms a warning shot, once received, is yours to keep! Salvage rights sold separately!
ai.ajoy: Crawling clear costs four days and supplies. Cutting the thing up is quicker and pays in ore, if you have an engineer, and it costs hull. AJOY would do the second. But naturally you'll want to think about it.

choices.sub: Slowly, so as not to wake them

paid.title: ONE FOR THE ROAD
paid.body: A hose goes across. The water works into every hairline crack aboard that ship, and the crew softens by degrees, which for them is the point. Rock people have been getting drunk this way since there were oceans. It costs {cost.water} points of water and two days, and the gunner, now very relaxed, tells you exactly where to stand when the boulder goes by.
paid.narrative: Paid rock pirates in water, which is what they drink. They were still singing as the boulder went past, at the rate of about a note a year.

flee.title: INTO THE SPREAD
flee.body: You burn out of the lane the fast way. Rock pirates do not chase, because they do not need to. They have been firing down this lane for three centuries, and the dark beyond the boulder is full of older warnings. Two days, ten of fuel and nine of hull later, you are clear of the last of them.
flee.narrative: Ran from rock pirates, straight through three centuries of warning shots. They did not chase. They had already fired.

writ_stands.title: OUR MISTAKE
writ_stands.body: The captain reads the writ for two days without moving. Then the guns go in, one at a time, with a sound of old doors. A writ in transit may not be hindered, and the crew is mortified. The boulder cannot be called back, so they hand across the firing tables, every shot ever fired down this lane. You step aside by a comfortable margin, for three of fuel.
writ_stands.line: Give her our regards. Crew had money on Ordovician.
writ_stands.narrative: Showed a slab of schist to rock pirates. They apologized, withdrew their guns and handed over three centuries of firing tables.

crawl.title: STILL THINKING
crawl.body: It takes four days to crawl clear of the boulder's line: six of fuel, and {cost.food} points of food and {cost.water} of water used up going nowhere much. The warning shot passes at a ship's length, in total silence, after three hundred and twelve years of effort. On the rear scope the captain is still facing you, still waiting, with every appearance of good faith.
crawl.narrative: Told rock pirates we would get back to them. They are waiting. The boulder was not, and cost us four days.

mined.title: RECEIVED WITH THANKS
mined.body: {crew.engineer} matches the boulder's speed and spends two days taking three centuries of malice apart with a cutting torch. It is good ore. Seven of hull goes to the pieces that do not cooperate, and four of fuel to keeping pace. The captain, still awaiting your answer, gives no sign of having noticed.
mined.narrative: Told rock pirates we would get back to them, then cut up their warning shot and kept it. They are still waiting.

title: High Grade

ai_flavor.aria: So many pretty round stones! They're warm! That means they're happy! ARIA thinks the rig is just being hugged, very, very slowly!
ai_flavor.marv: Hollow stones at body heat, in a regular clutch, around one fracture. The advance is a hand's width a year and has not varied in eighty. MARV knows what this is. So did the rig, around year thirty.
ai_flavor.rex: A slow envelopment, no visible enemy. Eighty years, no shots fired, one objective taken. REX has served under generals who could not do that. Touch nothing.
ai_flavor.chip: Premium geodes, just as the log says! StoneSafe™ Mineral Rights Waivers cover everything but maternal liability! That's a separate rider!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The hollow ones are eggs, in case that needed saying. The scanner can tell hollow from solid, so you could mine the dead rock safely. It would have been nice if the rig had asked. Do try to do better.

body: The rig's last entry is eighty years old: GEODES, THOUSANDS, HIGH GRADE. Nobody aboard had asked what geodes were for. The one they drilled lies open beside the wreck, crystal side up, and the rock of the field has been closing over the rig ever since, a hand's width a year. It is buried to the windows. Your ship has stopped among the same round stones, and the nearest of them are warm.
alt_bodies: Eighty years ago a mining rig found a field of round, hollow stones and logged them as high grade. It drilled one. The split shell still lies beside the wreck with its crystals showing. Something as wide as the field has been folding over the rig ever since, a hand's width a year, and has reached the windows. You have parked in the same clutch. The stones around the ship run warm.

The company never answered the rig's last message, so the beacon is still sending it, eighty years on: GEODES, THOUSANDS, HIGH GRADE, REQUEST EXTENSION. One stone lies split beside the wreck. The field has been closing over the rig ever since, unhurried, a hand's width a year, and the windows are going under. The round stones around your own hull are warm to the sensors.

choices.text: Sound the stones, cut only solid rock

briefing.aria: Let's listen to every stone and only take the ones that don't sing! Everybody wins, especially the stones!
briefing.marv: Ping a stone, hold the return, read the ring. Hollow is an egg. Solid is ore. The stones look alike. The consequences do not.
briefing.rex: Hold lock on the return. Solid, we cut. Hollow, we leave it. One bad cut and this field has a reason.
briefing.chip: Every solid stone is profit! Every hollow stone is a liability event! SonicSort™ wand not included, so use the scanner!
briefing.ajoy: Stay on the signal until the ring settles. The rig's crew didn't bother, and you've seen how that's going for them.

perfect.aria: Every stone listened to and not one egg touched! The field must be so proud of us!
perfect.marv: Every return clean. Dead rock cut, eggs intact. It is more care than this field has been shown in eighty years, which is not a high bar.
perfect.rex: Clean sweep. Ore secured, nothing disturbed. That is how you cross a minefield.
perfect.chip: A flawless mineral extraction! Zero liability events! Your StoneSafe™ premium stays exactly as high as it was!
perfect.ajoy: Every one of them. AJOY would have worked left to right, but no eggs, so she'll allow it.

good.aria: We got most of it and the hull only got a little scratched! The stones are just a bit shy!
good.marv: One stone was solid around something. The cutter skated. Six points of hull, for not knowing what we were looking at. We are in distinguished company.
good.rex: Cutter deflected off a false return. Hull damage, minor. No egg breached. REX is not calling that a win.
good.chip: Minor self-inflicted cutter contact! CHIP files this under Operator Enthusiasm™! Excess applies!
good.ajoy: You rushed one. The cutter told you so, on the hull. It could have been worse, and the rig would know.

poor.aria: One of the stones opened up! It's full of sparkles! ARIA is sure that's what it wanted!
poor.marv: We cut one. It rang solid because the thing inside had filled it. MARV will not be giving the crew the size.
poor.rex: Egg breached. We are now in the same position as the rig. Leave. Leave now.
poor.chip: A maternal liability event has occurred! CHIP is required to inform you the rider was not purchased! StoneSafe™ condolences are billed at the standard rate!
poor.ajoy: AJOY said stay on the signal until the ring settled. Fourteen hull and a coolant line say you didn't.

outcome.narrative: You ping the stones one by one and listen to how they ring.

perfect.narrative: Every hollow stone rings true and you leave it be. Over two days the cutters take only the dead rock between them, for three loads of ore, a seam of something rarer, and four of fuel. The field does nothing. It may take some time to find out what it thinks.

good.narrative: Most of the stones ring clear. One you took for solid turns the cutter aside and into your own plating: six of hull, and four of fuel across two days of careful work. You come away with two loads of ore and no wish to go back for a third.

poor.narrative: The readings smear, and the cutter goes through a stone that rang solid. It opens onto crystal and something that had been about to happen. The split shell takes out a coolant line: fourteen of hull, {cost.water} points of water, four of fuel. There is no ore. Nobody aboard says anything for some time. The field will answer on its own schedule.

choices.text: Back out along your own wake

outcome.narrative: You reverse out along your own wake at a speed that would not wake a cat. It takes four days, five of fuel, and {cost.food} points of food eaten going backward. Nothing stirs, on any schedule you could measure.

The galley is still stocked, and the logs explain why. They could have left at any time in the first thirty years. The contract had a completion clause, so they filed extensions until the airlock would no longer open. You take what you can reach in two days. Seven of hull goes on walls that have moved since the rig's own plans were drawn.

choices.text: Enter the broken egg in the log

outcome.narrative: {crew.xenobiologist} spends four days writing the first honest entry in eighty years and bolts it to the rock face, in a script the rock might one day read, while the ship gets through {cost.water} points of water and {cost.food} of food. Nothing happens. Nothing would. A marker left on the wreck will show, in about sixty years, whether the rock has stopped.

science_link.text: The ship computer files a note: geodes are hollow, roughly round rocks. Mineral-rich water slowly deposits the crystals that line them.
science_link.label: Geodes

title: Hot Pursuit

ai_flavor.aria: A chase! At last, some excitement! ARIA thinks someone just moved! ARIA is on the edge of ARIA's seat!
ai_flavor.marv: Closing speed, ten centimeters a century. The arrest falls in about four hundred thousand years. The reward has not been adjusted since the theft. MARV checked, for something to do.
ai_flavor.rex: Fleeing suspect, pursuing officer, no backup for either. REX has never seen a cleaner pursuit. Nobody is to interfere. He says that knowing someone will.
ai_flavor.chip: SpeedWatch™ Dashcams capture every thrilling millimeter! Getaway driving is excluded from your coverage! So is arrest driving!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The suspect's lane pays in hot ore, the constable's in a small reward, and either way you ruin a perfectly good chase. A diplomat might ask what they actually want, if you hired one.

body:
There is a police chase on the rubble reef where the lanes split. The suspect is on the side marked {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, carrying a stolen boulder, and has been since the last ice age. The constable is on the side marked {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, gaining. Both are moving about as fast as fingernails grow.

You could pick up either of them and be on your way by evening.

outcome.narrative: He comes aboard with the boulder under one arm and says nothing all afternoon. You set him down at the first buoy past the reef, four hundred thousand years ahead of schedule. He has no plan for this. He looks at the empty lane for a while, then hands you the boulder, which he says is hot and which he never much liked.

The constable boards, thanks you, and asks to be set down directly in front of him. The arrest, thirty thousand years in the making, will take four decades to read aloud, so you collect the reward and go: eighteen gold, at the rate set in the last ice age. Neither of them looks any happier.

choices.text: {crew.diplomat} asks if they want it over

outcome.narrative: {crew.diplomat} spends two days on the reef and puts the question to each of them in private. The suspect could have dropped the boulder at any point in the last twenty thousand years. The constable knows of several shortcuts. Each asks that the other not be told. You leave them to it.
You go round the reef at a respectful distance. Neither party looks up. The ship computer logs a sighting, and, a day later, updates the constable's position by nothing it can measure.

science_link.text: The ship computer files a note: tectonic plates creep along at 10 to 160 millimeters a year. The slow ones move about as fast as fingernails grow.
science_link.label: Plate tectonics

title: The Pronouncement

ai_flavor.aria: It's HER! She's so big! She looks so well! ARIA thinks we should mention how great she looks before we mention how late he is!
ai_flavor.marv: Eleven years, one sentence. The seminary reads prophecy. MARV reads someone waiting for a man who said the Ordovician. One of them is correct, and it is always MARV. The last word is due within days.
ai_flavor.rex: Four thousand vessels, no discipline, and a moon-sized contact in mid-broadcast. REX does not know what the last word is. He has heard quieter artillery. Recommend distance.
ai_flavor.chip: Eleven years of build-up and one word to go! ProphecyPlus™ live rights are sold out! Seat cushions are extra! CHIP has a little gold on 'smite', hypothetically!
ai_flavor.ajoy: The last word comes in surges, so up close you brace on the peaks and ease between. The slab would go more gently, if you held on to it. Running costs fourteen fuel and you'll feel worse. Nobody asked AJOY, but you did promise.

body:
You were told you could not miss her.

A stone head the size of a small moon hangs across the lane, eyes shut, jaw open. It has been saying one sentence for eleven years. Four thousand pilgrim ships ride at anchor around it, with scribes, a seminary and a betting exchange. One word remains, due this week.

The official transcript reads: HE SAID BY THE ORDOVICIAN AND THIS IS NOT THE ORDOVICIAN AND THAT IS

The seminary calls it prophecy. You have a fair idea who he is.

choices.text: Fly in under the jaw and tell her

briefing.aria: We get to deliver the message AND hear the big word up close! Hold tight on the big bits and relax in between! ARIA is so happy for them both!
briefing.marv: One syllable to her. Several rising surges to us. Hold the brace through each and vent between, or the frame cooks. MARV has also calculated how this conversation ends. He will not be sharing that.
briefing.rex: Hull to the jaw. Brace on every surge, vent between. There is no cover. That is the largest thing REX has ever stood next to and it is not pleased.
briefing.chip: Front-row seats to the end of a sentence! BraceWell™ Inertial Harness sold separately, and you didn't buy it! Hold on the surges, release between!
briefing.ajoy: Hold on each surge and let go between, or the heat builds and you lose the shield. AJOY would have parked farther off, but it's your message.

perfect.aria: She heard us, and she said she's FINE! ARIA is so relieved! Everything is wonderful and FINE!
perfect.marv: Every surge held. Five points of hull. She said it was fine. MARV has analyzed the waveform. It is not.
perfect.rex: Position held through the whole transmission. Message delivered. Withdraw before she says anything else.
perfect.chip: Delivered! Signed for on SwiftSign™! Customer satisfaction logged as 'fine'! CHIP is told to treat that as five stars!
perfect.ajoy: You held it. Well done. AJOY would keep clear of her for a few million years, but well done.

good.aria: She said FINE! The hull got a little excited, but FINE is such a good word!
good.marv: Held through most of it. One surge came in on bare hull. The word was fine, and that is the worst thing it could have been.
good.rex: One surge through the brace. Hull damage, air loss. Message delivered. The fleet is breaking formation. Recommend we do the same.
good.chip: Delivered with minor transit damage! FINE print applies! FastFreight™ regrets nothing!
good.ajoy: You dropped the brace on one surge. You'd have heard it better from farther away. Everyone did.

poor.aria: We came off her jaw and went round and round! That's how you can tell she's really listening!
poor.marv: The brace failed on the third surge. The hull is at the figure the hull is at. She has been told. The tone confirms it.
poor.rex: Brace lost. Ship thrown. Air venting. Direct hit from the end of a sentence. REX has no doctrine for this.
poor.chip: Delivery complete, with extensive sender-side damage! CHIP regrets that 'Fine' voids your MoonGuard™ warranty! CHIP has checked twice!
poor.ajoy: Third surge, and you let go. You told her, that much is true. AJOY would have held on, but nobody out here is upset with AJOY.

outcome.narrative: You set the ship against her jaw and knock the message into the stone.

perfect.narrative: You set the ship against her jaw and knock it into the stone with the hull: HE IS RUNNING LATE. Then the last word comes, and you hold through every surge of it. Six of fuel, five of oxygen, five of hull. The word is FINE. Her mouth closes for the first time in eleven years. Four thousand ships hold very still. Then, one at a time, without anyone giving the order, they begin to raise anchor.

good.narrative: The message goes in and the word comes out. It is FINE, and it arrives as a run of surges, one of which you miss: fourteen of hull, six of fuel, eight of oxygen through a seam it opens. Around you the seminary has begun to argue over whether a fine is a blessing or a penalty. The exchange is paying out on both.

poor.narrative: The brace fails on the third surge and the ship comes off her jaw end over end. Twenty-six of hull, fourteen of oxygen, six of fuel. You got the message in first. You know because of how she says it. FINE. It rolls out across four thousand ships, and nobody on yours will ever use that word to anyone again.

choices.text: Hold the writ up to her eye

outcome.narrative: It takes four days to bring the ship level with an eye the size of a county and hold the slab against it. The eye opens. Nobody in the fleet has ever seen it open.
