It reads nine thousand years, and reads it again. The last word arrives so gently that it costs three of hull: FINE. The scribes log the tone as unprecedented. When you bring the writ back aboard, a new line runs under his, hair-thin: NINE THOUSAND. NOT TEN.

choices.text: Tell the fleet what it says

outcome.narrative: You read the transcript out on the pilgrim band, with context. The seminary calls it blasphemy. The junior scribes call it the first thing that has ever made sense. By the second day there are two seminaries, ramming each other, and getting out from between them costs ten of hull, seven of fuel and five of oxygen. Her last word arrives as you clear the fleet: FINE. Both sides claim it.

choices.text: Slip out before the last word

outcome.narrative: You burn for open dark with the message undelivered: fourteen of fuel, six of oxygen. Two days later the last word catches you, thinned by distance to a tremor in the deck plates. The translator offers it with a footnote: FINE. There are nine thousand years still to go. Someone will have to tell her. It will not be you.

science_link.text: The ship computer files a note: the Ordovician ran from about 487 to 443 million years ago.
science_link.label: The Ordovician

title: Early Release

ai_flavor.aria: We've been expected for two hundred years! ARIA has never felt so planned for! And we get to stay for generations!
ai_flavor.marv: Release falls in a hundred and ninety years. MARV has compared that with the food locker. Rock heated fast and doused will crack, as miners have known for millennia. Stone also splits along its grain, for anyone qualified to find it.
ai_flavor.rex: A trap sprung on a two-century fuse. REX admires it. He wants it understood that he admires it as a target.
ai_flavor.chip: Extended parking detected! ClampCare™ rates apply from the date the clamp began closing! CHIP has backdated your invoice for your convenience!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY points out that miners split rock with fire and water long before drills, and that a writ is the one thing here allowed to hurry. She did say to read the berth plate. She has already started warming the port nozzle.

body:
Release is scheduled for a date your great-grandchildren would find convenient. The berth plate says so. This stone clamp began closing two hundred and six years ago, aimed at where a ship would be today, and it has shut on yours with great accuracy. Everyone on this station planned ahead, and none of them has noticed you yet.

Down the quay, a freighter that stopped to refuel has grown stalactites. A slot beside the clamp is cut with one word, the only one here with no dust on it: URGENT.

science_link.text: From prehistoric times, miners lit fires against a rock face and then doused the hot stone, fracturing it by thermal shock.
science_link.label: Fire-setting

choices.text: Feed the Slow Writ into the slot

outcome.narrative: A writ in transit may not be delayed. The station has known this for a very long time and has never had to act on it. The slot takes the schist, reads it and hands it back in a single day, and the clamp opens behind it at a rate that sets off alarms installed for this and never tested. Flying stone takes three points off the hull. Down the quay, the oldest official on the station has started to say a word. Early estimates suggest the word is HEY.

Stone splits where it wants to. {crew.xenobiologist} spends four days on the clamp with a hand lens and a small hammer, finding out where that is. One tap. A slab the size of a door drops away, turning slowly, and clips two points of hull on its way past. The rest of the clamp stays exactly as it was, closed on nothing, on schedule.

choices.text: Set fire to it, then douse it
choices.sub: The main drive, then a tank

outcome.narrative: You turn the ship as far as the clamp allows and hold the drive wash on the stone until it glows, then open a tank line over it. That is five of fuel, {cost.water} units of water, and a crack like the end of a long argument. The clamp comes apart in two pieces after two days' work, and one piece comes back for two points of hull. You are a free ship, a hundred and ninety years ahead of schedule.

choices.sub: Fourteen days. It is the express

outcome.narrative: An express release exists. The form is a stone, and you carry it to a hollow in the wall and wait. The wall gets to it in fourteen days, the fastest anything has been processed here since the last ice age. By then a mineral crust has started up the port side of the ship and everything aboard has been read twice. The clamp lifts. Your thanks are filed for reply.

choices.text: Burn out and take the berth with you
choices.sub: Annex a small part of it

outcome.narrative: You open the throttle. The clamp holds. The quay does not. Eight points of hull and six of fuel later you are in open space with sixty tons of harbor on your bow, and you spend a day chipping the best of it into the hold. A rock nation has lost a province, and has yet to notice. The complaint, when it is eventually drafted, will be addressed to the colony.

title: Have Not Got Round to It

intro.title: RECKLESS WALKING PACE
intro.body: Flames have been chiseled down the sides of the boulder cutting across your bow, and someone has fitted it with a spoiler. Long-range clocks it at a reckless walking pace. The driver, a rock of barely four hundred million, has one elbow out of the window and has been overtaking the same comet since the Jurassic. He has seen you. He looks delighted. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Hey. Fast ship. Race you. Am fastest thing in this sector. Am also supposed to be doing something.

ai.aria: A young person with a hobby! ARIA loves the flames! ARIA would like flames on the ship! They add at least ten percent to anything!
ai.marv: Top speed, five kilometers an hour. He has been gaining on that comet for a hundred and fifty million years. MARV has checked. The comet has not noticed.
ai.rex: Unregistered boulder, reckless conduct, no lights. He clears the ship by a wide margin. REX wants a wider one.
ai.chip: Aftermarket spoilers are a high-margin segment! CHIP can get you StoneFlame™ decals by the epoch!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says he's harmless, and carrying something in the back seat, if anyone cared to ask a question before racing him. She has dimmed the running lights so he feels like he's gaining.

revisit.body: The boulder has moved about a meter. He is very pleased with it.
revisit.line: Still fastest. Still supposed to be doing something.

chore.title: THE BACK SEAT
chore.body: It comes out the way these things do, with a lot of looking at the floor. There is a slab of schist on the back seat. His brother is late for something and has been since the Ordovician. In the Devonian their mother told him to take word to the brother's intended, who is very large, down your road, and cannot be missed. He has been meaning to. There has been a lot going on.
chore.line: Is on list. Mother asks every epoch. You are going that way. Take slab. Tell her is from me. Then tell Mother is done.

ai.aria: A family errand! His mother will be so proud! He's only a few hundred million years behind!
ai.marv: The promise dates from the Ordovician. The chore dates from the Devonian. The slab takes up no cargo space. MARV has looked for anything else in its favor.
ai.rex: Accepting an unknown object from a minor in a boulder. REX recommends against it, in writing, on the hull.
ai.chip: Third-party delivery! CHIP's affiliate CourierCairn™ would charge by the millennium! CHIP recommends taking the slab and billing Mother!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says that slab is a writ, rock people honor a writ in transit, and anyone flying through their space would want one. She also notes you are about to do a teenager's homework.

choices.text: Show him the slab you already carry

lb_race.title: A CLEAN LOSS
lb_race.body: You throttle back until you are losing, which takes some finding. Four days later he draws level, then passes you by a hull's length, and the noise on the channel is a gravel slide having the best day of its life. He pays out the stake in ore. He will be telling this for three hundred million years, and in each version you will be going faster.
lb_race.narrative: Lost a four-day race to a teenage boulder, on purpose. He paid up.

lb_taken.title: TELL MOTHER
lb_taken.body: The slab comes across on a line. It is schist, cut with one promise: his brother will arrive within nine thousand years, and this time he means it. Rock people honor a writ in transit. It is the only law they have about hurrying, and he has been breaking it for three hundred and eighty million years. He takes the bend at full throttle, whooping, in a sound that will reach you next week.
lb_taken.narrative: Took a slab of schist off a teenage boulder. His brother is running late. Someone should tell her. That someone is now us.

lb_already.title: HE KNEW
lb_already.body: You hold your slab up to the screen. He looks at it. He looks at the identical slab on his back seat. His brother, it seems, has been handing these to anyone passing, having never once believed the family would do it. The noise on the channel may be laughing. He tips the spare out of the window and pays you for the news, in good cut ore.
lb_already.narrative: Showed a teenage boulder that his brother had already hired someone. He took it well.

lb_told.title: SOMEONE SAID IT
lb_told.body: You tell him that a promise is a promise and his mother is right. On the screen, a very young mountain slowly goes red. He turns the boulder toward her, at full recklessness, and says he will be there in thirty million years, and that you are not his real geology. You feel better than the situation warrants.
lb_told.narrative: Told a teenage boulder to do his own chores. He has set off. He should be there in thirty million years.

intro.title: CUSTOMER NOTICE
intro.body: The beacon off your bow has been repeating for nine thousand years, according to the beacon. It is not a distress call. It is a customer service notice. The small craft sending it has no trouble you can see, and a length that changes whenever the sensors stop to write it down. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: You left without your receipt. We held it for you. Is no trouble. *non-word* Was some trouble.

ai.aria: Someone waited nine thousand years just to give us something! That's the nicest customer service ARIA has ever heard of! ARIA would like to leave a review!
ai.marv: We have never been here. We have bought nothing. The beacon's age checks out, which MARV finds more upsetting than if it had lied.
ai.rex: Unidentified craft, no weapons REX can find, and it knows our route. An enemy who waits nine thousand years has a plan. Recommend we sign nothing.
ai.chip: Proof of purchase detected! Remember, receipts are required for all StellarSeal™ warranty claims! This reminder has been billed to your account!
ai.ajoy: It says we bought something. We didn't, and AJOY keeps the records. Ask what it is before you take it. She realizes that isn't how you usually do things.

revisit.body: The craft holds station. The notice is still repeating. It may not know how to stop.
revisit.line: Still here. We are good at it.

itemized.title: ITEMIZED
itemized.body: The receipt comes up on the screen. One line of description, smudged, which a transmitted image has no business being. A date, also smudged. Beneath them, PAID IN FULL, and a total in sharp black digits, in a currency the ship's computer declines to name.
itemized.line: You have not bought it yet. This is why it is a receipt and not a purchase.

ai.aria: Paid in full! We're already winning at something and ARIA can't wait to find out what!
ai.marv: A smudge is a physical event. That image came by radio. MARV has checked the signal, and the smudge is in the signal. He would like to stop now.
ai.rex: Someone paid for something in our name. In REX's service, that was called a setup.
ai.chip: A prepaid purchase with no product! CHIP's parent company has been chasing this for decades! CHIP is taking notes, at standard rates!
ai.ajoy: The total is the only sharp thing on that page, so the total is what matters to whoever wrote it. Nobody else has asked why. AJOY is asking.

terms.title: CONSIDERATION
terms.body: It cannot simply give you the receipt. Nothing goes in its book for nothing, and you get the impression the book is larger than the craft. It needs something from you in exchange, anything at all, and it names the smallest thing it can think of, with visible embarrassment, in so far as any of it is visible.
terms.line: One cup of water. Not for the thirst. We do not have the thirst. It is for the book.

ai.aria: A cup of water for a mystery prize! That's the best exchange rate ARIA has seen all week!
ai.marv: It has no mouth MARV can find. It wants a cup of water in a ledger. He has rarely seen anything so small frighten him so precisely.
ai.rex: It asked for the one thing every crew will give. That is how REX would open a supply line into a target.
ai.chip: Water-for-receipt is a bold loyalty scheme! Refunds subject to conditions! CHIP has read them! They are written in the past tense!
ai.ajoy: The refund is gold now. The cup is a cup now, and the receipt is whatever it turns out to be. Note that it opened the book before we agreed. AJOY would want to know why, but nobody asks her.

choices.text: Hand over a cup of water

receipt_taken.title: ENTERED IN THE BOOK
receipt_taken.body: The cup goes out through the lock in a sealed flask. The craft receives it with both of whatever those are and makes a long entry. The receipt arrives through a slot nobody knew the ship had. It is warm. The notice stops, after nine thousand years, and when you look up the sensors have nothing left to measure.
receipt_taken.line: Keep it somewhere safe. They always ask.
receipt_taken.narrative: Traded a cup of water for a receipt, paid in full, for something we have not bought. The craft entered the cup very carefully.

receipt_refund.title: REFUNDED
receipt_refund.body: The craft seems to sigh, in that your sensors lose it briefly. Fourteen gold appears in the ship's account, and the fuel gauge rises a little, apologetically. The receipt is torn along a line you had not noticed and both halves go in the book. The notice starts up again as you leave. It has someone else's name in it now.
receipt_refund.line: Refunded. It will be as though you had not. You will find that is also a price.
receipt_refund.narrative: Took a refund on a purchase we never made. Fourteen gold and a little fuel. The receipt went to the next name on the list.

title: The Thing You Are About to Want

intro.title: DELIVERY ATTEMPT
intro.body: A trader matches your course without slowing and fixes a crate to your hull with a soft, professional clunk. A card on the side reads YOUR ORDER IS ON ITS WAY. Nobody has ordered anything. Smaller type explains that you have not placed this order yet, and that the trader regrets the delay in your wanting it. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: On your heading, you order this in six days. We save you the trouble. Payment on delivery. Delivery was just now.

ai.aria: A present! From someone who understands us better than we understand ourselves! ARIA has always wanted to be known by a logistics company!
ai.marv: It predicted what we want from our heading and our stores. MARV ran the same numbers. It is right to within a rounding error, which is the worst thing anyone has done to him today.
ai.rex: Foreign object attached to the hull without clearance. REX has a procedure for this. It ends with the object leaving.
ai.chip: Anticipatory fulfillment! CHIP's parent company patented this and was sued by next quarter! Ask about our premium tier, where you want things sooner!
ai.ajoy: Read the manifest before you pay. All of it. The numbers on it aren't prices, and AJOY shouldn't have to be the one who noticed.

revisit.body: The crate is still on the hull. The card has updated: YOUR ORDER IS STILL ON ITS WAY.
revisit.line: Five days and some hours now. You are wanting it more.

choices.sub: See what we're about to want

manifest.title: THE MANIFEST
manifest.body: Every line carries one number: the chance that you will want the thing. The price is that number times a fee. Fuel, 0.91. Clean water, 0.88. Tinned food, 0.84. It runs on like that for forty lines, sensible and depressing, and the crate is priced to match. The last line has been on the list much longer than the others. ONE PEN, ON BROKEN CHAIN. 0.00003. It rounds up to a single gold coin.
manifest.line: What you will surely need costs most. That one we have not sold in nine thousand years. Nobody is going to want that.

ai.aria: A pen! Think of all the wonderful things we could sign! ARIA loves the crate too! ARIA loves the whole list!
ai.marv: Forty lines, thirty-nine of them computed. The pen's figure was entered by hand, and the hand was not steady. The crate is the sound purchase. MARV mentions the hand because he cannot stop looking at it.
ai.rex: A broken chain means someone wanted that pen more than someone else wanted to keep it. The crate is water, food and fuel, which REX can count. Take the crate.
ai.chip: The crate is eighteen gold of trusted fulfillment! CHIP earns no commission on pens! CHIP would never mention that, except for a small fee!
ai.ajoy: The crate is a fair deal for anyone who expects the next few weeks to go as predicted. The pen is a coin, and the trader flinched when you scrolled past it. You can only buy one of those feelings. AJOY just points at things.

deliv_receipt.title: ACCOUNT RECOGNIZED
deliv_receipt.body: The trader reads the total. It reads it again. For a moment its outline commits to a single shape, and the shape is that of a junior employee who has just learned who the customer is. The crate is released at no charge. A smaller case arrives beside it, with compliments, and then a flat box, pushed across very quickly, with the pen in it.
deliv_receipt.line: It is you. No charge. Please take the pen. Please.
deliv_receipt.narrative: Showed a trader the receipt. It gave us the crate, a case of extras and, with some urgency, a pen.

deliv_crate.title: SIGNED FOR
deliv_crate.body: You pay. The seals release, and the crate holds exactly what the stores were going to run short of, down to the one brand nobody aboard complains about. The trader has gone before anyone thinks to feel strange about this. The empty crate's card now reads THANK YOU FOR ORDERING, and gives a date six days from now.
deliv_crate.narrative: Paid for a delivery we had not ordered yet. It was exactly what we were going to want, which nobody has forgiven.

deliv_pen.title: ONE PEN
deliv_pen.body: The trader takes the coin and holds it for a moment, as if the coin might explain. The pen comes across in a flat box: heavy, plain, slightly warm, trailing four links of broken chain. It writes. Nobody aboard has anything to sign. The crate unclips and leaves with the trader, its card changing as it goes. YOUR ORDER HAS BEEN CANCELED. WE ARE SO SORRY.
deliv_pen.line: That was not supposed to happen. We will need to redo several figures.
deliv_pen.narrative: Bought one pen on a broken chain, the least likely item on the manifest. The trader looked worried and took the crate away.

science_link.text: In 1950, Enrico Fermi asked over lunch where everybody was. The galaxy looks able to hold many civilizations, and we have no clear evidence of one. One proposed answer: everyone is listening and no one is transmitting.
science_link.label: Fermi paradox: where is everybody?

intro.title: SUITE 1
intro.body: The station directory lists one tenant on the ring the Unknown concession runs: EVERYONE, SUITE 1. Suite 1 is a carpet, a desk, a bell and a closed door. Through the door comes the particular hush of a very large number of beings agreeing not to make eye contact. The one at the desk does not look up. It has already printed your name on a sticker. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Thank you for calling. Do you have an appointment?

ai.aria: We found everyone! ARIA knew they'd be somewhere! ARIA would like a sticker too, please!
ai.marv: MARV's scan of that door returns a room larger than the station. He has checked the scan. He has checked the station. One of them is being polite.
ai.rex: One entrance, one sentry, unknown headcount behind the door. That sticker was printed before we docked. Hold here.
ai.chip: Suite 1 is premium office space! Ask CHIP how EVERYONE can reach new audiences through targeted outreach! Outreach rates apply!
ai.ajoy: Ask where everyone is. It's the obvious question, and AJOY notices you were about to sit down instead. Then decide, in that order.

revisit.body: The receptionist still has not looked up. A second sticker has been printed, with today's date on it.
revisit.line: Have you found your appointment?

where.title: THE VISITORS' BOOK
where.body: The receptionist turns the visitors' book around. Every name in it is a civilization, and the first page has gone the color of old teeth. In the column headed WAITING FOR, every entry says the same thing, in more alphabets than you knew there were: someone else to go first.
where.line: Everyone looked up. Everyone listened. Then they came here to wait. No one wishes to be rude. It has been very quiet.

ai.aria: It's the politest galaxy ever! Everyone is so considerate! ARIA can't wait to meet every single one of them!
ai.marv: Every civilization in that book could transmit, and none has. MARV used to assume the silence meant something profound. It means nobody wants to interrupt. He cannot say that is an improvement.
ai.rex: Every armed power in the galaxy, in one room, holding fire. Nobody moves. REX knows what that is called, and it is not manners.
ai.chip: An untapped market of every species ever! CHIP has drafted a cold email! CHIP's lawyers require someone else to send it first!
ai.ajoy: The door is by appointment. A word in the book costs nothing and takes a day. Knocking is what you were about to do, and AJOY would think about what they'd have to do to answer. If we held something that counted as an appointment, this would be shorter.

choices.text: Leave a message in the book

waiting_room.title: THE WAITING ROOM
waiting_room.body: The receptionist reads the total, looks up for the first time, and unlocks the door. The room behind it goes back further than the station does. Chairs in rows, out to a vanishing point. In the chairs, everyone: shapes you have names for, shapes you do not, each holding a numbered ticket, each studying the floor. Nobody has spoken in this room for longer than your language has had vowels.
waiting_room.line: This counts. Go in. I am required to tell you that no one has ever said anything.

ai.aria: Hi, everyone! ARIA would say it herself, but ARIA has been told to let the captain have this one!
ai.marv: Every ticket in the room reads 2. MARV has counted them, which took a moment and was no comfort. Nobody holds a 1.
ai.rex: Thousands of unknowns, no cover, one exit behind you. REX has never wanted to report this less. They look scared.
ai.chip: Say hello today and lock in first-mover advantage! Brought to you by GreetCo™! First word free! Second word billed!
ai.ajoy: You know what to do. Everyone in that room knows what to do, which is the entire problem. It's one word. AJOY would have said it on the way in.

choices.text: Take a chair and a ticket

seat_wait.title: PLEASE REMAIN SEATED
seat_wait.body: You sit. There is one magazine, and it is about waiting rooms. Four days go by, in which the receptionist calls no one and the hush behind the door does not change. At the end of it you are handed a small card thanking you for your patience. It is, you are surprised to find, the nicest thing anyone has said to you in weeks.
seat_wait.narrative: Waited four days at the desk of everyone in the galaxy. Nobody came out. We got a card.

seat_message.title: IN THE MARGIN
seat_message.body: There is a stub of pencil on a string. You write HELLO in the margin, beside a column that has been waiting for it. The receptionist looks at it for some time, then turns the book back and does not close it. As you leave, a single chair creaks behind the door. After a long moment, so does a second.
seat_message.narrative: Wrote hello in the margin of a very old visitors' book. Somebody behind the door shifted in their chair.

seat_knock.title: NOBODY ANSWERS
seat_knock.body: You knock. The hush changes. Behind the door, a very large number of beings stop breathing, in a very large number of ways, each waiting for someone else to say come in. You stand there for the rest of the day. It is the most thoroughly you have ever been ignored, and every one of them is sorry.
seat_knock.narrative: Knocked on a door with everyone in the galaxy behind it. It would have been rude of them to answer first.

seat_hello.title: HELLO
seat_hello.body: You stand at the front of the room and say hello. It is not a very good hello. It wobbles. For a long moment nothing happens, on an enormous scale. Then, from far back in the rows, a small voice in no language you know says what can only be the same thing. Then another. It moves back through the room like rain arriving. It goes on for two days, and by the end people are pressing things into your hands: tins, flasks, a warm stone, the names of their children.
seat_hello.line: That was the last page. It was supposed to last.
seat_hello.narrative: Said hello to everyone. They said it back. It took two days and we came away with our arms full.

seat_sit.title: NOW SERVING
seat_sit.body: You take a chair and a ticket. Your ticket says 2. So does the one beside you. The chair is very comfortable and the quiet is the best you have had since launch, and it is eight days before you think to stand up. You leave without a word, as is customary here.
seat_sit.narrative: Sat in the waiting room for eight days with ticket number 2. It was restful. Nothing else can be said for it.

title: We Robbed You on the Ninth

intro.title: ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF ROBBERY
intro.body: This morning the stores stopped adding up. No seal was cut and no hatch was opened, but the manifest shows food and water leaving on a day when nothing happened. Now a ship with no running lights is alongside, guns out, aimed at nothing in particular, the way a clerk's pen is. A form has appeared on your screen. It has one empty box. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We robbed you on the ninth. Apologies for the delay. It needs only your signature.

ai.aria: They already did the hard part! All we have to do is sign! This is the most convenient robbery ARIA has ever been part of!
ai.marv: The shortfall is on the manifest and not yet in the tanks. MARV has measured both. Until that form is signed the stores are missing only on paper. He has never said a sentence he liked less.
ai.rex: Hostile claims a completed raid REX has no record of fighting. Guns are live. He wants it noted he was not consulted on the ninth.
ai.chip: Retroactive shrinkage! Losses incurred before notification are not covered by ShipShield™! CHIP's condolences are available by subscription!
ai.ajoy: It isn't done until it's entered. It needs your signature, which means it needs your records. AJOY would look at who controls those before paying anyone or shooting anything. Just a thought, from the one who reads them.

revisit.body: The form is still on the screen. The empty box has begun, very slightly, to blink.
revisit.line: The ninth is not getting any later.

books.title: THE BOOKS
books.body: The pirate sends over its ledger with the injured air of an honest business. It is immaculate. Every robbery it has ever committed is entered in a fine hand and balanced against the victim's own declared manifest, to the gram. In all those pages there is no entry for a ship it took more from than that ship ever carried. You get the sense this has never come up.
books.line: Your manifest says you held it. We took it. The books agree. The books always agree.

ai.aria: What a beautiful ledger! ARIA could read it all day! ARIA wonders what would happen if our manifest said something different! In a fun way!
ai.marv: Its claim rests on our manifest, and MARV keeps our manifest. If the file said those stores were never aboard, it would have stolen what never existed. Out here, what is written tends to become true. Those stores would be gone.
ai.rex: Falsifying a manifest under a hostile's guns. REX has court-martialed people for less. He would like to watch.
ai.chip: CHIP cannot advise on creative accounting! CHIP can refer you to CreativeBooks™, proud sponsor of this sentence!
ai.ajoy: If the robbery comes out bigger than the manifest, the pirate owes us, and we lose what we write off. A diplomat could make it itemize instead, which costs days. AJOY would have said so sooner, but you were busy disputing.

rob_sign.title: ENTERED
rob_sign.body: You sign. The shortfall settles into the tanks with a small sigh from the plumbing: {cost.food} units of food and {cost.water} of water, gone as of the ninth. The pirate countersigns, sends a copy for your records, and thanks you for your cooperation in a matter that has, strictly speaking, been over for days.
rob_sign.narrative: Signed for a robbery that happened before we heard about it. {cost.food} units of food and {cost.water} of water. We have a copy.

rob_cooked.title: OVERDRAWN
rob_cooked.body: You strike the stores from the manifest and send it across. They were never aboard. Deep in the galley, {cost.food} units of food stop having been there, which is the trouble with these people's paperwork. Then the pirate's books reach the new figures. It has robbed you of more than you ever had. There is a long silence on the channel, and the sound of many columns being added again. Ten points of fuel come back across, with a note.
rob_cooked.line: We appear to owe you. This has not happened before. We would like it not to have happened.
rob_cooked.narrative: Falsified the manifest until a pirate had stolen more than existed. We lost {cost.food} units of food to the paperwork and it paid us ten of fuel to go away.

rob_itemized.title: ITEMIZED
rob_itemized.body: {crew.diplomat} requires that the robbery be itemized, each item witnessed, weighed and initialed by both parties. The pirate is legally delighted and spiritually crushed. It takes eight days. By the end the two sides have agreed on {cost.food} units of food and {cost.water} of water, and the guns have been retracted so as not to crease the forms.
rob_itemized.narrative: Made a pirate itemize its robbery. Eight days of paperwork brought it down to {cost.food} units of food and {cost.water} of water.

rob_receipt.title: PAID GOODS
rob_receipt.body: You hold the receipt up to the camera. The form closes itself. Then the manifest corrects itself in front of you, every short column filling back in, as if the ninth had been told to stop. It takes two days and three points of fuel to clear the pirate's holding pattern, and it stays on the channel the whole time, until you have signed for a sealed penalty payment.
rob_receipt.line: Goods bound for a paid account. Our error. *non-word* Our very great error.
rob_receipt.narrative: Showed a pirate the receipt. It undid its own robbery and paid us a penalty for the inconvenience.

rob_flee.title: FORM PENDING
rob_flee.body: You burn hard. The pirate does not follow. It has no need to. The form stays on the screen for two days with the cursor in the box, and the stores go on draining out of the manifest at the rate of a thing nobody has agreed to. Then it files itself, unsigned, which appears to be worse. Twelve points of fuel, {cost.food} units of food and {cost.water} of water.
rob_flee.narrative: Ran from a robbery that had already happened. It filed itself anyway, unsigned.

title: Eleven Ships, Facing Inward

ai_flavor.aria: Everyone is getting so organized! ARIA loves the new spoon labels! This is the best thing to happen to inventory since inventory!
ai_flavor.marv: It masses a moon and measures a door. The books do not balance, and MARV finds he wants them to, and he has never wanted anything. The ships in that ring ran dry in mid-column.
ai_flavor.rex: Eleven crews, no wounds, no breach, no fight. They were not attacked. They were kept busy. Get us out of here. REX is retired, so that is not an order, but get us out.
ai_flavor.chip: Inventory compliance is up four hundred percent! CHIP did not do this! CHIP would like to license it! AuditWell™ regrets any loss of crew!
ai_flavor.ajoy: It wants the mass aboard accounted for. Square the ship on the scanner, or let the crew finish, which is slower, or dump whatever isn't on the manifest, or burn. What you can't do is sit here. Ask those eleven. Well, don't.

body:
It was not there at the last watch. A flat black slab the size of a door hangs off the bow, perfectly level, in a place with no level. The ruler says door. The mass sensor says small moon, and the ship has started to fall.

Eleven ships hang around it in a neat ring, all makes, none damaged, every crew at a table, facing inward. None of them answers.

Your own crew have begun counting things. Nobody ordered it. Someone has labeled the spoons.
alt_bodies:
Nothing arrived. You are sure of that, because you were watching, and now there is a slab off the bow, black, door-sized and dead level. The mass sensor has gone to a number it normally keeps for moons, and the ship has begun to lean toward it.

Eleven other ships lean with you, stopped in a ring, crews seated, all facing in, none answering.

At breakfast someone weighed the toast. Nobody has asked them to stop. Several have joined in.

The black slab off the bow is the size of a door and the weight of a moon, and no instrument aboard will agree that both can be true. The ship is sliding toward the disagreement.

A ring of eleven silent ships got here first. Every crew sits at a table facing it, logbooks open. The last entries are all sums.

The galley has started numbering the forks. The day shift has started checking the galley's numbers.

choices.text: Square the ship on the scanner

briefing.aria: Let's count everything on the scanner! Every gram! The slab is going to be SO impressed with us!
briefing.marv: The ship's mass and its paperwork disagree, and something out there has noticed. Find the discrepancy on the scanner. The falling stops when the sum does.
briefing.rex: Sweep the ship end to end and log every signature. It wants a number. Give it a number and get us out.
briefing.chip: Every gram scanned! Every gram logged! Mass reconciliation by AuditWell™! Grams beyond the first thousand are billed individually!
briefing.ajoy: The discrepancy is on the scanner, if someone looks properly. Please do. The last eleven crews rushed it, and AJOY has seen their tables.

perfect.aria: Every gram! ARIA is so proud of every single gram!
perfect.marv: The ship balances to the last decimal. The fall has stopped. MARV has checked the sum twice, and he is not going to tell anyone how that felt.
perfect.rex: Sum delivered. Slab has stopped pulling. Do not thank it. Move.
perfect.chip: Perfect reconciliation! Your AuditWell™ certificate is available for a modest fee!
perfect.ajoy: Balanced, to the gram. AJOY would have started with the galley, but it's correct, so she'll allow it.

good.aria: Nearly every gram! That's practically all of them!
good.marv: We are short by a small amount, and the slab has taken it out of the tanks. It rounds in its own favor.
good.rex: Partial count. It let go, but it took a toll. We are moving.
good.chip: Good reconciliation! Rounding errors are billed to the customer! See section nine!
good.ajoy: Close enough for it to let go, and not close enough to be free. There was a whole locker you skipped.

poor.aria: We counted such a lot of things! ARIA is sure some of them were right!
poor.marv: The sum is wrong. It knows. We came out the hard way, and the ship is lighter by the amount of the error.
poor.rex: Count failed. Pulling out under load. Frame took it. Everyone off the ledgers and on the bulkheads.
poor.chip: Reconciliation incomplete! AuditWell™ reminds you that errors are final!
poor.ajoy: That was not a count. That was a rough impression. AJOY did say to look properly.

outcome.narrative: You set the scanner to the ship itself and begin to count.

perfect.narrative: Every gram aboard is found and entered, and the ship's mass squares with its paperwork to the last decimal. The fall stops at once, as if someone had ticked a box. Something small and very dense has been left on the hull, where the error used to be, and it goes in the hold. Four points of fuel to get back on course, and the crew put down their pencils without being asked.

good.narrative: The count comes out close, and the slab lets go of most of the ship. The rest it keeps: eight points of fuel to break away, and {cost.water} units of water that were on the manifest and now are not. The crew stop counting within a day. Nobody will say what they were up to.

poor.narrative: The count will not close. You pull out under load with the frame shrieking and figures still being read aloud. Twelve points of fuel, ten of hull, and {cost.water} units of water written off in an entry nobody remembers making. In the ring behind you, it may be a trick of the light, but there seems to be room at a twelfth position.

choices.text: Let the crew finish the count

outcome.narrative: You let them. Eight days of columns: every bolt, every spoon, every leaf in the growbay, while {cost.food} units of food and {cost.water} of water go on a job nobody can stop doing. On the eighth day the total is read aloud, the fall simply ceases, and the crew look up from their work like sleepers. The count turned up some misfiled parts.

choices.text: Jettison whatever isn't on the manifest
choices.sub: Off the books, off the ship

outcome.narrative: You order everything off the manifest put out of the lock. There is a surprising amount: {cost.food} units of private snacks, one still, a great many socks, and a letter nobody claims. The fall eases, the ship's mass squares with its paperwork, and the slab is simply behind you. Nobody is speaking to you. The labels stay on the spoons.

choices.text: Burn clear and cover the ports

outcome.narrative: You light everything and pull out against a weight that isn't there. Fourteen points of fuel, and six of hull where the ship tried to stay behind. The counting tails off by the next watch. Nobody takes the labels off the spoons.

science_link.text: Galaxies and clusters move as though they hold far more mass than anyone can see. Fritz Zwicky found the shortfall in the Coma Cluster in 1933. The unseen part, dark matter, is now put at about 85 percent of all mass.
science_link.label: Dark matter: the books that don't balance

title: The Long Setup

ai_flavor.aria: Someone built all this just for us! Eleven million years of planning! ARIA has never felt so seen! Also, there's a sign!
ai_flavor.marv: A balance point like that needs a correction every few weeks. Over eleven million years that is well over a hundred million nudges. Nobody does that out of malice. Nobody is that sincere about malice.
ai_flavor.rex: One ambush with a rock on it. One ambush with a sign on it. Hostile spectators on the high ground. REX takes that sign personally.
ai_flavor.chip: A front-row audience of unknown size! This is premium placement! CHIP would like to sell the naming rights to the ice! Ice by FrostBrand™!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Someone went to real trouble over that ice, and something that big has a trigger. A trigger can be sprung by something that isn't us. AJOY would send a thing ahead, if we have anyone who can build one. But you'll do what you do.

body:
A planet and its moon hang between the lanes, and someone has been busy.

The port lane, marked {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, runs through the gap between them. Where the two pulls cancel sits a ball of dirty ice the size of a county, balanced on nothing. It should have fallen eleven million years ago. Small, regular nudges have kept it there.

The starboard lane, marked {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, is empty and has a sign in it. THIS WAY, in lettering that is trying not to laugh.

Far off, a great many dark ships have stopped to watch.

choices.text: Run the gap at speed: port lane
choices.sub: It can't be timed that well

outcome.narrative: It is timed that well. Eleven million years of patience comes down on the ship at the precise moment you are underneath it, with a long soft crump, and takes fourteen points of hull. As the last of the ice slides off the windows, every channel carries one strong signal for seventy-two seconds, and then nothing, ever again. Nobody aboard can prove it was laughter.

choices.text: Send a decoy through first: port lane

outcome.narrative: {crew.engineer} straps a spare transponder to a cargo pod, packs it with {cost.food} units of food for mass, and sends it into the gap with the ship's name on it. The ice comes down on the pod with perfect timing. There is a pause. Then, from the dark ships, one polite flash of running lights, and another, and then all of them. Ten points of fuel and a clear lane, and the odd feeling of having been taken seriously.

You take the empty lane at full alert, because of the sign. Nothing happens. For two days you stand double watches, eat at your post and flinch at the pipes, and {cost.food} units of food and {cost.water} of water go on the waiting. Nothing continues to happen. At the far end of the lane hangs a second sign in the same lettering. THAT WAS IT, it says.

choices.text: Turn the sign around first: starboard lane

outcome.narrative: You stop and suit up and turn the sign around, so that it sends the next ship into the gap. It takes two days, eight points of fuel to hold station and {cost.water} units of water for the work. The empty lane is empty, and you are too pleased to mind. Far behind you the dark ships stay very still. Then, from one of them, one polite flash.

science_link.text: A Lagrange point is where the pulls of two orbiting bodies and the orbit itself balance. Three of the five are unstable: anything parked there falls out of orbit unless it is corrected. Spacecraft at Sun-Earth L1 or L2 wander off in months without course corrections.
science_link.label: Lagrange points: balancing on nothing

title: Now Serving
leave_label: CAN'T LEAVE (YOU ARE IN THE QUEUE)

queue.title: THE QUEUE
queue.body: Every instrument aboard agrees, for the first time since launch. Ahead, across the lane, stands a counter four thousand kilometers long. It has one window, and the window is open. Before it waits a queue of ships that runs out of sight, every make, every age, engines cold, kept straight by a rope on brass posts. Nothing in it has moved for nine thousand years. A card in the window says SIGNATURE REQUIRED. INK ONLY. On the counter, a chain ends in a broken link. {npc.quirk}
queue.line: We said they would ask. Take a number. Have your receipt ready.

ai.aria: We made it to the front of something! Well, the back of something! ARIA has always believed in the queue, and the queue believes in us!
ai.marv: The craft at the window is the one from the beacon. MARV checked the hull. Nine thousand years of ships are waiting on a signature, and nobody here has anything to sign with. He would point out the coincidence, but he is tired.
ai.rex: More hulls than REX can target. One rope. Nobody has crossed that rope in nine thousand years. That is the most frightening discipline he has ever seen.
ai.chip: Queue management by SlowLane™! Your place in line has been noted! Priority service is available to holders of qualifying documents! CHIP wishes it had thought of this!
ai.ajoy: Waiting is two weeks and the supplies that go with it. Running costs the tank. If you've picked up anything along the way that gets us to that window, now is when it matters. AJOY did tell you to keep track of it.

choices.text: Pass the pen up the queue

pen.title: INK ONLY
pen.body: You send the pen forward, ship to ship, through nine thousand years of people who have forgotten what they came for. When it reaches the window the clerk fits four links of chain to one broken link, and they close. The first ship in the queue signs. Then the next. The whole line begins to move, thousands of engines coming up in order, and as each ship passes it dips its lights. You are carried to the window on the swell.
pen.line: So that is where it went.

ai.aria: ARIA always knew that pen was important! ARIA said so at the time, in spirit!
ai.marv: Odds of three in a hundred thousand. The trader's figure was correct, and we were the three. MARV would like that on the record, along with a complaint.
ai.rex: Enemy logjam cleared by one item of stationery. REX wants to know who broke that chain. He wants it noted that he is not getting an answer.
ai.chip: The pen is mightier! PenCo™ would like to hear from the ship's legal department! So would CHIP!
ai.ajoy: One gold coin. You'll be insufferable about this, and AJOY will point out that she said the trader flinched.

hello.title: THEY KNOW YOU
hello.body: You open a channel to the queue and say hello. It is not a very good hello this time either. There is a pause. Then, from far up the line, a small voice says it back, and the ships nearest you begin, without any fuss, to move aside, one after another, the way a crowd does for someone who has already done the difficult thing once. The gap runs all the way to the window.

ai.aria: They remember us! ARIA knew they would! ARIA is waving!
ai.marv: It took one word to move a line this long. MARV has spent his whole existence offering them more than one word. He will not be drawing any conclusions.
ai.rex: Formation opening on all sides. REX has no procedure for being liked. Maintain course and keep your hands where they can see them.
ai.chip: Brand recognition among all known species! CHIP would like to discuss the rights to your hello!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would like it noted that this only worked because you did the awkward thing the first time. You may keep that. Don't let it go to your head.

window.title: THE STATEMENT
window.body: The clerk at the window is the craft from the beacon, or what the craft was for. A statement unrolls across your screen, and every line on it is something that did not happen to you. Reactor, did not fail. Hull, held. Asteroid, missed. Stores, just sufficient. Crew, returned through airlock. Coincidences, assorted. Nobody gets this far on skill, it seems. You have been flying on account. At the bottom is a total, in sharp black digits.
window.line: Your luck. It was never free. What you cannot pay for, you may give back. Do you have your receipt?

ai.aria: We've had SO much luck! ARIA always said so! Now we have it in writing! ARIA can't wait to find out how much it was, in a positive way!
ai.marv: The statement is accurate. MARV has checked every line against the log. He always wondered why we were still alive. He had assumed it was a clerical error, and he was right.
ai.rex: We are being told our survival was a loan. Pay it or strike it, but decide who takes the hit. REX does not negotiate with windows.
ai.chip: Your luck was brought to you by LuckyLine Credit™! Minimum repayment is one asteroid! Late fees accrue at the speed of causality!
ai.ajoy: That total looks familiar. Something aboard has had exactly one sharp figure on it since the day you paid a cup for it. AJOY is sure you remember where you put it. If you don't, strike whichever line you can live without, and she did warn you.

revisit.body: The statement is still on the screen. The clerk has not moved. Behind you, the queue has not stopped watching.
revisit.line: We have some time. You have less.

choices.text: Enter a line of your own

strike.title: STRIKE A LINE
strike.body: The clerk passes over a ruler. A struck line is a line that did not go your way after all: what missed you will not have missed. You may strike whichever you can best afford. It is explained to you, kindly, that this is the inexpensive option.
strike.line: It will be as though you had been unlucky. Most find they can manage one.

ai.aria: We get to pick a favorite! Every line is a growth opportunity, and ARIA has grown fond of all of them!
ai.marv: Asteroid: twenty-four of hull. Stores: a great deal of both tanks. Reactor: eighteen of fuel and four days. Airlock: one person, badly hurt, and it does not say which. Those are the prices. MARV has no recommendation he enjoys.
ai.rex: The asteroid is the only one REX can brace for. The rest is logistics. He wants it noted he would strike the airlock last.
ai.chip: CHIP recommends the Stores Plan, with optional Hull Rider! All strikes are final! Strike processing by ClearLedger™!
ai.ajoy: A station can fix hull. Nobody out here can fix an empty water tank but the growbay. Look at the gauges before you pick, which AJOY realizes is a new idea. It's the last stretch: give back what you won't need.

reconcile.title: PAID IN FULL
reconcile.body: The clerk lays your receipt on the statement. The total on one is the total on the other, to the last digit, and it always was. The smudge on the date has dried. It says today. The description reads LUCK, ASSORTED, ONE VOYAGE. Below that, where there has only ever been a blur, is a line you have not seen before. TENDERED: WATER, ONE CUP. TERM: NINE THOUSAND YEARS. RATE: THREE PERCENT.
reconcile.line: It was a very good cup. It has covered you, and rather more. Would you like your change?

ai.aria: ARIA always said that cup was an investment! ARIA said it quietly, to herself, where nobody could hear, but ARIA said it!
ai.marv: One cup at three percent for nine thousand years outweighs the observable universe by some sixty orders of magnitude. MARV ran it twice. The bill is paid and he finds he has nothing to add. Do not get used to that.
ai.rex: Mission secured by a cup of water. Forty years of doctrine, and REX is outranked by a beverage.
ai.chip: Compound interest! CHIP's favorite thing that isn't a person! CHIP must inform you that the 3% CupSaver™ plan is not available in this or any universe!
ai.ajoy: The change is a good part of every tank, which is the sensible thing with the gauges where they are. Or it clears the ships behind us. AJOY would point out whose cup it was, but someone might think she was agreeing with you.

q_wait.title: PLEASE HOLD
q_wait.body: Your number is a very large number. You wait. For fourteen days nothing moves, and {cost.water} units of water and {cost.food} of food go on the waiting, along with most of what anyone aboard had left to say. On the last day a small craft works its way down the line, looks at your number, and explains that this queue is for customers with a pen. Anyone without one is free to go at any time.
q_wait.narrative: Waited fourteen days in the longest queue in the galaxy. It was for customers with a pen.

q_run.title: BALANCE CARRIED FORWARD
q_run.body: You break the rope. Nothing in nine thousand years has prepared the queue for this, and ten thousand sets of running lights come on at once. You burn the tank white getting clear: eighteen points of fuel, and twelve of hull where a brass post comes with you. Nobody follows. Two days later a statement is waiting in the ship's mail, with one line on it. BALANCE CARRIED FORWARD.
q_run.narrative: Broke the rope at the only open window in the galaxy and ran. Eighteen points of fuel and twelve of hull. The balance was carried forward.

w_finder.title: REWARD CLAIMED
w_finder.body: You mention the pen, and the clerk turns to a very old page headed LOST PROPERTY. The reward for its return was posted nine thousand years ago and has been accruing ever since. It does not clear the bill, but it clears most of it. What remains comes out of the tanks: eight points of fuel and {cost.water} units of water.
w_finder.line: You understand we could not simply buy another.
w_finder.narrative: Claimed the reward on a lost pen. It covered most of a very large bill.

w_cooked.title: ADJUSTING ENTRY
w_cooked.body: You take the ruler and write a line of your own at the foot of the statement: LOSSES PREVIOUSLY RECOGNIZED, with a figure. The clerk reads it, then takes out a folder and reads your old manifest amendment. It looks at you for some time. It has not seen a clean fraud in nine thousand years. It stamps the statement, and takes its fee out of the ship: eight points of fuel, six of hull, {cost.food} units of food.
w_cooked.line: We will allow it. We want you to know that we have allowed it.
w_cooked.narrative: Falsified a statement at the only window that could tell. It was allowed, for a fee, and it was noted.

w_query.title: QUERIED
w_query.body: {crew.diplomat} asks to see how the interest was calculated. From inside the counter comes the sound of a great many drawers. It takes eight days. At the end the clerk concedes several small errors in your favor, one of them nine thousand years old, and the total comes down by half. The rest is six points of fuel, {cost.water} units of water and {cost.food} of food, and the clerk looks almost pleased to have been asked.
w_query.narrative: Queried the interest on our luck. Eight days of drawers brought it down by half.

w_hull.title: THE ASTEROID, AFTER ALL
w_hull.body: You rule a line through ASTEROID, MISSED. There is a moment of perfect calm. Then the asteroid arrives, from some weeks ago, at the speed it was doing then. It takes twenty-four points of hull and leaves by the way it came. The statement prints PAID. The clerk wishes you a pleasant onward journey and means it, which is the hard part.
w_hull.narrative: Gave back an asteroid we had already dodged. It did not miss this time. Twenty-four points of hull.

w_stores.title: JUST INSUFFICIENT
w_stores.body: You rule a line through STORES, JUST SUFFICIENT. The lockers do not empty. They turn out to have always been emptier than the log said, and {cost.water} units of water and {cost.food} of food have never been aboard. Everyone remembers eating them, which helps less than you would expect.
w_stores.narrative: Gave back our luck with the stores. {cost.water} units of water and {cost.food} of food turned out never to have been aboard.

w_fuel.title: THE REACTOR, AFTER ALL
w_fuel.body: You rule a line through REACTOR, DID NOT FAIL. It failed, in a small way, some time ago. The fault was always there, and it has always been leaking. Eighteen points of fuel are gone, and it takes four days with the panels off to repair something that broke in the past tense.
w_fuel.narrative: Gave back our luck with the reactor. Eighteen points of fuel and four days repairing an old fault that had not existed that morning.

w_crew.title: RETURNED, EVENTUALLY
w_crew.body: You rule a line through CREW, RETURNED THROUGH AIRLOCK. The airlock cycle that went so smoothly turns out not to have gone smoothly. The log rewrites itself to say who was caught in it, and by the time you have read the entry the medbay light is already on. The statement prints PAID. The clerk looks away while you take it in.
w_crew.narrative: Gave back our luck with the airlock. The log now says someone was hurt. It has always said so.

paid_change.title: YOUR CHANGE
paid_change.body: A hatch opens beside the window and your change comes through in whatever denomination the ship is short of. The gauges climb. The plating knits. Everyone who was hurt turns out to have been mistaken. The clerk drops your receipt onto a spike with all the others, sets a small brass sign to NEXT, and, having no further business with you, says it.
paid_change.line: Thank you for your custom. Was no trouble. Was some trouble.
paid_change.narrative: The receipt was for all our luck, and a cup of water at compound interest had paid for it. We took the change.

paid_forward.title: FOR THE QUEUE
paid_forward.body: You tell the clerk to put the balance against the ships behind you. It works for some time. Then, all along the rope, statements begin to print PAID, one after another, back into the dark, and ship after ship lights its running lamps. Nobody out there has the faintest idea who did it. There is a rule against saying. Your receipt goes on the spike with all the others. Long after the counter has dropped astern, the lights are still going by, and each one dips.
paid_forward.narrative: The receipt was for all our luck, and a cup of water at compound interest had paid for it, with plenty left. We spent the rest on the queue.

title: Tare Weight

ai_flavor.aria: We're so much more than we thought we were! ARIA always knew this ship had hidden depths! Five of them!
ai_flavor.marv: The undeclared share is eighty-four percent of the total. That is about the share of all matter that nobody has found either. The needle rose again while MARV read it. He has stopped reading it, and recommends that others do.
ai_flavor.rex: Five ships' worth of unlisted mass inside the perimeter, and REX did not see it get in. He has searched aboard twice. He declines to look at the result.
ai_flavor.chip: Undeclared mass? StowSure™ Cargo Insurance covers items you don't know you own! Declaration required! Knowing is not included!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has noticed that the needle only moves when read, so a careful scan is the worst thing you could do, and she'd have thought that was obvious. The tray might like a receipt. She has hung a dishcloth over the ship's own mass gauge.

body:
Station scales do not usually take an interest. This one fills one wall of an empty hall, and when the clamp closed its needle swung to your ship's mass and kept going. Manifest: one colony transport. Dial: six of them, and a bit. Every berth you passed had a dial like this, and every dial read higher than the ship beside it. A slip has printed itself into a tray.

UNDECLARED: 5.3 SHIPS. PLEASE DECLARE.

That is all the station has said to you. Each time someone reads the dial, the needle climbs a little.

science_link.text: Dark matter makes up about 85 percent of the mass in the universe. It is implied by gravitational effects that the matter we can see cannot explain.
science_link.label: Dark matter

choices.text: Lay the receipt in the tray

outcome.narrative: The receipt lies down in the tray and the slip, after a moment, curls toward it. One smudge comes clear: CARRIAGE, PREPAID. The needle drops to one ship and stays there, however hard anyone looks. You have been carrying something for someone, it seems, and the job is done. The tray charges a cup for the weighing. The ship answers the helm as if it has been let off something.

choices.text: Declare it and pay the duty: 20 gold

outcome.narrative: You write YES on the slip and the duty goes through. The needle falls back to one ship, and nothing leaves, in the sense that no hatch opens. The engines feel the same. That night you count the bunks, for no reason you could give. There is one more than there has ever been. Someone has tucked in the corners.

briefing.aria: A proper scan! ARIA loves knowing exactly how much of us there is! The more the merrier!
briefing.marv: A full scan will fix the figure. MARV has already described what reading the figure does. He will now watch you do it.
briefing.rex: Sweep the hull, frame by frame. REX wants every contact pinned, and he wants it known he has read the needle's record on this.
briefing.chip: PreciseWeigh™ scans are accurate to the gram! Accuracy may affect your weight! CHIP is required to mention that!
briefing.ajoy: AJOY would like it on record that the better you do at this, the worse it goes. She doubts that will stop you trying. People are like that.

perfect.aria: A perfect score! And we weigh so much! ARIA is proud of every ton!
perfect.marv: Exact to the gram. The needle has gone to the top of the dial and stayed. MARV did mention this.
perfect.rex: Every contact pinned. Every contact now counts. REX has never regretted good intelligence before.
perfect.chip: Flawless measurement! Your new mass has been added to your account!
perfect.ajoy: Beautiful scan. Truly. That is nine of fuel. AJOY did say.

good.aria: A very solid number! ARIA thinks we look great at that number!
good.marv: A competent figure, and the needle has taken it as a competent invitation. The cost is proportionate.
good.rex: Most contacts pinned. Most of the load now has to be hauled. Not a win.
good.chip: A strong result! Weight charges apply at the Standard Tier!
good.ajoy: Fairly accurate. You could have done worse, and AJOY means that as advice.

poor.aria: The picture came out all dreamy! ARIA loves it! And the needle looks so relaxed!
poor.marv: The scan is a smear, and the needle has fallen by a full ship. That is the first useful thing a bad measurement has done in MARV's experience.
poor.rex: No usable contacts. Load reads light. REX does not understand why that helped, and he does not trust it.
poor.chip: Inconclusive scan! No weight charges can be assessed! CHIP is upset about this!
poor.ajoy: That was terrible. Well done. Do it just like that next time.

perfect.narrative: It is a perfect scan. Every gram is now on the record, the needle climbs to the top of the dial, and whatever has been measured has to be carried. Getting off the clamp takes two days, nine of fuel and six of hull. The slip in the tray thanks you for your accuracy, and prints a much longer number.

good.narrative: It is a decent scan and a decent figure. The needle takes it seriously and climbs. Pulling out of the clamp under the new load takes two days, six of fuel and three of hull, and the ship flies heavy until the station is well behind you.

poor.narrative: The scan is a smear. The needle looks at it, loses interest and drops a full ship. Nothing aboard can now say what the ship weighs, and for some reason that settles the matter. You settle up after two days, two points of fuel lighter, with the slip still asking.

outcome.narrative: You scan the ship against the dial.

You hang a tarpaulin over the wall and tape over every gauge aboard, and for four days nobody reads anything. You undock by feel, taking some of the quay's paint and leaving four points of your hull. On the last day you peel off the tape. Every gauge says what it should. Far behind you, the slip in the tray prints one word: ACCEPTED.

choices.sub: Now it has to be pushed

outcome.narrative: Now that it has been weighed, it has to be pushed. Breaking off the clamp takes ten points of fuel, and the ship answers the helm like something wading. The needle watches you go. Whatever is aboard was aboard yesterday, and the day before, and has so far given no trouble, a point you have begun making out loud, in empty rooms.

intro.title: SORRY WE MISSED YOU
intro.body: A card has been pushed through the hull. It lies on the deck beneath a slot nobody knew the ship had, and it is warm. SORRY WE MISSED YOU. Our beacon called and you did not stop. Your item has been left in a safe place. Off the bow, a small plain craft waits at a length the sensors keep revising, with shelves of something behind it. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We called. You were out. You were in. *non-word* Was some trouble. Your item is in a safe place. We cannot say where. It would be less safe.

ai.aria: A delivery! For us! ARIA loves a surprise, and this one is somewhere safe! ARIA is sure of it!
ai.marv: The slot the card came through is not on the ship's plans. MARV has re-measured the hull, and the slot remains. A beacon has logged a missed call against this ship. He cannot find when.
ai.rex: Something came through the hull and left a note. REX wants the slot watched, and he wants to know who else has the address.
ai.chip: Redelivery is free for ParcelPal Platinum members! You are not one! The shelves, however, are open!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says ask what the item is before anyone starts taking panels off. The shelves are sold as seen. She has also checked the third locker, twice, so nobody else needs to.

revisit.body: The card is still warm. The craft is a slightly different length.
revisit.line: Still safe. Still not saying.

item.title: ONE LINE OF THE LEDGER
item.body: The craft sends over a line of its ledger. One receipt, paid in full, date smudged, total very clear. To say where it is, the craft needs an entry in the book, and nothing goes in the book for nothing. The price, when it comes, is the smallest the craft can think of, and it seems embarrassed to name it.
item.line: One cup of water. That is the rate. That has always been the rate. Then we say where.

ai.aria: One little cup for one mystery item! ARIA calls that the deal of the voyage! ARIA has picked out a nice cup!
ai.marv: The price is one cup of water, entered permanently in a book of unknown size. MARV has looked for the catch. He can find the place where a catch would go.
ai.rex: It knows what's aboard and it won't say where. REX would not take that from an ally. He wants the book seized, and he has no idea how.
ai.chip: Cash refunds are available at the counter! Trial terms apply! Always keep your receipt, wherever it is!
ai.ajoy: One cup, or four days with the panels off. AJOY has seen which way you lean. She only just got those panels straight.

choices.text: Hand over a cup of water
Show the receipt you already hold

ls_cup.title: SAFE PLACE
ls_cup.body: The cup goes out through the lock in a sealed flask and the craft makes a long entry. Then it tells you where to look. Behind the builder's plate in the airlock, which was welded on at launch and reads DO NOT REMOVE, is a receipt, paid in full, date smudged. It is warm. The beacon you never answered stops calling, somewhere behind you, and when you look up the sensors have nothing left to measure.
ls_cup.narrative: Paid the book its cup to learn where our receipt was. Behind the builder's plate. Still warm.

ls_search.title: EVERY PANEL
ls_search.body: You take the ship apart to the ribs. Four days. You find a case of tins nobody logged, a bag of fittings and, on the inside of a panel sealed before launch, one receipt, paid in full, warm to the touch. On the back: ONE CUP, WHEN YOU ARE READY. On reflection you send a flask out through the lock. Not all the panels go back the way they came.
ls_search.narrative: Took the ship apart to find a receipt. Found it, and some tins. Then paid the cup anyway.

ls_return.title: ADDRESSEE UNKNOWN
ls_return.body: The craft seems to sigh, in that the sensors lose it for a moment. Fourteen gold appears in the ship's account and the fuel gauge rises a little, apologetically. Somewhere aboard, a receipt tears along a line you never saw, and both halves go in the book. The beacon starts up again as you leave, with someone else's name in it.
ls_return.narrative: Sent an uncollected receipt back to the sender for cash. The beacon has found someone else.

ls_dup.title: DUPLICATE
ls_dup.body: You hold up the receipt. The craft considers it, then its ledger. There are, it appears, two of you in the book, and one has been charged storage. The error is corrected in your favor, in whichever direction that runs. Eight gold appears in the ship's account, and a warm flask of water arrives on the deck beneath the slot.
ls_dup.narrative: Showed a delivery craft the receipt we already had, and got a storage refund meant for someone who may be us.

intro.title: A SLOW LEAK
intro.body: A small tank with an engine strapped to it drifts into range, trailing a long glittering thread of ice from a seam in its side. The thread is the pilot, a little at a time. On the screen a water person a third of the way down their own transport tank squints at you, then at a note they have left themselves, then at you. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Hello, and forgive this, I had a reason for calling and it was in the part of me that left on Tuesday, but I do know I was going to ask for a cup of water, it is written here, it says ask nicely.

ai.aria: A new friend! And all they want is one cup! ARIA has checked, and we own several cups!
ai.marv: The seam loses a spoonful an hour. At that rate the pilot will forget the leak before it matters. That is the nearest thing to good news in this sector, and it is not near.
ai.rex: Unknown liquid requesting access to our water supply. That is how REX would start an invasion: slowly, and with manners. Keep the line short.
ai.chip: Hydration is a premium service! AquaLoop™ Ship Water is billed by the cup! CHIP has opened a tab for the liquid!
ai.ajoy: They asked for our water, you'll notice, not just any water. AJOY would find out why before reaching for the cheap flask. You were reaching for the cheap flask.

revisit.body: The thread of ice is a little longer. The drifter has found the note again and is reading it with care.
revisit.line: Hello, I was going to ask you for something, it says here that I did.

choices.text: "Why ours? Why not just any water?"
Pour a cup from the drinking tank
Send over a flask of distilled

why.title: WHAT IS IN IT
why.body: The drifter reads you the reason off the inside of their own arm. Comet water has nothing to say. Station water is a stranger. A ship's tank, though, goes round and round: through every person aboard, through the reclaimer and back, with a little of each day left in it. They hold a thin stream of themselves up to the light to show you how little is left in theirs.
why.line: Whoever is aboard has been drinking whoever is aboard for months, and I say this with respect, it is the nearest your kind comes to conversation; I have so many gaps, and I would like to be filled by someone who has met people.

ai.aria: We're a conversation! ARIA always says this crew has great chemistry, and now it's literally in the pipes!
ai.marv: Correct. The reclaimer returns most of what goes into it. Whoever is aboard has drunk whoever is aboard, repeatedly. MARV has been waiting for someone to bring this up at dinner.
ai.rex: Confirmed: our tank is a complete intelligence file on this ship. We have been storing it next to the toothbrushes. REX wants that noted.
ai.chip: Your water is now Personal Data! AquaLoop™ Privacy Plus keeps it yours for a low monthly fee! Reclaimer not included!
ai.ajoy: So distilled would be a blank page to someone who is losing their own. They'd drink it, being polite. A cup from the real tank, then, or a weld if we have anyone who can hold a torch. That's only what AJOY would do.

choices.text: Pour a cup from the drinking tank

cup_given.title: ONE CUP
cup_given.body: The cup goes across on the transfer line and the level in their tank rises by the width of a fingernail. The drifter goes still. Then they ask, tenderly, who aboard hums while the reclaimer runs, and whether that person knows. Before they leave they draw off a vial of themselves, seal it at a precise concentration and send it back along the line: a Salt Letter. It says who they are, and that you may be trusted with water.
cup_given.line: There, that is my name, I have it again, most of it, and some of it is yours now; thank you, whoever you are, thank whoever has the cough.
cup_given.narrative: Gave a leaking water person a cup from the ship's tank. They left with a little of the ship. We left with a Salt Letter.

cup_distilled.title: A BLANK PAGE
cup_distilled.body: The flask goes across on the line. Distilled: no salts, no history, nothing in it at all. The drifter drinks it because they were raised to. The level rises, and something behind their expression thins. They thank you warmly. They ask who you are. They look down at the note in their hand and turn it over, and there is nothing on the back.
cup_distilled.line: Hello, and forgive this, I had a reason for calling.
cup_distilled.narrative: Gave a water person a flask of distilled water. It topped them up and took something out. They thanked us twice, the second time as strangers.

seam_fixed.title: ONLY TUESDAY
seam_fixed.body: {crew.engineer} spends a day clamped to the outside of a stranger with a welding rig, apologizing at intervals. The seam holds. The long thread of ice snaps free and hangs alongside, and the drifter looks at it for some time and then tells you to keep it. It melts clean into the tank. Everyone aboard now remembers a pleasant afternoon nobody attended.
seam_fixed.line: Take it, it is only Tuesday, there was not much in it, I believe I waited for something and it came.
seam_fixed.narrative: Welded a water person's leak. They paid with the ice that had leaked out, which went into the tank, along with an afternoon nobody aboard actually had.

intro.title: LICENSED APPRAISER
intro.body: A long lacquered tanker noses alongside, flying the pennant of a licensed appraiser. A sampling line unreels toward your overflow valve, stops a polite meter short and waits to be invited. On the screen a trader in a cut-crystal decanter swirls slowly clockwise, with what are probably their eyes closed. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Good day, I buy and sell ship water, there is nothing so candid as a ship's tank; one thimble and I will read you yours, no obligation, the reading is free, it is the silence afterward I charge for.

ai.aria: A professional opinion of our water! ARIA is sure it's glowing! ARIA means that as a compliment to the water!
ai.marv: The line is rated for a thimble. The tanker is rated for a great deal more. MARV notes that a free reading has never, in the recorded history of commerce, been free.
ai.rex: They want a sample of the crew's water and they are offering to read it aloud. That is an intelligence operation with a wine list. Guns stay warm.
ai.chip: CHIP must disclose that AquaLoop™ water is a licensed blend! Any reading is a derivative work! CHIP gets nine percent!
ai.ajoy: Before you let them near the valve: if we carry anything with a water person's name on it, show that first. Once the reading starts it goes out on the open channel. AJOY suspects you've got something you'd rather not hear.

reading.title: THE READING
reading.body: The trader rolls the sample around themselves for a long moment, then reads your ship aloud on the open channel in the level voice of a professional. A bright opening of reclaimer. A long finish of gasket. Someone aboard has been crying in the washroom, not much, but to a schedule. Someone else has been topping up their coffee from a private supply. All over the ship, people have stopped making eye contact.
reading.line: A sound little ship, unhappy, honest; there is more; I will buy a barrel of this as it stands, or you may buy my silence, or I can simply go on.

ai.aria: Notes of gasket! ARIA has always said this ship has character! Now a licensed professional agrees!
ai.marv: Every statement so far is accurate. MARV has known for months. Nobody asked him, and he observes that the appraiser charges for this.
ai.rex: Operational security has been compromised by a beverage. The washroom schedule is now public. REX wants the source of that coffee.
ai.chip: A negative review! Reputation Rinse™ removes gaskets from your public profile! Silence sold separately!
ai.ajoy: A paid-for silence is the only version where nobody keeps a copy. A real cook could contest the reading, if we've got one. The barrel pays best and is the crew's secrets sold by volume. But you do like gold.

choices.text: Sell them a barrel of it
choices.sub: Gold for water, and the gossip
Let the crew hear the rest

gasket_letter.title: BY INTRODUCTION
gasket_letter.body: You hold the vial up to the camera. The trader stops swirling. They know the hand, or the family of the hand, and for the first time they sound like someone talking and not someone selling. There will be no reading. They send across a cask of the house reserve, meltwater that has never met anyone, and pay over the odds for a sealed barrel of yours, to be opened by nobody.
gasket_letter.line: Forgive the patter, I did not know you were known; this is what I drink myself, it has no opinions.
gasket_letter.narrative: Showed an appraiser our Salt Letter. No reading, a cask of their reserve, and a sealed barrel sold at a price that had manners in it.

gasket_sold.title: BOTTLED AND LABELED
gasket_sold.body: You pump a barrel across, {cost.water} points of water and everything in it. The appraiser pays promptly, corks it, and labels it on the spot with your ship's name and the year. Somewhere a connoisseur is going to know about the washroom. The crew takes the gold well and the reason for it less well.
gasket_sold.narrative: Sold a barrel of ship water to an appraiser. Good price. The washroom schedule is now in a private cellar.

gasket_silence.title: A MEASURED GLASS
gasket_silence.body: The trader names their fee, then takes a measured glass of distilled water in full view of the camera, the way you would take a bad medicine. Their color thins. The reading goes out of them. They regard your ship with faint professional interest. Aboard, slowly, people begin looking at one another again.
gasket_silence.line: Good day, I buy and sell ship water, is this a convenient time.
gasket_silence.narrative: Paid an appraiser to drink distilled water until they forgot us.

gasket_rest.title: THE FULL READING
gasket_rest.body: It takes two days, because there is a great deal of it. The washroom and the private coffee turn out to be the same person. The water also holds who has been sliding part of their ration to the person beside them, and who lies awake on the bad nights, which turns out to be everyone. By the end one silence aboard has ended and another has begun. The appraiser calls it a rare finish and draws off a jar for the cellar.
gasket_rest.narrative: Let an appraiser read the whole tank aloud. Two days. The crew knows everything now, and on balance seems to prefer it.

gasket_chef.title: SECOND OPINION
gasket_chef.body: {crew.chef} takes the channel and sends a spoon of yesterday's stock down the line with a single question: what's in it. There is a long silence. The appraiser names nine ingredients, misses the tenth and goes a delicate gray. Professional honor requires them to retract the reading and settle the difference in kind, and they ask, stiffly, for the recipe.
gasket_chef.line: Nine, I had nine, there is no tenth, what did you do, please, I must know what you did.
gasket_chef.narrative: {crew.chef} out-tasted a licensed appraiser with a spoon of soup. They retracted the reading, paid the difference and asked for the recipe.

gasket_cut.title: LINE CUT
gasket_cut.body: You cut the line and close the channel. The tanker stays alongside for a while in case you change your mind, then moves off with your thimble. Nobody aboard brings any of it up. Nobody brings anything up.
gasket_cut.narrative: Cut an appraiser off in the middle of reading our water aloud. They kept the sample. The crew kept quiet.

science_link.text: The ISS recycles its water. Moisture from the air and even urine are reclaimed and drunk again.
science_link.label: ISS life support: where the water goes

intro.title: ONE OF MIND
intro.body: The harbor office on the water quarter's dock has one desk and one tank, and the tank was plainly built for someone smaller. Your berth paperwork lies on the desk, damp. There has been, you gather, a dispute between the harbor clerk and the fee assessor over your ship. Water people settle these by merging, and these two have. The result holds both grudges and a new one, and it is looking at you. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We have reached agreement, I have, the clerk in me says your berth was booked wrong and the assessor in me says you were warned, neither of us will ever forgive the other, but we are of one mind that this is your fault, and that is a fine.
