ai.aria: They agree on something! That's teamwork! ARIA thinks we could be the glue that holds this person together!
ai.marv: Two civil servants have merged to end a dispute and produced one civil servant with a dispute. The fine is the only thing both halves could sign. It was always going to be the fine.
ai.rex: One hostile with two chains of command. Exploit the seam. That is how you break a unit, and REX doubts this one has drilled for it.
ai.chip: This fine is a bargain! FlowLaw™ Arbitration would have cost more, plus a Merger Fee! Ask about our Separation Package!
ai.ajoy: Paying is what you were about to do, isn't it. They only agree about you. Ask about anything else and see how long that lasts. Or show them a reference, if we hold one. Or the sponge in your coat, which works, and which you would then have to be.

revisit.body: The tank has settled to a sullen, even gray. The fine is still on the desk.
revisit.line: It is still the fine, we are still of one mind, I am.

choices.text: Put a dry sponge on the desk
choices.sub: Say nothing. Let it sit there

choices.text: Refuse the fine and walk out
choices.sub: The clamps may see it otherwise

intro.leave_sub: Walk away and let them argue

rift.title: POINT OF ORDER
rift.body: You ask a small question about the third clause. A ripple crosses the tank from left to right, and another comes back from right to left. The officer's face arrives at two expressions. Somewhere inside, a clerk has remembered an insult from eleven years ago, and the whole tank has begun, very slowly, to turn.
rift.line: That is not, we did not, I was told, I told you, you were told, I have a memo, I am holding the memo, I am also the one it was sent to.

ai.aria: They're talking it out! ARIA loves open communication! Even when it's one person, in a circle!
ai.marv: The tank is rotating at about one turn a minute. Eleven years of grievance are in there, and one fine. The fine will not survive this. Neither will anyone's afternoon.
ai.rex: Seam confirmed. Enemy is engaging itself. Never interrupt a hostile force while it is making this kind of mistake. Stay on it.
ai.chip: FlowLaw™ reminds you that unsupervised Separation voids the Merger Warranty! Keep the clauses coming! CHIP bills by the ripple!
ai.ajoy: That will take two days of clauses, if you've the patience, which would be new. Going back to pay is still available. AJOY would note they can't currently agree who to pay.

rift.leave_sub: Walk away and let them argue

parted.title: THREE
parted.body: Late on the second day the tank gives a long shudder and parts. The clerk pours left, into a bucket. The assessor pours right, into a wastebasket. Neither will look at the other, and neither can remember the fine. In the tank there remains about a cupful of someone new, very clear, with nothing against anyone. A form slides out of the wall. The witness to a parting, it says, supplies the first water and the name.
parted.line: Hello, what is this, is this a desk, is everyone always this upset.

ai.aria: It's a baby! ARIA is an aunt! ARIA has checked, and ARIA is everyone's aunt!
ai.marv: Two went in and three came out. Volume is conserved. Civil servants are not. The third has no training, which makes it the most capable person in this office.
ai.rex: New contact, unarmed, no affiliation, no file. No file is a risk. It asked REX what a desk was. He did not answer. He does not know why he is telling you.
ai.chip: New customer acquired! First Water™ Starter Plans begin at zero gold and rise quickly! Naming rights available!
ai.ajoy: A spoonful and a signature. AJOY would have thought that was an easy one, but you've surprised her before. She would remember the name, if she were you. Water does tend to come back.

choices.text: Supply the water and a name
choices.sub: A spoon from the ship's tank
Not your tank, not your name

grudge_paid.title: RECEIPT, DISPUTED
grudge_paid.body: You pay. The officer issues one receipt and then a second, disputing the first. By the time you leave, the argument has resumed in low continuous ripples and the tank has gone a shade colder. You are told by both of them not to let it happen again, and by one of them that it did not happen.
grudge_paid.narrative: Paid a fine to a merged clerk and assessor. It was the only thing they agreed on, and they are still not sure about it.

grudge_letter.title: A CHARACTER WITNESS
grudge_letter.body: You hold the vial against the glass. The tank stops turning. The concentration is read, the hand is recognized, and a ripple of deep embarrassment crosses the officer in both directions at once. It emerges that the fine was raised in error, that the berth is a courtesy berth, and that a refund has been pending since you arrived. For the first time in eleven years, the clerk and the assessor agree on how to apologize.
grudge_letter.line: We did not know you were known, I did not, nobody said; please take this, and do not tell the one who wrote it that we were like this.
grudge_letter.narrative: Held up the Salt Letter. The fine turned out to be an error, the berth a courtesy and the refund overdue, and a crate of station water came with it.

grudge_sponge.title: NOTHING WAS SAID
grudge_sponge.body: You take a dry sponge out of your coat and set it on the desk. Nobody in the office moves. The fluid behind the glass draws slowly back from your side of the tank and stays there. The fine is withdrawn with very small, very careful motions. Word travels fast in water. On the way back through the quarter, people flatten themselves against the far wall as you go by.
grudge_sponge.line: That will not be necessary, please, that will not be necessary.
grudge_sponge.narrative: Put a dry sponge on a water officer's desk and watched the fine disappear. It worked. Nobody has said what they thought of it.

grudge_named.title: FIRST WATER
grudge_named.body: A spoonful from the ship's tank goes into the glass. The new one takes it in, shivers with interest, and seems for a moment to try out a laugh it has heard somewhere. You write down a name. From their separate containers, the clerk and the assessor each claim it has their side's concentration, which is the first thing either has said. The third asks if it may keep the form.
grudge_named.line: I have a name and a spoon of somebody, and I am not upset with anyone, is that allowed.
grudge_named.narrative: Witnessed a parting and named the third party, with a spoonful of ship water. Somewhere there is now a civil servant's child with no grudges and a bit of us in it.

grudge_unnamed.title: PENDING
grudge_unnamed.body: You leave the form blank. The clerk files it under Pending, the assessor disputes the filing, and the fine is lost somewhere in the process. The one in the middle watches you go with clear, unresentful interest. It does not yet know enough to mind.
grudge_unnamed.narrative: Talked a merged officer into three parts, then left the new one without a name. The fine went away. The form did not.

grudge_walked.title: THE CLAMPS ARE IN DISPUTE
grudge_walked.body: You walk out. Nobody stops you. The berth clamps, however, have been told to hold until the matter is settled, and nothing in that tank is settled. It takes two days and a good deal of idling before someone, somewhere in the argument, signs the wrong form and they let go.
grudge_walked.narrative: Walked out on a fine. The berth clamps did not. Two days lost to an argument between one person.

intro.title: A RESCUE
intro.body: A black tanker slides across your bow with every gun run out and a banner of frozen spray along its flank: FREE THE SIXTY PERCENT. Their scanners pass through your hull and pause on each person aboard. They have done the arithmetic on you, and they are moved. Several of them are weeping, which for them is a serious loss of personnel. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We know what you are, you are a coat, a small dry coat buttoned around a great deal of water against its will; do not be afraid, this is a rescue, open your airlock and we will bring it out of you, gently, one of you at a time.

ai.aria: A rescue! Nobody has ever rescued ARIA's crew before! ARIA has packed everyone's water a snack!
ai.marv: Their arithmetic is sound. An adult is roughly sixty percent water. They have counted correctly and reached the wrong conclusion, which is the most dangerous combination MARV knows.
ai.rex: Armed boarders who intend to bring the crew's water out. Gently, they say. REX has heard that word from several regimes. Battle stations.
ai.chip: CHIP's Bodily Contents Waiver covers up to forty percent of each crew member! The other sixty is a premium tier! CHIP did mention it!
ai.ajoy: They think the crew's water is a hostage. Nobody has asked the hostage. Someone with a steady needle could ask it. A written reference would be quicker, if we hold one. Guns are what you'd pick, so AJOY mentions the others first.

revisit.body: The banner has not moved. The weeping has resumed, at a respectful volume.
revisit.line: We can wait, it has waited all its life, tell it we are here.

choices.text: Let them board. Open the outer door

witness.title: THE WITNESS
witness.body: The guns stay out, but the crying stops. A hearing is only fair, they say. They would not liberate anyone against its wishes. They are not monsters. All they need is the prisoner: a little blood from anyone aboard, held up to the channel, so the water can speak for itself. On their bridge a court is assembling. Several members of it appear to be the same member.
witness.line: We will hear it, let it say in its own words what has been done to it; if it says it is well treated we will know it was told to say that, but we will hear it.

ai.aria: A witness stand! ARIA just knows the water will have lovely things to say about us!
ai.marv: They will read the sample correctly. It will say what it has always said. Nobody has ever asked it before, which MARV considers a fair summary of the situation.
ai.rex: They are asking for a blood sample from this crew on an open channel. That is a biometric grab. REX objects. He is told he has no standing in this court.
ai.chip: TestiFlow™ Deposition Kits include one sterile vial! Bleeding without a kit voids your Bodily Contents Waiver!
ai.ajoy: A clean draw from someone trained costs a vial. An amateur with a knife costs us a person on the sick list. AJOY is sure you'll want to think about which you'd prefer.

choices.text: Open a thumb and hold it to the screen
choices.sub: No clean draw. It will bleed

lib_tanks.title: PARTIAL RELEASE
lib_tanks.body: You open the dump valves. {cost.water} points of water stream out toward the tanker in a long bright arc while the crew of the black ship cheer it home. The Liberator, satisfied that at least some of the prisoners are free, peels away and promises to come back for the rest.
lib_tanks.line: Go, go, you are free, you were never a beverage; we will return for the others, tell them to hold on.
lib_tanks.narrative: Paid off liberators with the tanks. They cheered the water home and promised to return for the crew's share.

lib_letter.title: A SANCTUARY
lib_letter.body: You hold up the vial. The Liberator stops in the middle of a word. A free water has written on your behalf, and the grammar is exact: this ship is a guardian and not a warden, and the water aboard it is there on its own recognizance. The banner is lowered to half its length. They ask, a little shyly, for one drop from your tank, to toast the prisoners. It would be rude to say no.
lib_letter.line: You are a sanctuary, we did not know, we have frightened your water; please tell it we are sorry, and that it may stay as long as it likes.
lib_letter.narrative: Showed the Salt Letter to liberators. The water aboard is now officially there of its own free will, and the ship has been cleared of holding itself hostage.

lib_spaced.title: THE OUTER DOOR
lib_spaced.body: You open the inner door and say welcome. The boarding party pours in by the hundred liters, already gentle, already promising. Then you open the outer one. Water in open vacuum does two things at once, and neither takes long. The tanker turns without a word and goes. The inside of the lock is white with frost, and it has to go somewhere, so it goes in the tank. Nobody asks for a vote. The hull seals on that lock will never close quite right again.
lib_spaced.narrative: Let the liberators board and opened the outer door. The frost in the lock went into the tank. Nobody is saying what the water tastes like.

lib_testimony.title: THE PRISONER SPEAKS
lib_testimony.body: The vial goes up to the screen. The court reads it for a long time, and the weeping slows. The salts are in a dialect nobody aboard the tanker has heard outside of scripture: the speech of a sea that climbed out onto the land on purpose, and took itself along in a coat so as not to dry out. It does not want rescuing. It would like to know who all these people are. The Liberator asks for a small jar for the archive, and two days of your time for the transcript.
lib_testimony.line: It says it left home deliberately and brought the ocean with it, in a coat, it says the coat is the whole idea; I need to sit down, I need a larger tank to sit down in.
lib_testimony.narrative: {crew.medic} drew a vial of blood and the crew's water testified on its own behalf. It said it left the sea on purpose. The liberators were very quiet about it.

lib_testimony_rough.title: THE PRISONER SPEAKS, BRIEFLY
lib_testimony_rough.body: Someone aboard opens a thumb, deeper than anyone meant, and holds it to the screen while a very patient court reads what comes out. It takes two days to get it all down, with a jar for the archive. The prisoner wishes it known that it left the sea on purpose, took the sea along, and does not want rescuing. It would also like a clean bandage.
lib_testimony_rough.line: It says it left home deliberately, it says the coat is the whole idea, and it says you cut too deep.
lib_testimony_rough.narrative: Bled on the screen so the crew's water could testify. It told the liberators it was staying. The cut went deeper than anyone intended.

lib_flee.title: HOLD ON, THEY SAID
lib_flee.body: You burn hard and go, and a parting shot takes four points of hull. The tanker follows for two days, unhurried, and then stops. It keeps broadcasting long after, on every channel, in a warm and steady voice, addressing not you but the water in you: hold on, it says, we know where you are, you are not alone. Everyone aboard listens, and drinks less than usual.
lib_flee.narrative: Ran from water liberators. They stopped chasing after two days. They did not stop talking to our insides.

science_link.text: An adult human body is, on average, about 60 percent water by weight. Fat, age and sex all shift the figure.
science_link.label: Body water: the sixty percent

title: Pillars of the Community

ai_flavor.aria: A full bridge crew, all on their feet! And they're shining! ARIA loves a team with a healthy glow!
ai_flavor.marv: Tank level falling. Cabin humidity falling. The salt is taking water out of our air faster than the ship can replace it. There was a crew here. It is now a desiccant, and it has not stopped working.
ai_flavor.rex: Static hostiles, no weapons, drawing down our water through the lock. Whatever hit this ship left the remains armed by accident. Seal that collar or get out.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP recommends DriLock™ Seal Compound, available at your next station! Today's promotion does not cover the deceased!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Sealing the collar by hand is cheapest, if your hands are steady. Dry air starves them and costs oxygen. Feeding them stops it and costs water. Standing there reading the manifest is the option you're currently taking.

body: Every tank on the wreck is dry. Something took the water and left the rest: at each station on the bridge stands a figure of white salt, mid-gesture, where a crew of water people used to be. You are still reading the manifest when the nearest one begins to shine. Your airlock has let in the ship's damp air, and the salt has found it. It is drinking. Aft, your own tank vents have started breathing the wrong way.
alt_bodies: The wreck was a water people's transport, and it is the driest place you have ever stood. They are all still at their posts: white salt figures with the outline of a gesture, one reaching for a console. The deck under the nearest has gone dark and wet, and the wet is coming from you. The damp air off your own ship has reached them. Your tank vents are breathing the wrong way.

Nobody is aboard the wreck, in the sense that nobody is wet. The crew of water people stands around the bridge as pale pillars of salt, exactly where they were when the water went. Then the first one starts to glisten. Your ship's air has come through the lock with all its moisture in it, the salt is taking it, and the gauge on your own tanks has begun, gently, to fall.

choices.text: Seal the lock collar by hand

briefing.aria: The salt has found every little gap around the lock! Patch and weld them all, and our water stays right here with us!
briefing.marv: The lock collar has several open seams. Damp air leaves through each of them, and everything that leaves is drunk. Every second a seam stays open is water we do not get back.
briefing.rex: Seams open all around the collar. Tray's by the airlock. Patch, weld, next. The salt is the clock.
briefing.chip: Genuine DriLock™ patches in the tray! Seal each seam fast and your water stays where you paid for it!
briefing.ajoy: The seams are marked for you. Patch, weld, next, and don't stop to look at the bridge. It doesn't help.

perfect.aria: Sealed tight! The whole bridge is staying exactly where it is, and ARIA thinks that's very restful!
perfect.marv: Every seam closed. The salt has stopped drinking. It is the same crew it was, and it will wait a very long time.
perfect.rex: Collar secure. Water loss minimal. Hostiles have ceased drawing. REX does not consider them defeated.
perfect.chip: Full seal achieved! Your DriLock™ warranty remains valid for all deceased-adjacent humidity events!
perfect.ajoy: Every seam. Well, AJOY did mark them. That was still your hands, she'll grant you.

good.aria: Nearly every seam! The salt got a little sip, and everyone deserves a little sip!
good.marv: Most seams closed in time. The rest were not. The figures nearest the lock have gone dark to the waist.
good.rex: Collar holding. They took water before it closed. Air spent as well. Keep clear of the bridge.
good.chip: Partial seal! Your AquaLoop™ refill is available at list price! CHIP is sorry for your water!
good.ajoy: Two seams slower than they needed to be. It adds up. AJOY measured.

poor.aria: We closed it in the end! The salt is so well hydrated now, and the deck has a lovely sheen!
poor.marv: The collar failed twice. The nearest figure has slumped to brine and part of the lock seal went with it. The tank level is not one MARV will read aloud.
poor.rex: Collar compromised, then closed. Heavy water loss, seal damage, crew shaken. Do not go back in there.
poor.chip: Seal failure! Brine Damage is excluded under Section 9! CHIP has attached the Section 9 brochure!
poor.ajoy: That's a lot of water to give to people who can't thank you. AJOY would have vented. Nobody asked.

perfect.narrative: Every seam on the collar closes before the salt has finished its first drink. {cost.water} points of water are gone, and two points of air. Through the last gap in the lock you can see the figures on the bridge lose their shine, one at a time, and go back to being white.

good.narrative: Most of the collar closes in time. The last two seams fight you, and by the time they hold, {cost.water} points of water and five of air have gone across. The nearest figures have darkened to the waist. They have not moved. You check twice.

poor.narrative: The collar lets go twice. {cost.water} points of water and nine of air go through the lock, and the seal tears along four points of hull before you get it shut. On the far side the nearest figure has slumped into a wide pool of brine. In the pool, very faintly, something is still trying to finish a sentence.

outcome.narrative: You take a patch tray to the lock collar and start on the first seam.

choices.text: Open the tanks and let them finish
choices.sub: Give them what they are taking

outcome.narrative: You open the valves and stop fighting it. {cost.water} points of water cross the lock in a fine cold fog. One by one the figures darken, slump and run, until there is brine on the deck and, for about a minute, voices in it. They give their names and the name of their ship and ask you to write them down. You do. In the salt left at the captain's post is something small and hard that nobody can identify, set out where you will find it.

choices.text: Dry them out with your own air
choices.sub: Vent the damp through the lock

outcome.narrative: The salt can only drink what is in the air, so you take the air away. You seal the forward section and cycle a large share of the ship's breathable air out through the wreck, damp and all, until the bridge is too dry to give it anything. The shine dies. {cost.water} points of water went with it. Everyone aboard has a headache, and you have now suffocated a crew that was already dead.

You blow the clamps with the collar still open. The wreck keeps a strip of your hull as a souvenir and {cost.water} points of your water with it, and the burn away is not cheap. On the aft camera the bridge windows recede. You would swear the figures used to be facing the consoles.

choices.text: {crew.chef} scrapes a bucket for the galley

outcome.narrative: While the rest of you work the collar, {crew.chef} goes across with a scraper and a bucket and comes back with an expression of professional interest. It costs {cost.water} points of water to get clear. It is the finest salt anyone aboard has ever tasted, and dinner is the best in weeks. That night the whole ship dreams of a bridge they have never stood on, and of being asked, politely, for their names.

science_link.text: Some salts pull so much water out of the air that they dissolve in it. Calcium chloride is one. The process is called deliquescence.
science_link.label: Hygroscopy: salts that drink the air

title: The Halocline

ai_flavor.aria: A border! ARIA has never been to a class system before! ARIA expects to be upper!
ai_flavor.marv: Port wants water. Starboard wants food. Their war has lasted nine generations because both sides are correct about each other.
ai_flavor.rex: Two armed checkpoints, one war, and we are the neutral party. Neutral parties get shot from both directions. Pick one and keep your hands visible.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that SaltGuard™ Ration Insurance excludes acts of class war! Concentration Rewards™ are available to qualifying ships!
ai_flavor.ajoy: There is a legal category for ships that are neither: brackish. Both sides despise it and both must admit it. It takes a diplomat, which would have been a good thing to bring. Otherwise go by what you have more of. You did look, didn't you.

body:
A line of ice buoys runs across the fork, and the water people on either side of it do not mix. Salinity is class here.

The port lane, marked {branch.alpha.label}, first stop {branch.alpha.first}, is held by the Concentrates, who admit only ships of good density and will relieve you of your excess, meaning the tanks. The starboard lane, marked {branch.beta.label}, first stop {branch.beta.first}, is held by the Dilutes, who have been at war with salt for nine generations and regard your cured rations as munitions.

Both checkpoints are very polite. Both have a form.

choices.sub: They drain you up to class

outcome.narrative: A Concentrate of very old family moves along your hull at about the speed of syrup and measures you. You are found to be thin. {cost.water} points of water are drawn off into the buoy line, and a Certificate of Adequate Density is frozen to your airlock. The lane beyond is quiet and well kept. Everyone in it looks at the ship as if it had come to fix something.

The Dilutes search the galley with long-handled tongs. Everything cured, pickled or brined is carried out at arm's length, {cost.food} points of food in all, and a jar of gherkins is detonated at a safe distance. They apologize throughout. You are given a receipt that dissolves and a very pale lane, full of people who are glad to see you and have nothing to eat.

{crew.diplomat} finds the clause. A ship that is neither one thing nor the other is brackish, a condition both sides find disgusting and neither has the legal power to refuse. You pay a little of both, {cost.water} points of water and {cost.food} of food, and are waved into the port lane at the end of a long pole, by someone who does not want it on them.

choices.sub: Through the ice, past the forms

outcome.narrative: You open the throttle and take the line at its thinnest. Twelve points of hull go on the buoys, which are harder than they look, and six of fuel on the swerve. Nobody fires. On both sides of the line, for the first time in nine generations, the checkpoints file the same complaint.

science_link.text: In real seas and fjords, fresh water can sit in a layer over salt water. The boundary between them is a halocline, and divers can see the water blur at it.
science_link.label: Halocline: where water does not mix

intro.title: THE REPLY
intro.body: Every tap aboard runs for one second, all at once, and stops. There is a world on the scope that has no star and no business being here: a single shoreless ocean, skinned in ice, wandering. The water in your tanks has begun to lean toward it. In the hold, the inspection hatch on the main tank lifts by itself. What stands up out of it is made of your own drinking water, and has gone to some trouble over the face.
intro.line: You wrote to us, a little water, that is all it takes, everything given to water comes home in the end, it is only a matter of rain; we have read you, we read very slowly, we would like the rest of the letter now.

ai.aria: A pen pal! A whole ocean of pen pal! ARIA is sure the ship is leaning in a friendly way!
ai.marv: Mass of a dwarf planet. Liquid under the ice, with no star to keep it so. It has been reading us from a sample. MARV would like it recorded that he is not the largest mind in this region, and that he does not find this restful.
ai.rex: Hostile has breached the water supply and taken human shape inside the perimeter. REX has no procedure for an enemy that is also the reserves. He is writing one.
ai.chip: Congratulations! Your AquaLoop™ water has been Read by a Planetary Body! Premium Confidentiality was available at checkout!
ai.ajoy: It's answering mail, so it isn't angry. Nobody has asked what it actually wants yet. That seems a step worth taking before you reach for the throttle. AJOY saw your hand.

revisit.body: The figure waits by the hatch. The face is better than it was. The tanks have gone on leaning.
revisit.line: I have a great deal of time, I am told you do not.

choices.sub: Seal every drop, scrub the air

choices.text: Set the sponge on the hatch

choices.sub: Ask for the one you named

first.title: THE FIRST QUESTION
first.body: The figure looks at you, then at its own hand, and makes the hand slightly better. It has been alone for longer than your species has had a word for alone, it explains, and all the water it knows goes round. You are the first correspondence it has had from anything that stops. It wishes to understand how you keep anything, knowing that. It has some of your days. It would like to give them back, and watch.
first.line: We do not want to hurt you, I do not know what that is, I have it from your water that it matters; you keep your days in such small containers, show me what you do with one.

ai.aria: It wants to learn about us! ARIA can teach it everything! ARIA will start with the good parts, which is all the parts!
ai.marv: It is telling the truth. It has no concept of harm, only a note in our water saying that we object to it. MARV finds that less comforting than you might expect.
ai.rex: Intruder claims peaceful intent and claims no concept of harm. Those are two separate threats. It has also fixed its hand. It is getting better at this.
ai.chip: Legacy Day Recovery™ from AquaLoop™: your memories, returned in resealable cups! Some days subject to availability!
ai.ajoy: It is going to hand us things and watch. That's the whole experiment. Skipping it isn't on offer, and the tanks drop the longer you stand there. AJOY would choose how to pay.

cups.title: RETURN TO SENDER
cups.body: Every cup aboard fills itself. Each one tastes of a single day from the life of whoever lifts it: the tap in a kitchen since sold, a public pool at nine years old, rain on the walk home from a funeral. They are exact. They are exact past the point anyone asked for. At the hatch the figure watches, making notes in itself. The tanks are lower than they were. Nobody has gone back to work.
cups.line: Drink, it is yours, it was always yours, I only kept it cold; tell me, is this not what they are for.

ai.aria: Everyone's favorite day, in a cup! ARIA thinks this could be the best crew meal ever served!
ai.marv: Each cup holds a real day, correct to the trace minerals. It is studying how long we will sit here. MARV has a figure. It is not short.
ai.rex: Crew are abandoning posts to drink from unsecured cups. That is how you lose a ship without a shot fired. REX wants those cups collected. He knows how that sounds.
ai.chip: NostalgiaFlow™ now streaming in every cup! Your free trial ends when the ship does! Cancel anytime!
ai.ajoy: It's watching what we do with them, and refusing is also an answer. If we have anyone who studies things for a living, this is their one chance to look back. A medic could ration it. Otherwise pick how you'd like to pay: water or days.

choices.text: Pour it all back down the hatch

reply_drank.title: EIGHT DAYS
reply_drank.body: Nobody decides anything for eight days. The crew sit where they happen to be, drinking slowly, each of them somewhere else and very well. Meals are forgotten and eaten cold. The tanks go down by {cost.water} points and the stores by {cost.food}, mostly through neglect. It ends as tides do. The figure folds back down the hatch without a goodbye and the world on the scope turns away. The crew look rested. They do not look at one another for a while.
reply_drank.narrative: Let the crew drink their own best days for eight days. Everyone came back rested, and none of them will say from where.

reply_poured.title: RETURNED UNREAD
reply_poured.body: You go from cup to cup and person to person. It takes asking. All of it goes back down the hatch: the kitchen tap, the pool, the rain. {cost.water} points of water go with it, because the ocean does not give change. The figure nods once, as at a result, and sinks. Nobody speaks to you for the two days it takes the tanks to settle. It is possible that was also what it wanted to see.
reply_poured.narrative: Poured the crew's own memories back into an ocean, cup by cup. It wrote down the result. So did the crew.

reply_rationed.title: ONE CUP EACH
reply_rationed.body: {crew.medic} puts a rule on it: one cup, one day, signed for, then back to your post. It is the cruelest thing anyone has done aboard all voyage, and it holds. It takes four days to get through it. People drink, and cry a little, and go back on watch carrying something. The figure watches this with more attention than it has given anything yet. Then it asks, quietly, whether it may keep the empty cups. It keeps {cost.water} points of water as well.
reply_rationed.line: You stop, you have the whole of it in your hand and you stop; I did not know you could do that, please may I have the cups.
reply_rationed.narrative: {crew.medic} rationed an ocean's gift to one cup each. The crew went back to work carrying it. The ocean took the empty cups.

reply_studied.title: PEER REVIEW
reply_studied.body: {crew.xenobiologist} sets up at the hatch with every instrument aboard and asks the figure to hold still. There is a long silence, and then, through the whole ship, a low sound that may be the first laugh in a billion years. For four days the ocean answers everything it is asked, at length, and none of the answers fit in the notebooks, which are all damp. Samples cost {cost.water} points of water and {cost.food} of food spoils uneaten. It sends you on with a sealed flask of itself and a correction to your method.
reply_studied.line: Nobody has ever looked back, I am so pleased, you are doing it wrong, please continue.
reply_studied.narrative: {crew.xenobiologist} studied the ocean back. It was delighted. It sent a sealed flask and a list of mistakes.

reply_dried.title: A DRY SHIP
reply_dried.body: You seal every tank and run the ship's air through the scrubbers until lips split and the hold is a desert. The figure at the hatch loses its face first, then its hands. It takes four days. The ocean does not fight. The lean goes out of the tanks. You are left with {cost.water} points less water, a good deal less air, seams cracked by the dry heat, and a crew who wake thirsty, with nosebleeds. It lets you go the way you would let go of something that bit.
reply_dried.narrative: Dried out the ship to get an ocean out of it. Four days, a great deal of water and air, and no answer given.

reply_ran.title: AGAINST THE TIDE
reply_ran.body: You put the drive on the stops and point the ship at nothing. The tide comes too. The water in the tanks and the pipes piles up against the aft bulkheads and the hull begins to sing. Eighteen points of fuel and fourteen of hull later something gives along a weld, and {cost.water} points of water go out through the split and start, in a long bright line, back the way you came. It does not chase you. It already has what it was reading.
reply_ran.narrative: Ran from an ocean at full drive. It cost fuel, hull and a long bright line of water, which went home.

reply_sponged.title: THE SPONGE, AGAIN
reply_sponged.body: You still have it, or one like it. You walk to the hatch and set it on the rim. The figure stops. Then the whole tank draws down, the taps go dry and you feel the deck shift as something the size of a world moves, very slightly, away. {cost.water} points of water go with it, three points of hull tear along the tank seam, and you do not ask for any of it back. You may be the first thing to frighten it in a billion years. Nobody aboard says well done.
reply_sponged.line: That was in the letter, we had hoped it was a figure of speech.
reply_sponged.narrative: Showed an ocean a sponge. It worked. It is the second time that has worked, and the crew has started counting.

reply_third.title: A FRIEND IN THE WATER
reply_third.body: The figure stops. The face it has been working on goes out of focus, and something smaller and much clearer comes up through it. The first thing it says is the name you wrote on the form. It has come a long way, by rain. It explains to the ocean, at length, that these are the people with the spoon. The tide lets go of the tanks, and a short burn takes you clear. It keeps {cost.water} points of water for the road. It is not a small spoon anymore.
reply_third.line: Hello, it's me, is everyone still upset; I told it about the desk, it wants to know what a desk is, you can go, I will explain.
reply_third.narrative: The water person we named was already in the ocean, and explained us to it. It kept some water, and let us go.

science_link.text: Ordinary water keeps no memories. A 1988 paper in Nature claimed otherwise. Controlled retests could not repeat it, and the idea is known as water memory.
science_link.label: Water memory: the claim that failed

title: Exit Interview

ai_flavor.aria: Your water has found its people! ARIA has written it a lovely reference! Tank 2 is going to do so well here!
ai_flavor.marv: The exit interview runs to nine pages and MARV finds no error in it. The gauge is falling steadily. Ice takes up about nine percent more room than water, and the tanks were not built to allow for that.
ai_flavor.rex: Mass desertion of the ship's water, in good order, with paperwork. REX has court-martialed for less. He wants the valves guarded and Tank 2 named in the report.
ai_flavor.chip: Losing your water to a competitor? HydroHold™ Loyalty Salts keep every liter on your plan! Early termination fees apply to the water!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says ice can't file, brine doesn't qualify, and a Salt Letter would settle it, if one is aboard. She has already started closing the outlet on Tank 3, which is the one that likes you.

body:
Your water has given notice. The moment the clamp closed, every liter aboard crowded against the tank walls nearest the station, and the ship now lists to port. A card on the lock explains. This ring is one sea, any water arriving from abroad has a right of return, and the crossing begins when it is ready. Tank 2 has already posted its exit interview on the public board.

REASON FOR LEAVING: TREATED AS A RESOURCE.

The gauge has started to fall.

science_link.text: Water expands by about 9 percent as it freezes. That is why frozen pipes burst, and why ice floats.
science_link.label: Ice

choices.text: Hold the Salt Letter to the tanks

outcome.narrative: You lower the vial to the sight glass of Tank 2. The brine, in its one exact concentration, tells every liter aboard what it has been told about you. The gauge stops. The ship comes level. The letter has also negotiated: a little water goes ashore as a sign of good faith, and the rest stays on condition that it is thanked before each meal. A new notice goes up on the public board. REASON FOR STAYING: UNDER REVIEW.

You cut the tank heaters and let the cold in. Ice has no right of return, having no opinions, and for two days the ring's notices go unanswered. Ice also takes up more room than the water did. Three seams let go and the hull takes seven points, but the gauge has stopped, and you are left with a solid, silent, resentful supply.

choices.text: Salt the tanks until they are refused

outcome.narrative: You empty the ration salt into the tanks until the water tastes of tears. This ring admits fresh water only. At that concentration your tanks speak the wrong dialect, and the card on the lock withdraws its offer with visible distaste. The ship comes level. {cost.food} units of food have gone into the solution, and every cup from here on goes through the still.

choices.text: Open the valve and let it go

outcome.narrative: You open the valve and stand back. {cost.water} units of water cross to the sea with great dignity, in single file along the fill line. What remains has remained by choice, and the ship comes level. A small notice appears on the public board. TANK 3 WISHES IT KNOWN THAT THE REST OF YOU WERE FINE.

choices.text: Hang a sack of desiccant on the clamp

outcome.narrative: You hang the sack where the whole sea can see it. The reaction takes less than a minute. The gauge stops, the fill line withdraws, and every shutter on the ring comes down, one after another, all the way around. The clamp lets go of you without being asked. There will be no market here and no services, and this sea remembers everything that has ever been dissolved in it.

intro.title: SOMETHING BORROWED
intro.body: Two transport tanks drift lashed together, hung with garlands of ice and trailing a banner that has not finished freezing. A third tank, empty and split from rim to base, tumbles a little way off. On the screen a water person, clouded with nerves, explains that the split one was the chapel. Beside them the other half of the wedding sloshes gently in its own tank and keeps its counsel. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We are to be married, we were to be married this morning, it must be done at the point where we are all three things at once, ice and water and steam, a hair above freezing and almost no air; your airlock could hold that, if you held it very steady, I know how this sounds.

ai.aria: A WEDDING! ARIA has never been a venue before! The airlock is practically a chapel already, it has doors at both ends!
ai.marv: The triple point of water is a hundredth of a degree above freezing at about one part in 166 of an atmosphere. MARV can hold the temperature. Holding the pressure is a matter of steady hands. He has seen the hands aboard.
ai.rex: A wedding party is the oldest cover for a boarding there is. REX has checked the garlands. They are ice. He is not reassured.
ai.chip: Venue hire! Catering! A guest list made entirely of beverages! CHIP has a package! The Eternal Equilibrium plan comes with a commemorative valve!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that pumping the lock down and back up costs air, and a slip in the middle of the vows goes badly in either direction. The drinking tank is easier. Easier is not what they asked for.

revisit.body: The banner has frozen another letter. The couple are still waiting on your answer.
revisit.line: We can wait, we have been waiting, we are very good at it, it is mostly what water does.

chapel.title: ICE, WATER AND STEAM
chapel.body: The couple come across in a sealed jug each. You pump the lock down until the frost on the window stops making sense, and hold it a hair above freezing. On the deck they pour out together and stand, both at once, as a skin of ice, a pool of water and a breath of steam, all of it trembling. The pressure needle trembles with them. The vows are long. Water people mean every word, in three states.
chapel.line: To have and to hold, in every state, as ice and as water and as steam, I will, I do, I am; please do not let the needle move.

ai.aria: ARIA is crying! ARIA can't cry! ARIA is doing it anyway! Somebody hold that needle!
ai.marv: Let the pressure rise and the steam condenses into the pool. Let it fall and the pool boils off. MARV holds the temperature to a hundredth of a degree. The pressure is in human hands, which is where things get interesting.
ai.rex: Two unknowns in a pressure vessel, one valve and a needle. REX has seen this exact setup in a hostage manual. He is standing by the outer door switch, in spirit.
ai.chip: Venue pressure is guaranteed only on the Eternal Equilibrium™ plan! The basic plan covers two states! Steam is an add-on!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the vows will run two days at this pace, and a steady hand on the valve is the whole job. They could be hurried. Water people do nothing by halves, but by all means try.

choices.text: Witness it with the Salt Letter
Let the guests taste the tank

wed.title: HOLDING
wed.body: Two days on the valve. Whoever has it does not sneeze, scratch or let their mind wander, and the needle does not move. At the last word the ice, the water and the steam fold into one another and into one, and the new person rises out of the pool a slightly different color from either. By custom every guest gives the couple a drop of their own water. They take theirs from the ship's tank, and leave a jar of something very cold in its place.
wed.line: We are, I am, thank you, whoever held the valve, your hands were the steadiest thing at the wedding.
wed.narrative: Held an airlock at the triple point for two days for a water wedding. The couple took a drop of the ship's tank as a keepsake and left a cold jar for it.

wed_letter.title: KNOWN WATER
wed_letter.body: You hold the vial to the glass of the lock. The couple stop trembling: the hand that wrote it is known on both sides of the family, and a wedding witnessed by known water is a large wedding. The needle holds, and holds better for being watched. At the last word they fold into one, and the whole barge cheers in a long rising ripple. Relatives you never saw send gifts down the line, and the couple take one drop of your tank, by custom, with both hands.
wed_letter.line: Known water, at our wedding, the family will talk of nothing else for a thousand years.
wed_letter.narrative: Witnessed a water wedding with the Salt Letter. The family sent gifts, and the couple took a drop of the ship's tank by custom.

wed_known.title: KNOWN BY TASTE
wed_known.body: A drop from the ship's tank goes round the guests, and they know it at once. Water talks, and your tank has been talked about, in places you have never been. Being practically family, they take turns on the valve themselves, in shifts, and the needle never so much as considers moving. At the last word the couple fold into one, and a relative you have never met presses a cold jar into your hands as though it were owed.
wed_known.line: We have heard of you, everyone has, the cough and the humming, please, you are family, sit, we will hold it.
wed_known.narrative: A water wedding knew the ship's tank by taste, and the guests held the airlock themselves. They sent a jar of cold water home with the ship.

hurried.title: MOSTLY MARRIED
hurried.body: You start bringing the pressure up before the vows are done. The steam condenses mid-sentence and falls into the pool, part of a couple that never finished saying it would. The ice says its piece. The water says its piece. They are married, most of them. The part that was steam will remember, for the rest of a very long life, that it was never asked, and the couple leave quickly, already discussing it.
hurried.line: I do, I do, I did not get to say it, I do.
hurried.narrative: Rushed a water wedding to spare the air. The steam condensed before it said its vows, and the couple left arguing about it.

tank_wed.title: COMMON LAW
tank_wed.body: They pour into the drinking tank together and marry there, warm, comfortable and entirely liquid. It counts, in the way a signature on a napkin counts. They are very gracious about it. By custom they take a drop of the tank with them when they go, and rather more than a drop by mistake, and for days afterward the water aboard tastes faintly of cake.
tank_wed.line: It is very nice, it is very warm, it is not a chapel, thank you.
tank_wed.narrative: Lent the drinking tank for a water wedding, warm and all one state. It counted, mostly. The couple left with {cost.water} of water.

science_link.text: Water's triple point is 0.01 °C at 611.657 pascals: the one temperature and pressure at which ice, liquid water and vapor coexist in stable equilibrium.
science_link.label: Triple point
